Realtime Text to Speech

Build streaming text-to-speech apps with realtime AI models.

Overview

Realtime TTS models convert text into streaming audio. Unlike standard TTS that processes a full prompt and returns an audio file, realtime TTS streams AI-generated speech as a continuous PCM audio stream over a WebSocket connection, in real time. The text prompt is submitted via POST /Run, not over the WebSocket. The WebSocket carries only task events (task_info, task_stream_ready, etc.), binary audio frames, and control messages (task_session_end).

No microphone is required. The flow is one-directional: text goes in, audio comes out.

The flow is:

  1. Run the realtime TTS model via POST /Run with your text prompt in the parameters
  2. Connect to the WebSocket and send task_info with your socketaccesstoken
  3. Wait for task_stream_ready: the model has loaded and is generating audio
  4. Receive AI audio as binary frames and play them
  5. End the session with task_session_end or wait for the stream to finish naturally

How It Differs from Realtime Voice Conversation

Realtime Voice Conversation Realtime Text to Speech
Input Microphone audio (streamed) Text (sent with the run request)
Output AI audio + transcripts AI audio only
Direction Bidirectional (client ↔ server) Server → client only
Microphone Required Not required
Transcripts TRANSCRIPT_USER: / TRANSCRIPT_AI: via task_output None
Use case Interactive voice chat Narration, voiceover, assistants

Run Parameters

Each realtime TTS model has its own set of parameters. Use POST /Tool/Detail to discover the exact parameters for a specific model. See Model Parameters for parameter types.

Browse available realtime TTS models on the models page (filter by Realtime TTS category). Common parameters typically include the input text and an optional reference audio clip for voice cloning. Example run for MOSS-TTS-Realtime:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/Run/openmoss/moss-tts-realtime" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Hello, this is a realtime text-to-speech demo."
  }'

Important: Parameters vary per model. Always check the model's detail page or use /Tool/Detail to get the exact parameter list before integrating. The run response returns a socketaccesstoken used to subscribe to the WebSocket.

Connection & Registration

After running the task, connect to the WebSocket and register with task_info:

var ws = new WebSocket("wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1");

ws.onopen = function() {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({
    type: "task_info",
    tasktoken: "YOUR_SOCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN"
  }));
};

Note: Both standard and realtime models use type: "task_info" with tasktoken to register on the WebSocket. The registration flow is identical to Realtime Voice Conversation.

Realtime Events

During a realtime TTS session, you'll receive these WebSocket events:

Event Description
task_stream_ready Session is ready: the model is generating audio and will begin sending chunks
task_stream_end The model finished generating audio for the current segment
task_cost Cost update: includes turnCost, cumulativeCost, and usage (raw cost breakdown from the model provider)
task_session_stopped The server is ending the session after the turn that reached a spend limit or used up the balance: reason is spend_limit or balance, with code and message. The closing events follow (see Ending a Session)
task_end The model process has exited. Post-processing follows. Wait for task_postprocess_end to close the connection.
task_postprocess_end Post-processing is complete. Safe to close the WebSocket connection.

No task_output events. Unlike voice conversation, TTS sessions do not produce transcript events. The input text is already known (you provided it), and the AI output is audio, not text.

Event Sequence

A typical TTS session produces events in this order:

task_stream_ready     ← model is ready, audio chunks start arriving
[binary frames]       ← PCM audio data (many frames)
task_stream_end       ← audio generation complete for this segment
task_cost             ← cost for this segment
task_end              ← model process exiting
task_postprocess_end  ← safe to close WebSocket

Audio Format

Audio flows in one direction only: server → client. The client does not send any audio.

Property Value
Format PCM (raw, uncompressed)
Bit depth 16-bit signed integer (Int16)
Sample rate 24,000 Hz (24 kHz)
Channels Mono (1 channel)
Byte order Little-endian
Chunk size Variable (typically 200 ms = 4,800 samples = 9,600 bytes)

Binary Frame Format

Every binary WebSocket frame from the server is structured as:

[tasktoken]|[PCM audio data]

The pipe character | (0x7C) separates the token from the raw audio bytes. To extract the audio:

  1. Find the first | byte in the binary frame
  2. Everything after it is raw PCM Int16 audio data
  3. Convert Int16 samples to your playback format (e.g., Float32 for Web Audio API)

Client → server: In TTS mode, you do not send binary audio frames. The only messages you send are task_info (to register) and task_session_end (to end the session).

Receiving AI Audio

AI speech arrives as binary WebSocket frames in PCM Int16 24 kHz format. To play them:

  1. Check if the incoming message is binary (a Blob in JavaScript, bytes in Python) before attempting JSON parse
  2. Find the pipe | separator and extract audio data after it
  3. Convert Int16 → Float32 and create an AudioBuffer
  4. Schedule gapless playback using AudioBufferSourceNode to avoid clicks between chunks

Gapless Playback

Audio arrives in many small chunks. To play them seamlessly:

  • Track a nextPlayTime variable initialized to 0
  • For each chunk, schedule it at max(audioContext.currentTime, nextPlayTime)
  • Advance nextPlayTime by the chunk's duration
  • This ensures chunks play back-to-back with no gaps or overlaps

Ending a Session

To gracefully end a realtime TTS session, send task_session_end:

{
  "type": "task_session_end",
  "tasktoken": "YOUR_SOCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN"
}

After sending this, the server will finish any in-progress generation, send final cost events, and then emit task_postprocess_end. Wait for task_postprocess_end before closing the WebSocket.

For TTS sessions, the stream often ends naturally when the model finishes generating audio for the provided text. In this case, you'll receive task_stream_end followed by task_end without needing to send task_session_end. However, it's good practice to send it explicitly for a clean shutdown, especially if you want to stop playback early.

The server can also end a session on its own, after the turn that uses up your balance or reaches a spend limit. It then sends the same closing events, ending with task_postprocess_end.

When a spend limit or the balance ends the session, the server first sends task_session_stopped, right after that turn's task_cost:

{
  "type": "task_session_stopped",
  "id": "534574",
  "reason": "spend_limit",
  "code": 93,
  "message": "This team's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.00 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC.",
  "result": true,
  "success": null,
  "terminal": false,
  "exitCode": null
}

reason is spend_limit, with code 93, or balance, with code 97. For a spend limit, message is the refusal /Run would give for that limit, which names it and says when it resets. For the balance it is The balance ran out, so the session ended. The event is not a failure: the usual closing events follow, and task_postprocess_end reports success. When it arrives, let the audio you already have finish playing, show message and keep listening until task_postprocess_end. You don't need to send task_session_end. The event can also come after you sent task_session_end, when that last turn uses up the limit or the balance; the session ends either way. No task_session_stopped is sent when a session ends for any other reason.

Safety: If the client disconnects without sending task_session_end, the server automatically terminates the session to prevent the pipeline from running indefinitely (and the provider from continuing to charge). Always send task_session_end explicitly for a clean shutdown.

Insufficient balance: The session is charged turn by turn as it runs. When a charged turn uses up your available balance (the team wallet's balance when you use a team project's API key), the server stops the session right after that turn. That turn is charged in full, and so is any final usage reported while the session closes, so your balance can end slightly below zero. You still receive the final task_cost and task_end events, and task_session_stopped with reason balance and code 97 says why the session ended.

Realtime Speech to Text

Transcribe live microphone audio into text in real time using streaming ASR models.

Overview

Realtime speech-to-text models convert streaming audio into text transcripts as the user speaks. Unlike Realtime Voice Conversation which produces two-way audio, this mode is audio in → text out only. There is no AI audio playback. The server returns transcript strings over the WebSocket.

The flow is:

  1. Run the realtime STT model via POST /Run to get a socketaccesstoken
  2. Connect to the WebSocket and send task_info with your token
  3. Wait for task_stream_ready: the model is ready to receive audio
  4. Stream microphone audio as binary frames (client → server)
  5. Receive transcript text as task_output messages with TRANSCRIPT_USER: prefix
  6. End the session with task_session_end

Key difference from Voice Conversation: No binary audio is sent back from the server. All server → client messages are JSON text events.

How It Differs from Realtime Voice Conversation

Realtime Voice Conversation Realtime Speech to Text
Input Microphone audio (streamed) Microphone audio (streamed)
Output AI audio + transcripts Transcript text only
Direction Bidirectional (client ↔ server) Client → server audio, server → client text
Binary frames from server Yes (AI audio) No (all server messages are JSON)
Transcripts TRANSCRIPT_USER: and TRANSCRIPT_AI: TRANSCRIPT_USER: only
Use case Interactive voice chat Live dictation, captioning, meeting transcription

Run Parameters

Each realtime STT model has its own set of parameters. Use POST /Tool/Detail to discover the exact parameters for a specific model. See Model Parameters for parameter types.

Browse available realtime STT models on the models page (filter by Realtime STT category). Common parameters typically include a transcription delay setting that trades speed for accuracy; some models also take a language. Example run for Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/Run/mistralai/voxtral-mini-4b-realtime-2602" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "transcriptionDelay": "balanced"
  }'

Important: Parameters vary per model. Always check the model's detail page or use /Tool/Detail to get the exact parameter list before integrating. The run response returns a socketaccesstoken used to subscribe to the WebSocket.

Connection & Registration

After running the task, connect to the WebSocket and register with task_info:

var ws = new WebSocket("wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1");

ws.onopen = function() {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({
    type: "task_info",
    tasktoken: "YOUR_SOCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN"
  }));
};

Note: Both standard and realtime models use type: "task_info" with tasktoken to register on the WebSocket.

Realtime Events

During a realtime speech-to-text session, you'll receive these WebSocket events:

Event Direction Description
task_stream_ready server → client Session is ready: start sending microphone audio
task_output server → client Transcript text prefixed with TRANSCRIPT_USER:
task_stream_end server → client Transcription stream has ended: no more transcripts will arrive
task_cost server → client Cost update: includes turnCost, cumulativeCost, and usage breakdown. On models priced by time, each update covers the time since the previous one.
task_session_stopped server → client The server is ending the session after the turn that reached a spend limit or used up the balance: reason is spend_limit or balance, with code and message. The closing events follow (see Ending a Session)
task_end server → client The model process has exited. Post-processing follows. Wait for task_postprocess_end before closing.
task_postprocess_end server → client Post-processing complete: safe to close the WebSocket now.

Unlike voice conversation, there are no binary audio frames from the server. Every server message is a JSON text event.

Audio Format

Audio flows in one direction only: client → server.

Property Value
Format PCM (raw, uncompressed)
Bit depth 16-bit signed integer (Int16)
Sample rate 24,000 Hz (24 kHz)
Channels Mono (1 channel)
Byte order Little-endian
Chunk size Any size. The examples on this page send 4,800 samples (200 ms) = 9,600 bytes.

The server passes each frame to the model as it arrives. Smaller chunks, such as 20 ms (480 samples, 960 bytes), reach the model sooner.

The server internally resamples to the model's native rate (e.g. 16 kHz for Voxtral). Always send at 24 kHz. The server handles conversion.

Binary Frame Format

Every binary WebSocket frame sent from the client is structured as:

[tasktoken]|[PCM audio data]

The pipe character | (0x7C) separates the token from the raw audio bytes. There are no binary frames from the server. All responses are JSON text.

Sending Microphone Audio

Capture microphone audio at 24 kHz using the Web Audio API with an AudioWorklet. Convert Float32 samples to Int16, prepend your task token, and send as a binary frame.

Key steps:

  1. Request microphone with getUserMedia (enable echo cancellation and noise suppression)
  2. Create an AudioContext at 24,000 Hz sample rate
  3. Use an AudioWorklet to buffer and convert samples to Int16
  4. Send each chunk as tasktoken|pcm_data binary frame
  5. Continue sending until you end the session

Tip: You can send audio continuously. The model handles silence detection and only returns transcripts when speech is detected.

Transcripts

Transcripts arrive as task_output messages with the TRANSCRIPT_USER: prefix. Each message carries the next piece of transcribed speech, usually a word or a short phrase:

{
  "type": "task_output",
  "message": "TRANSCRIPT_USER:What's"
}

{
  "type": "task_output",
  "message": "TRANSCRIPT_USER:the"
}

{
  "type": "task_output",
  "message": "TRANSCRIPT_USER:weather"
}

Progressive Results

Transcripts arrive progressively as words and phrases are recognized, not just at segment boundaries. The model streams TRANSCRIPT_USER: messages word-by-word as speech is detected, so the client can display live, incremental results. A message never repeats or corrects earlier text, so add each one to what you have instead of replacing it. To build a full transcript, concatenate all received messages with spaces:

var fullTranscript = [];

// Inside your message handler
if (msg.type === 'task_output' &&
    typeof msg.message === 'string' &&
    msg.message.startsWith('TRANSCRIPT_USER:')) {
  var segment = msg.message.substring(16);
  fullTranscript.push(segment);
  console.log('Segment:', segment);
  console.log('Full:', fullTranscript.join(' '));
}

Note: Unlike voice conversation, there is no TRANSCRIPT_AI: prefix. All transcripts are user speech.

Ending a Session

To gracefully end a realtime session, send task_session_end:

{
  "type": "task_session_end",
  "tasktoken": "YOUR_SOCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN"
}

After sending this, the server processes any remaining buffered audio, sends final transcript and cost events, and then emits task_postprocess_end. Wait for task_postprocess_end before closing the WebSocket.

The server can also end a session on its own: after a period without speech, or after the turn that uses up your balance or reaches a spend limit (see below). It then sends the same closing events, ending with task_postprocess_end. The server never sends task_session_end; that message only goes from the client to the server.

When a spend limit or the balance ends the session, the server first sends task_session_stopped, right after that turn's task_cost:

{
  "type": "task_session_stopped",
  "id": "534574",
  "reason": "spend_limit",
  "code": 93,
  "message": "This team's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.00 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC.",
  "result": true,
  "success": null,
  "terminal": false,
  "exitCode": null
}

reason is spend_limit, with code 93, or balance, with code 97. For a spend limit, message is the refusal /Run would give for that limit, which names it and says when it resets. For the balance it is The balance ran out, so the session ended. The event is not a failure: the usual closing events follow, and task_postprocess_end reports success. When it arrives, stop sending microphone audio, show message and keep listening until task_postprocess_end. You don't need to send task_session_end. The event can also come after you sent task_session_end, when that last turn uses up the limit or the balance; the session ends either way. No task_session_stopped is sent when a session ends for any other reason.

Safety: If the client disconnects without sending task_session_end, the server automatically terminates the session to prevent the pipeline from running indefinitely (and the provider from continuing to charge). Always send task_session_end explicitly for a clean shutdown.

Insufficient balance: The session is charged turn by turn as it runs. When a charged turn uses up your available balance (the team wallet's balance when you use a team project's API key), the server stops the session right after that turn. That turn is charged in full, and so is any final usage reported while the session closes, so your balance can end slightly below zero. You still receive the final task_cost and task_end events, and task_session_stopped with reason balance and code 97 says why the session ended.

Files

Manage folders and upload files for use with AI models.

Overview

The Files API lets you organize and upload data that can be referenced in model runs. Common use cases include:

  • Training data: upload datasets for fine-tuning models
  • File inputs: provide images, audio, or documents as model inputs
  • Batch processing: store files for repeated use across multiple runs

Authentication and Public File URLs

All file-management endpoints, including FolderCreate, Upload, List, Edit, Delete, CheckDisk, and Unzip, require normal Wiro project or Bearer authentication.

  • API Key Only projects: send x-api-key.
  • Signature projects: send x-api-key, x-nonce, and x-signature. See Authentication.
  • Dashboard requests: use the signed-in user's Bearer token.

The returned GET /File/:accessKey/:fileName URL intentionally remains public so browsers, AI model workers, and external clients can display the file without account credentials. Possession of the generated access key grants read access only; it does not grant file-management permission.

Code examples: The examples on this page show API Key Only authentication. Signature-authenticated projects must include the nonce and signature headers, as in this example:

NONCE="$(date +%s)"
SIGNATURE="$(printf '%s' "${YOUR_API_SECRET}${NONCE}" \
  | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "${YOUR_API_KEY}" \
  | awk '{print $NF}')"

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/File/FolderCreate" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: ${YOUR_API_KEY}" \
  -H "x-nonce: ${NONCE}" \
  -H "x-signature: ${SIGNATURE}" \
  -d '{"name":"training-data"}'

POST /File/FolderCreate

Creates a new folder to organize your uploaded files.

Parameter Type Required Description
name string Yes Folder name
parentid string No Parent folder ID for nested structure (omit for root)

Note: Folder names only allow letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores (A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -).

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "list": [{
    "id": "folder-abc123",
    "name": "training-data",
    "parentid": "root-folder-id",
    "size": "0",
    "contenttype": "",
    "addedtime": "1716276543"
  }]
}

POST /File/Upload

Uploads a file using multipart/form-data. You can optionally assign it to a folder.

Parameter Type Required Description
file file Yes The file to upload (multipart form field)
folderid string No Target folder ID (uploads to user's default folder if omitted)

File size limit: 100 MB per file.

Supported file types: Images (jpg, png, gif, jpeg, webp, heic), video (mp4, webm, mov), audio (mp3, wav, m4a), documents (pdf, csv, docx, xlsx, pptx, txt, md, epub), and ZIP archives (automatically extracted).

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "list": [{
    "id": "file-id",
    "name": "dataset.csv",
    "contenttype": "text/csv",
    "size": "1048576",
    "parentid": "folder-id",
    "url": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/...",
    "addedtime": "1716276727",
    "accesskey": "..."
  }]
}

Using Files in Runs

Once uploaded, reference a file by its URL or ID in your model run parameters. For example, an image upscaler model might accept an inputImageUrl parameter. Pass the URL returned from the upload response.

You don't always need to upload files first. Most models take a public URL in place of an upload, and the parameter's type decides where it goes: a combinefileinput takes it in the field itself (for example inputImage on most image models), a fileinput takes it in its {id}Url field (for example inputImageUrl), and a multifileinput takes a list in the field that puts Url before Multiple (for example inputDocumentUrlMultiple). See Model Parameters for each pattern.

{
  "inputImageUrl": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/...",
  "scale": 4
}

Pricing

Understand how billing works for AI model runs on Wiro.

Overview

When you run an AI model through Wiro, you are billed based on the type of work performed. Each model has its own pricing, visible on the model's page in the marketplace and on the pricing page. You pay only for successful runs. Server errors are never billed.

Wiro uses a prepaid credit model. You add credits to your account and they are drawn down as you use models. Credits also determine your concurrency limit.

Billing Methods

Every model on Wiro uses one of the following billing methods. The method is set per model and determines how the cost is calculated.

Fixed-Rate Methods

Billing Method Code How it works
Per Request cpr Fixed cost per run, regardless of output. Most common for image generation, image editing, and simple models.
Per Second cps Cost per second of processing time. When no dynamic pricing is set, this is the default: cost = elapsed seconds × cps rate.
Per Output cpo Cost per output item generated. Multiple files = pay per file. No output = base price charged once.
Per Token cpt Cost per token used. Total tokens (input + output) extracted from model's usage metadata. Used for LLM models.

Usage-Based Methods

Billing Method Code How it works
Per Pixel cp-pixel Cost based on output resolution. Each 1,048,576 pixels (1024×1024) = one tier. Can include per-input-image costs (priceInput).
Per Audio Second cp-audiosecondslength Cost per second of input audio duration.
Per Character cp-promptlength Cost per character in the input prompt. Total = prompt length × price.
Per Video Second cp-outputVideoLength Cost per second of generated output video.

Special Methods

Billing Method Code How it works
Per Realtime Turn cp-realtimeturn For realtime voice models. Billing per conversation turn, deducted in real time during the session.
Model-Reported cp-readoutput The model reports its cost when the run ends.

Dynamic Pricing

Many models have dynamic pricing: the cost varies based on the input parameters you choose. For example, a video generation model might charge different rates depending on the resolution and duration you select.

The pricing is returned in the dynamicprice field of the Tool/List and Tool/Detail API responses as a JSON array:

[
  {
    "inputs": { "resolution": "720p", "duration": "5" },
    "price": 0.13,
    "priceMethod": "cpr"
  },
  {
    "inputs": { "resolution": "1080p", "duration": "5" },
    "price": 0.29,
    "priceMethod": "cpr"
  }
]

How Dynamic Pricing Works

Each entry in the dynamicprice array represents a pricing tier:

Field Type Description
inputs object The input parameter combination this price applies to. Empty {} means the price applies to all configurations.
price number The cost in USD for this configuration.
priceMethod string The billing method code (see tables above).
priceExtra number (optional) Extra cost per additional tier. Used by cp-pixel: each additional 1MP tier costs this amount.
priceInput number (optional) Per-input cost. Used by cp-pixel: each input image incurs this cost per 1MP tier.

When inputs contains specific parameter values (e.g. "resolution": "720p"), that price only applies when you run the model with those exact parameters. When inputs is empty ({}), it's a flat rate that applies regardless of input parameters.

Input matching also supports QUANTITY values (e.g. "QUANTITY:1", "QUANTITY:3") for models where the number of input files affects pricing.

Example: Video Generation Pricing

A video model might have pricing tiers based on resolution and duration:

Resolution Duration Price
480p 5 seconds $0.06
720p 5 seconds $0.13
1080p 5 seconds $0.29
480p 10 seconds $0.12
720p 10 seconds $0.26
1080p 10 seconds $0.58

Example: Simple Flat Pricing

An image generation model with a flat rate:

[{ "inputs": {}, "price": 0.03, "priceMethod": "cpr" }]

This means every run costs $0.03, regardless of parameters.

Fallback Pricing (Per-Second)

When a model does not have dynamicprice set, billing falls back to per-second pricing:

totalcost = elapsed_seconds × cps

Where cps (cost per second) is the model's own rate or Wiro's default per-second rate. The API also returns an approximatelycost field, an estimate based on the model's average run time:

approximatelycost = average_elapsed_seconds × cps

This gives you a rough idea of the expected cost before running the model.

Checking Prices

Via the API

Pricing information is included in both the Tool/List and Tool/Detail responses in the dynamicprice field. Use POST /Tool/Detail with the model's slugowner and slugproject to get full pricing details.

Via MCP

When using the MCP server, both search_models and get_model_schema tools return pricing information in their responses. Your AI assistant can check the cost before running a model.

Pricing Page

Browse and compare model prices interactively on the pricing page. Select a budget to see how many runs each model can perform.

What You Pay For

You are billed for successfully completed model runs. A run is successful when the task reaches task_postprocess_end status with pexit of "0". The actual cost is recorded in the task's totalcost field, which you can retrieve via Task/Detail.

What You Are Not Charged For

  • Server errors: if a run fails due to a server-side error, no charge is incurred.
  • Queue time: time spent waiting in the queue before processing starts is free.
  • Cancelled tasks: tasks cancelled before processing completes are not billed.

Monitoring Your Spending

Via the API

Check the totalcost field in Task/Detail responses to see the cost of individual runs:

{
  "tasklist": [{
    "status": "task_postprocess_end",
    "pexit": "0",
    "totalcost": "0.003510000000",
    "elapsedseconds": "6.0000"
  }]
}

Via MCP

The MCP server provides three ways to check costs:

  • get_task: returns full task details including totalcost
  • get_task_price: dedicated tool that returns just the cost, billing status, and duration. Clearly indicates whether the task was billed or not.
  • get_account: with recent_transactions, lists the wallet's latest transactions, newest first, with what each one was for. Use it to check that a charge landed.

Dashboard

View your overall balance, usage history, and billing details in the Dashboard.

Spend Limits

To cap what you spend, set monthly or daily spend limits under Controls > Spend Limits in the dashboard or with the /SpendLimit endpoints: for the whole wallet, one API key, one team member, one way in such as the API or the LLM gateway, or one agent. Once a limit is reached, new work it covers is refused with error code 93, and an alert email can warn you before that. See Spend Limits.

Concurrency Limits

Understand and manage how many requests you can run simultaneously on Wiro.

Overview

Concurrency limits control how many tasks your account can process at the same time. When you reach your limit, the API returns an error response with code 96. You should wait for a running task to complete before submitting a new one, or add funds to increase your limit.

How It Works

Your concurrency limit is determined by your current account balance:

  • When your balance is $250 or below, your limit is one unfinished task for each full $10 of balance, never less than 1. So $20 allows 2, $55 allows 5 and $250 allows 25.
  • When your balance is above $250, there is no concurrency limit.

The balance is the credit that can pay for the model you run. Coupon credit that only works on other models is left out, so for those runs the limit can be lower than your wallet total would give.

For a team project's API key (or the team workspace in the dashboard), the limit uses the team wallet's balance, and every unfinished team task counts toward it, whichever member started it. Personal tasks count only against your personal balance. See Team Billing & Spending.

Examples

Account Balance Concurrent Task Limit
$10 1 concurrent task (minimum)
$50 5 concurrent tasks
$100 10 concurrent tasks
$150 15 concurrent tasks
$250 25 concurrent tasks
Above $250 Unlimited (no limit applied)

The formula: max(1, floor(balance_usd * 0.10)) while the balance is $250 or less. Above $250 there is no concurrency limit.

What Counts as Active

Every unfinished task counts toward your concurrency limit, from task_queue until it reaches one of these statuses:

  • task_postprocess_end: task completed (success or failure)
  • task_cancel: task was cancelled or killed

Until then the task counts, including while it waits in the queue and while it is in task_error, which does not close a task. Once it reaches either of these statuses, it no longer counts toward your limit.

API Response

When you hit the concurrency limit, the POST /Run endpoint returns an error with code 96:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 96,
      "message": "You have reached your concurrent task limit. With your current balance of $50.00, you can run up to 5 tasks at the same time. Add funds to increase your limit."
    }
  ]
}

The error message includes your current balance and the calculated limit, so you know exactly how many concurrent tasks you can run.

Error Codes

Code Meaning Action
96 Concurrent task limit reached Wait for a running task to finish, or add funds
97 Insufficient balance Add funds to your account

Handling Code 96

A refused request returns HTTP 200 with "result": false and an error with code 96. No task is created and nothing is charged. Handle it in one of these ways:

  • Wait and retry: send the same request again after a growing wait, for example 2, 4, then 8 seconds, up to a minute. The code examples on this page do this: they look for the number 96 in errors[].code, retry only that code, treat "result": true as success and stop after 8 attempts.
  • Queue on your side: keep at most as many unfinished tasks as your limit allows, and send the next request when a task reaches task_postprocess_end or task_cancel (Task/Detail or the WebSocket). Tasks started on the website, by agents and by workflows, and in a team by other members, use the same slots.
  • Direct LLM Gateway: through the Direct LLM Gateway the refusal arrives as HTTP 429 with error type rate_limit_error and a retry-after header; wait that many seconds before you retry. A streamed Responses request has already answered 200, so it ends with response.failed carrying code rate_limit_exceeded and has no such header; use a growing wait there.
  • Wiro MCP server: through the Wiro MCP server, run_model returns the same message as its tool error.

Increasing Your Limit

To increase your concurrency limit, add credits to your account. Your limit is recalculated automatically based on your current balance at the time of each run request.

Best Practices

  • Check error code 96: if you get this error, wait for a running task to complete before submitting new ones. See Handling Code 96.
  • Use WebSocket for monitoring: instead of polling /Task/Detail repeatedly, connect via WebSocket to get real-time updates without extra API calls.
  • Use bounded MCP waits: run_model waits up to 45 seconds by default and returns a recoverable token when the task is still active. Continue with wait_for_task; do not call run_model again for the same request. Use wait=false only when you need the token immediately, and get_task for a one-time status check.
  • Implement exponential backoff: if polling task status, start at 3 seconds and increase the interval for longer tasks.

Spend Limits

Cap what a personal account or a team can spend in a month or a day: the whole wallet, one team member, one API key, a surface such as the LLM gateway, or one agent.

How Spend Limits Work

A spend limit caps what a wallet can spend in a month or a day. Limits work the same way for a personal account's wallet and for a team's wallet. The limits of the workspace a call runs in apply: a team project's API key runs in its team, a personal project's key in your personal account, and the dashboard in the workspace you have selected.

Manage limits in the dashboard under Controls > Spend Limits, for your personal account or for the team workspace you have selected, or with the /SpendLimit endpoints below. Team and member limits set before this system were moved into it as monthly limits of the same amount.

What a Limit Caps

Each limit caps one scope of the wallet's spending:

Scope target What it caps
account None The whole wallet. In a team, the whole team's spending
member The member's useruuid from /Team/Member/List One team member's spending in the team (team wallets only). A member's spending includes their dashboard runs in the team workspace and every run made with the API key of a team project they created
project The project's id from /Project/List One API key: what is spent with that project's key
surface web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow One way in (see Surfaces below)
agent The agent's guid (its useragentguid) One deployed agent: all of its AI usage, both what its plan includes and what the balance pays, and its own model runs. Its plan payments count toward the wallet's other limits, not this one

Surfaces

Surface Label Covers
web the dashboard The Wiro dashboard, and calls with a signed-in user's Bearer token
api the API Calls with an API key, including /sync and, for now, the Wiro MCP package when you run it yourself
mcp MCP The hosted Wiro MCP server at mcp.wiro.ai, and the Wiro MCP package when it names itself (see Surfaces)
llm-gateway the LLM gateway The OpenAI and Anthropic compatible LLM gateway at llm.wiro.ai
extension the browser extensions Only the Wiro browser extensions
agent agents Your deployed agents: their plan payments, the AI usage their balance pays and the models they run
studio Studio Studio: the messages you send it and the models it runs for you
workflow-agent the Workflow Agent The Workflow Agent: the messages you send it
workflow workflows Workflow runs and resumes, and every step they run

When work fits more than one surface, the first match in this order decides: who does it (Studio, the Workflow Agent or a deployed agent), what it is (a workflow run and its steps, unless a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent started it), which client sends it (the LLM gateway, a browser extension or MCP), and last which credential it uses (an API key, else a signed-in session). So a message to Studio sent with an API key counts on studio, and a workflow run started with an API key or through MCP on workflow. Each task records the surface it counted on: see Surfaces. Refusal messages and /SpendLimit/Usage name a surface by its label.

Studio, the Workflow Agent and workflows used to have no surface of their own. Studio and Workflow Agent work counted on web, or on api when it was sent with an API key, and a workflow run counted on the surface that started it. Limits that were already set were not changed, so a limit on web or api no longer covers this work: to cap it by surface, set a limit on studio, workflow-agent or workflow.

Periods and Amounts

A limit's period is month (the default), which resets on the 1st of each month at 00:00 UTC, or day, which resets every day at 00:00 UTC. A scope and target can have one monthly limit and one daily limit.

amountusd is the limit in USD, rounded to cents. Once rounded, it must be at least 0.01. A limit counts everything spent in its current period, also what was spent before the limit was added, so a new limit below that amount is used up at once.

What Counts

Every charge to the wallet for usage counts: model runs, workflow runs, realtime sessions, Studio, the Workflow Agent, agent plans and upgrades, and the AI usage of an agent that the balance pays. Deposits are not spending.

The models Studio runs for you are checked and counted like the runs you start yourself: against the account's or the team's limits, your member limit in a team, the limit of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's Studio project for a message sent from wiro.ai) and the limit of the studio surface. What the chat of Studio and the Workflow Agent costs counts toward your limits too, on the studio and workflow-agent surfaces.

An agent's AI usage counts in two ways. What its plan's included usage covers counts only toward the agent's own limit: the plan payment already counted toward the wallet's limits. What the balance pays once the included usage is used up counts toward the agent's own limit, the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the agent surface. Member and API key limits don't apply to an agent's AI usage. The models an agent runs count like any other model run, and toward the agent's own limit too.

When Limits Are Checked

Limits are checked before work starts:

  • Model runs, workflow runs and workflow resumes, and each step of a workflow run before the step starts
  • Studio and Workflow Agent messages, and the models Studio runs for you
  • An agent deploy, upgrade or renewal that a person starts
  • Messages to an agent, against that agent's own limit and, once its plan's included usage is used up, against the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the agent surface

When the price of the work is known before it starts, as for fixed-price models, workflow runs and agent plans, the work is refused if spending so far, plus what work in progress holds, plus that price would go over the limit. Otherwise it is refused once the limit has no room left.

Work that is already running finishes and is charged, with two exceptions. A realtime session ends after the turn that uses up a limit, the same way it ends when the balance runs out: its WebSocket clients get a task_session_stopped event with reason spend_limit, code 93 and the refusal /Run would give (see Realtime Voice). An agent's voice call is a realtime session too and ends the same way: a web voice call then gets session_end with reason spend_limit (see Web Voice), and a caller on the phone hears a short notice before the call ends. An agent pauses at its next model call when a limit that covers it is used up, even in the middle of a reply (see below).

Every agent plan payment, a deploy, a move to a higher plan or a renewal, counts toward the account's or the team's limit and the limit of the agent surface, whichever way it was made, and in a team toward the limit of the member who bought the plan. A payment made with an API key also counts toward that key's limit. A plan payment never counts toward the agent's own limit. Automatic monthly renewals of running agents count the same way, with no API key, and are never refused by a limit.

Work in Progress

A run that starts holds its expected price against every limit that covers it, until it is charged or ends. The next check counts what is held, so runs started at the same time can pass a limit by one run at most. A run whose price is not known before it starts goes ahead while the limit has room. Refusal messages show what is held, and so does heldusd on the limits of /SpendLimit/List and in /SpendLimit/Usage.

When a Limit Is Reached

New work the limit covers is refused with HTTP 200, result: false and error code 93. The message names the limit and says when it resets:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 93,
      "message": "This API key's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.20 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC."
    }
  ]
}

When the price of the work is known before it starts, the message says what is left instead, for example This team's monthly spend limit has $3.10 left of $500.00, and this run costs $4.00. It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC. A daily limit says daily instead of monthly, and its message ends with It resets at 00:00 UTC. When work in progress holds part of the limit, the message also says how much.

Limit The message starts with
A personal account's account limit Your monthly spend limit
A team's account limit This team's monthly spend limit
member Your monthly spend limit in this team
project This API key's monthly spend limit
surface The monthly spend limit for and the surface's label, for example The monthly spend limit for the LLM gateway or The monthly spend limit for the Workflow Agent
agent This agent's monthly spend limit

Nothing runs and nothing is charged. Retrying does not help until the limit resets or someone who manages it raises it. Through the LLM gateway the refusal is an HTTP 402 error with code spend_limit_reached, and the MCP server returns it as a tool error.

When a limit that covers an agent is used up, the agent pauses: its own limit at any time, and the account's or the team's limit or the agent surface's limit once its plan's included usage is used up. While included usage is left, those wallet limits don't stop it. A turn that is running stops at its next model call (see Failed turns), new messages to the agent are refused, and its Scheduled Tasks are paused rather than failed. In Telegram, Slack and Discord it tells people so in a plain sentence, with the time the limit resets when that is known. Once the limit resets, is raised or is removed, the agent answers again and each Scheduled Task runs at its next scheduled time, with no restart.

Alert Emails

A limit sends an alert email when spending reaches its alertpct: 50, 80 (the default) or 90 percent of the limit, or null for no alert email. It sends a used-up email when the limit is reached. Each email goes out once per limit and period, and changing the limit re-arms both for the current period. The emails link to the Spend Limits page of the workspace the limit belongs to.

A personal account's limits email the account. A team's limits email the team's admins and the organization owner, and also the member a member limit is for, the person who created the API key a key limit is for, and the owner of the agent an agent limit is for.

Who Can Change Limits

  • Personal account: its owner
  • Team: a team admin or the organization owner. The person who created the team is one of its admins

Every team member can read the team's limits and spending with /SpendLimit/List and /SpendLimit/Usage. A member who is not an admin can't change any limit: not their own member limit, and not the limits of the API keys they created or the agents they deployed. A deployed agent's own calls to the /SpendLimit endpoints are refused with HTTP 403, reads included.

Changing Limits With the API

/SpendLimit/Set, /SpendLimit/Remove and /SpendLimit/Preview work in the dashboard, with a signed-in user's Bearer token and with an API key:

  • With an API key, the call acts as the person who created the key's project, in that project's workspace: the creator's personal account for a personal project, the team for a team project. The key follows its creator's current role: while the creator is a team member who is not an admin, the key can read limits but not change them.
  • With a Bearer token, the call acts as you, in your personal account. To work in a team, send the team's guid in the x-team-guid header. A call whose x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own, is refused with You are not a member of this team. Calls with an API key ignore this header.

/SpendLimit/List and /SpendLimit/Preview return the workspace they work in, so you can check where a change lands before you make it. Changes made with API keys are limited to 60 per workspace in any hour, counting spend limits and Model Access rules together. Preview does not count. Each change is recorded with who made it and how.

POST /SpendLimit/List

Returns the spend limits of the call's workspace, each with what has been spent in its current period, and how the call itself counts. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected (see Changing Limits With the API). Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. Send an empty body: {}.

Response

Field Description
workspace.type team or personal
workspace.teamguid The team's guid, or null for a personal account
workspace.canmanage Whether the caller can change limits in this workspace: true for a personal account's owner, a team admin and the organization owner, also with the API key of a project they created; false for other team members and their keys
caller.surface The surface this call counts on, such as api for a call with an API key (see Surfaces)
caller.projectid The project id of the API key the call used, or null without a key
limits[].guid The limit's guid, for /SpendLimit/Remove
limits[].scope account, member, project, surface or agent
limits[].target The member's useruuid, the project id, the surface or the agent's guid; "" for account
limits[].targetlabel The member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label; null for account
limits[].period month or day
limits[].amountusd The limit in USD
limits[].alertpct 50, 80 or 90, or null for no alert email
limits[].periodstart Start of the current period, in Unix seconds
limits[].resetsat When the current period ends and the limit resets, in Unix seconds
limits[].createdat, limits[].updatedat When the limit was added and last changed, in Unix seconds
limits[].updatedby Who changed the limit last: useruuid and label, the person's name, or their email when they have no name. In a team, the owner of its organization who is not a member of the team is labeled the organization owner, and someone who has left the team has a null label. A change made with an API key names the person who created the key's project. updatedby is null when Wiro changed the limit last, as for the team and member limits moved into this system
limits[].spentusd What has been spent in the current period, in USD
limits[].heldusd When work in progress holds part of the limit: how much it holds, in USD (see Work in Progress)

POST /SpendLimit/Set

Adds a spend limit to the call's workspace, or changes the existing limit with the same scope, target and period. Changing a limit re-arms its emails for the current period. Only the people who can change limits can call it (see Who Can Change Limits), in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key. To check a change first, send the same body to /SpendLimit/Preview.

Parameter Type Required Description
scope string Yes "account", "member", "project", "surface" or "agent". See Spend Limits
target string For every scope but account The member's useruuid, the project's id, the surface (web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow) or the agent's guid. Leave it out for account
period string No "month" or "day". Default: "month"
amountusd number Yes The limit in USD, rounded to cents. Once rounded, it must be at least 0.01
alertpct number No When the alert email goes out: 50, 80 or 90 percent of the limit, or null for no alert email. Default: 80

Examples

Cap the whole wallet at $500 a month, with the alert at 90%:

{
  "scope": "account",
  "amountusd": 500,
  "alertpct": 90
}

Cap one API key at $100 a month:

{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "period": "month",
  "amountusd": 100
}

Cap the LLM gateway at $25 a day, with no alert email:

{
  "scope": "surface",
  "target": "llm-gateway",
  "period": "day",
  "amountusd": 25,
  "alertpct": null
}

Response

limit is the limit as saved, shaped like a row of /SpendLimit/List:

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "limit": {
    "guid": "15be7fb3-c602-4ff1-a3f1-3afaa3996974",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 100,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": 1794474300,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" },
    "spentusd": 61.4
  }
}

Errors

Error Cause
scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent. scope is missing or not one of the five scopes
Member limits exist only in a team workspace. A member limit in a personal account
target is required for this scope. No target for a member, project, surface or agent limit
A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow. A surface limit with another target
target must be a project id. A project limit whose target is not a project id
period must be month or day. Another period
amountusd must be a positive number. amountusd is missing, zero or negative
amountusd is too large. amountusd is over 10,000,000
amountusd must be at least 0.01. amountusd is above zero but rounds to less than one cent
alertpct must be 50, 80 or 90, or null for no alert. Another alertpct
You are not a member of this team. With a Bearer token, x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own
Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit. In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner
This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit. With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin
That person is not an active member of this team. A member limit for someone who is not an active member of the team
That API key's project is not in this workspace. A project limit for a project of another workspace
That agent is not in this workspace. An agent limit for an agent of another workspace
Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later. With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour

POST /SpendLimit/Preview

Shows what /SpendLimit/Set would do, and changes nothing. It takes the same body as /SpendLimit/Set and checks it the same way, so only the people who can change limits can call it. Use it to see which workspace a change lands in, the limit as it would be saved and the limit it would replace.

Example

Raise the Production API key's monthly limit to $150:

{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "period": "month",
  "amountusd": 150
}

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "preview": true,
  "workspace": {
    "type": "team",
    "teamguid": "0d9aade4-d31b-4b97-88f3-a90482f080ea",
    "canmanage": true
  },
  "limit": {

    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 150,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": null,
    "updatedby": null,
    "spentusd": 88.2
  },
  "existing": {
    "guid": "15be7fb3-c602-4ff1-a3f1-3afaa3996974",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "period": "month",
    "amountusd": 100,
    "alertpct": 80,
    "periodstart": 1793491200,
    "resetsat": 1796083200,
    "createdat": 1794474300,
    "updatedat": 1794474300,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" },
    "spentusd": 88.2
  }
}
Field Description
preview Always true: nothing was changed
workspace The workspace the change would be made in, as in /SpendLimit/List: type, teamguid and canmanage, which is always true here
limit The limit as /SpendLimit/Set would save it, shaped like a row of /SpendLimit/List, with what has been spent in its current period. Its guid and createdat are those of the limit it would replace, or null for a new limit, and its updatedat and updatedby are null
existing The current limit with the same scope, target and period, which the change would replace, or null when there is none

When limit.spentusd is already at or above the new amount, the limit is used up as soon as it is saved. The errors are those of /SpendLimit/Set, except that Preview does not count toward the hourly cap on changes made with API keys.

POST /SpendLimit/Remove

Removes a spend limit from the call's workspace. The people who can change limits can remove one, in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key.

Parameter Type Required Description
guid string Yes The limit's guid from /SpendLimit/List

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": []
}
Error Cause
guid is required. No guid was sent
Limit not found in this workspace. The guid is not a limit of the call's workspace, or it was already removed
You are not a member of this team. With a Bearer token, x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own
Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit. In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner
This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit. With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin
Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later. With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour

POST /SpendLimit/Usage

Returns what the call's workspace has spent this month or today, in total and by surface, member, API key and agent. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected. Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key.

Parameter Type Required Description
period string No "month" or "day". Default: "month"

Field Description
usage.period month or day
usage.periodstart, usage.resetsat Start and end of the period, in Unix seconds
usage.totalusd What the wallet has spent in the period, in USD
usage.heldusd What work in progress holds, in USD. Present only when it holds something (see Work in Progress)
usage.surfaces One row per surface, always all nine in the order web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow, with its label
usage.members Spending per team member, with the member's name as label. Empty for a personal account
usage.projects Spending per API key, with the project's name as label
usage.agents Spending per deployed agent, with the agent's title as label
heldusd in a row of usage.surfaces, usage.members, usage.projects or usage.agents What work in progress holds for that row, present only when it holds something. A member, API key or agent whose only spending so far is held work is listed with spentusd 0

An agent plan's automatic renewal counts in totalusd, in the agent row of usage.surfaces and, in a team, in the row of the member who bought the plan, but in no row of usage.projects or usage.agents, so those rows can add up to less than totalusd. An agent's row counts what its own limit counts, so it also holds the AI usage its plan covered, which is not in totalusd: the plan payment already is.

For other breakdowns, /Project/UsageSummary gives usage per project and /Task/Stat gives time-series task execution data. Both filter by the active workspace.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Model Access

Choose which models a personal account or a team can run: allow or block single models and whole categories, for the whole wallet, one team member, one API key, a surface such as the LLM gateway, or one agent.

How Model Access Works

A Model Access rule decides which models a wallet's work can run. Rules work the same way for a personal account's wallet and for a team's wallet. The rules of the workspace a call runs in apply: a team project's API key runs in its team, a personal project's key in your personal account, and the dashboard in the workspace you have selected.

Manage rules in the dashboard under Controls > Model Access, for your personal account or for the team workspace you have selected, or with the /ModelAccess endpoints below. A workspace without rules can run every model. Team allowlists and blocklists set before this system were moved into it as rules for the whole team.

What a Rule Covers

Each rule covers one scope of the wallet's work, the same scopes as spend limits. A scope and target can have one rule:

Scope target What it covers
account None Everything the wallet runs. In a team, every run in the team
member The member's useruuid from /Team/Member/List One team member's runs in the team (team wallets only): their dashboard runs in the team workspace and every run made with the API key of a team project they created
project The project's id from /Project/List One API key: the runs made with that project's key
surface web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow One way in (see Surfaces below)
agent The agent's guid (its useragentguid) One deployed agent: the models it runs through Wiro, the chat models it answers with and its built-in voice

Surfaces

Surface Covers
web The Wiro dashboard, and calls with a signed-in user's Bearer token
api Calls with an API key, including /sync and, for now, the Wiro MCP package when you run it yourself
mcp The hosted Wiro MCP server at mcp.wiro.ai, and the Wiro MCP package when it names itself (see Surfaces)
llm-gateway The OpenAI and Anthropic compatible LLM gateway at llm.wiro.ai
extension Only the Wiro browser extensions
agent Your deployed agents' own runs
studio Studio: the chat model of each message you send it, and the models it runs for you
workflow-agent The Workflow Agent: the chat model of each message you send it
workflow Workflow runs and resumes, and every step they run

A run counts on one surface, decided the same way as for spend limits: the first match among who does it (Studio, the Workflow Agent or a deployed agent), what it is (a workflow run and its steps, unless a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent started it), which client sends it (the LLM gateway, a browser extension or MCP), and last which credential it uses (an API key, else a signed-in session). So a message to Studio sent with an API key counts on studio, and a workflow run started with an API key or through MCP on workflow. See Surfaces.

Studio, the Workflow Agent and workflows used to have no surface of their own. Studio and Workflow Agent work counted on web, or on api when it was sent with an API key, and a workflow run counted on the surface that started it. Rules that were already set were not changed, so a rule on web or api no longer covers this work: to decide its models by surface, set a rule on studio, workflow-agent or workflow.

Everything Else

Every rule has an Everything Else setting, access. It decides the models the rule names neither one by one nor by category:

  • allow (the default): every model can run except the ones the rule blocks
  • block: only the models and categories the rule allows can run

Categories

A rule can allow or block whole categories of models. Each category groups catalog categories, the values models carry in their categories field on /Tool/List and /Tool/Detail. A category also covers the models added to it later.

category Label Catalog categories
image Image Generation text-to-image, image-to-image, image-editing, image-to-text
video Video Generation text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, speech-to-video, talking-head, video-to-text, reference-to-video, audio-to-video, lip-sync
audio Audio & Speech text-to-speech, speech-to-text, speech-to-speech, video-to-music, voice-clone, text-to-audio, image-to-audio, realtime-conversation, realtime-tts, realtime-stt
music Music Generation music-generation, text-to-song, text-to-music, image-to-song, image-to-music
3d 3D Generation 3d-generation, text-to-3d, image-to-3d
llm LLM & Chat chat, llm, partner-llm, rag, llm-reasoning
utilities Utilities utils

A model is in every category that one of its catalog categories belongs to, so it can be in more than one. A model whose catalog categories belong to none of them is decided by its own entry or by Everything Else. /ModelAccess/List returns this list, and /ModelAccess/Check shows the categories of one model.

Single Models

A rule can also allow or block single models, named by their owner/slug, such as openai/gpt-6-2-astra, or by their id. A model's own entry comes before its categories, so a rule can block a category and still allow one model in it. A rule can name up to 500 models, and each must be a model listed on Wiro.

How One Rule Decides

A rule decides a model in this order:

  1. The model: when the rule names the model, that entry decides
  2. Its categories: otherwise, when the rule names one or more of the model's categories, they decide. If one of them is blocked, the model is blocked, even when another one is allowed
  3. Everything Else: otherwise the rule's access decides

For example, a rule with Everything Else set to allow, Video Generation blocked and bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash allowed lets every model run except video models, and Seedance v2.5 Flash is the one video model it lets run.

When Several Rules Apply

A run can meet several rules of its wallet: the whole account's, the member's in a team, the API key's, the surface's and the agent's. It goes ahead only when every rule that applies allows the model. A narrower rule can't open what a wider one blocks: when the account's rule blocks a model, an API key's rule that allows it does not let it run.

When more than one rule blocks the model, the refusal names the first of them in the order account, member, API key, surface, agent. /ModelAccess/Check shows how each rule decides a model.

Where Rules Apply

Rules are checked before work starts:

  • Model runs: /Run and its /sync wait, realtime sessions, the LLM gateway, the MCP server, the browser extensions and the dashboard
  • Workflow runs and resumes: every model step that will run must be allowed. Steps that will not run, such as the steps after a breakpoint, are not checked
  • Studio and the Workflow Agent: the models Studio runs for you, and the chat model of each message you send to Studio or the Workflow Agent, follow your own rules like the runs you start yourself: the account's or the team's rule, your member rule in a team, the rule of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's Studio project for a message sent from wiro.ai) and the rule of the studio surface, or of workflow-agent for a message to the Workflow Agent. A message whose chat model a rule blocks, the model it names or the default chat model when it names none, is refused with code 92 before anything runs. Chat models are LLM & Chat models: a rule that blocks LLM & Chat blocks them unless it allows the chat model by name, and a rule that lets only selected models run blocks them unless it allows LLM & Chat or the chat model. The Workflow Agent runs nothing but its chat model. /Studio/Status and /StudioWorkflow/Status list the chat models your rules block
  • The models your deployed agents run through Wiro
  • An agent's chat model: choosing one in the agent's settings, or sending model with Message/Send, follows that agent's own rule, the account's or the team's rule and the rule of the agent surface, since the agent's AI usage past its plan is paid from the wallet. Member and API key rules don't apply to it. If one of these rules blocks the model the agent already uses, its model calls are refused and the turn ends with [MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED]. A Scheduled Task whose model a rule blocks is paused rather than failed, and runs again at its next scheduled time once the model is allowed or another one is chosen
  • An agent's built-in voice: transcription of the voice notes people send the agent, and the voice replies it sends, follow the same rules as its chat model, as Audio & Speech models. A rule that blocks Audio & Speech, or that lets only selected models run without allowing Audio & Speech, blocks them, even when it allows LLM & Chat. Voice notes are then not transcribed, and the agent replies in text. An agent that chats on a Gemini model has its voice notes transcribed by google/gemini-3-flash, so a rule that names that model decides them too. A rule that does not name that model blocks those voice notes unless it lets both Audio & Speech and LLM & Chat models run

A change applies to work that starts after it. Work that is already running is not stopped, and a deployed agent's chat model and voice follow a change within about a minute. Browsing models is not affected: /Tool/List, /Tool/Detail and the LLM gateway's model list show the same models whatever the rules.

When a Model Is Blocked

A run of a model that a rule blocks is refused with HTTP 200, result: false and error code 92, even when the wallet has money. The message names the rule:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 92,
      "message": "This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run."
    }
  ]
}

The message also says what blocked the model:

Blocked by Example message
Everything Else This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.
The model's own entry This API key can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra. Model Access rules decide which models can run.
One of the model's categories MCP can't use Video Generation models, and bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash is one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.
Rule The message starts with
A personal account's account rule Your account
A team's account rule This team
member You, with in this team after the model or category, for example You can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra in this team.
project This API key
surface The surface's name: The dashboard, The API, MCP, The LLM gateway, The browser extensions, Agents, Studio, The Workflow Agent or Workflows, for example Studio can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra.
agent This agent

Nothing runs and nothing is charged. Retrying does not help: run a model the rules allow, or ask someone who manages the rule to change it. Through the LLM gateway the refusal is an HTTP 403 error with code model_not_allowed, and the MCP server returns it as a tool error.

Who Can Change Rules

  • Personal account: its owner
  • Team: a team admin or the organization owner. The person who created the team is one of its admins

Every team member can read the team's rules with /ModelAccess/List and /ModelAccess/Check. A member who is not an admin can't change any rule: not their own member rule, and not the rules of the API keys they created or the agents they deployed. A deployed agent's own calls to the /ModelAccess endpoints are refused with HTTP 403, reads included.

Changing Rules With the API

/ModelAccess/Set, /ModelAccess/Remove and /ModelAccess/Preview work in the dashboard, with a signed-in user's Bearer token and with an API key:

  • With an API key, the call acts as the person who created the key's project, in that project's workspace: the creator's personal account for a personal project, the team for a team project. The key follows its creator's current role: while the creator is a team member who is not an admin, the key can read rules but not change them.
  • With a Bearer token, the call acts as you, in your personal account. To work in a team, send the team's guid in the x-team-guid header. A call whose x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own, is refused with You are not a member of this team. Calls with an API key ignore this header.

/ModelAccess/List and /ModelAccess/Preview return the workspace they work in, so you can check where a change lands before you make it. Changes made with API keys are limited to 60 per workspace in any hour, counting spend limits and Model Access rules together. Preview does not count. Each change is recorded with who made it and how.

POST /ModelAccess/List

Returns the Model Access rules of the call's workspace, the categories a rule can name, and how the call itself counts. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected (see Changing Rules With the API). Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. Send an empty body: {}.
