Field Description
workspace.type team or personal
workspace.teamguid The team's guid, or null for a personal account
workspace.canmanage Whether the caller can change rules in this workspace: true for a personal account's owner, a team admin and the organization owner, also with the API key of a project they created; false for other team members and their keys
caller.surface The surface this call counts on, such as api for a call with an API key (see Surfaces)
caller.projectid The project id of the API key the call used, or null without a key
rules[].guid The rule's guid, for /ModelAccess/Remove
rules[].scope account, member, project, surface or agent
rules[].target The member's useruuid, the project id, the surface or the agent's guid; "" for account
rules[].targetlabel The member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label; null for account
rules[].access Everything Else: allow or block
rules[].categories The categories the rule names, each with its label and access, in the order of categories below
rules[].models The models the rule names, in id order: id (a string), model (owner/slug), title and access. model and title are null for a model that is no longer on Wiro
rules[].createdat, rules[].updatedat When the rule was added and last changed, in Unix seconds
rules[].updatedby Who changed the rule last: useruuid and label, the person's name, or their email when they have no name. In a team, the owner of its organization who is not a member of the team is labeled the organization owner, and someone who has left the team has a null label. A change made with an API key names the person who created the key's project. updatedby is null when Wiro changed the rule last, as for the team allowlists and blocklists moved into this system
categories The seven categories a rule can name: category (the key a rule uses), label and values (the catalog categories it covers)

POST /ModelAccess/Set

Adds a rule to the call's workspace, or replaces the rule with the same scope and target. The rule you send replaces the old one as a whole, so a category or model you leave out is no longer named. Only the people who can change rules can call it (see Who Can Change Rules), in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key. To check a change first, send the same body to /ModelAccess/Preview.

Parameter Type Required Description
scope string Yes "account", "member", "project", "surface" or "agent". See What a Rule Covers
target string For every scope but account The member's useruuid, the project's id, the surface (web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow) or the agent's guid. Leave it out for account
access string No Everything Else: "allow" or "block". Default: "allow"
categories array or object No The categories the rule allows or blocks, as [{ "category": "video", "access": "block" }] or as { "video": "block" }. A category is image, video, audio, music, 3d, llm or utilities
models array or object No The single models the rule allows or blocks, as [{ "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra", "access": "block" }] or as { "openai/gpt-6-2-astra": "block" }. Name a model by its owner/slug or its id. At most 500 models

Examples

Block video models for the whole account, except one:

{
  "scope": "account",
  "access": "allow",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "video", "access": "block" }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "model": "bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}

Let one API key run only image models:

{
  "scope": "project",
  "target": "48211",
  "access": "block",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "image", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}

Keep video models out of MCP:

{
  "scope": "surface",
  "target": "mcp",
  "categories": { "video": "block" }
}

Block one model for one agent:

{
  "scope": "agent",
  "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
  "models": { "openai/gpt-6-2-astra": "block" }
}

Response

rule is the rule as saved, shaped like a row of /ModelAccess/List:

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "rule": {
    "guid": "a4308936-5441-4012-96ee-f2b32ad3fd40",
    "scope": "project",
    "target": "48211",
    "targetlabel": "Production",
    "access": "block",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795184400,
    "updatedat": 1795188000,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
  }
}

Errors

Error Cause
scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent. scope is missing or not one of the five scopes
Member rules exist only in a team workspace. A member rule in a personal account
target is required for this scope. No target for a member, project, surface or agent rule
A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow. A surface rule with another target
target must be a project id. A project rule whose target is not a project id
access must be allow or block. Another access
categories must be a list of { category, access }. categories is neither a list nor an object
A category is one of image, video, audio, music, 3d, llm, utilities. A category that is not one of the seven
A category's access must be allow or block. A category with another access
models must be a list of { model, access }. models is neither a list nor an object
A rule can name at most 500 models. More than 500 models
Each model needs its owner/slug or id. A model entry with no model
A model's access must be allow or block. A model with another access
<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id. A model named neither by owner/slug nor by a number
<model> is not a model on Wiro. No model listed on Wiro has that owner/slug or id
<model> is named twice. models names a model twice: by the same name, or by its id and its owner/slug with a different access
You are not a member of this team. With a Bearer token, x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own
Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule. In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner
This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule. With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin
That person is not an active member of this team. A member rule for someone who is not an active member of the team
That API key's project is not in this workspace. A project rule for a project of another workspace
That agent is not in this workspace. An agent rule for an agent of another workspace
Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later. With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour

POST /ModelAccess/Preview

Shows what /ModelAccess/Set would do, and changes nothing. It takes the same body as /ModelAccess/Set and checks it the same way, so only the people who can change rules can call it. Use it to see which workspace a change lands in, the rule as it would be saved and the rule it would replace. For an agent rule, it also says whether the rule would block the chat model the agent answers with.

Example

Let the Support Agent run only image models:

{
  "scope": "agent",
  "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
  "access": "block",
  "categories": [
    { "category": "image", "access": "allow" }
  ]
}

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "preview": true,
  "workspace": {
    "type": "team",
    "teamguid": "0d9aade4-d31b-4b97-88f3-a90482f080ea",
    "canmanage": true
  },
  "rule": {
    "guid": "c2f0a9d4-5b7e-4c1a-8e36-9d4b2a7f1e05",
    "scope": "agent",
    "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
    "targetlabel": "Support Agent",
    "access": "block",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795195200,
    "updatedat": null,
    "updatedby": null
  },
  "existing": {
    "guid": "c2f0a9d4-5b7e-4c1a-8e36-9d4b2a7f1e05",
    "scope": "agent",
    "target": "6e4bbd6f-6b73-4421-adae-e9599ba2e317",
    "targetlabel": "Support Agent",
    "access": "allow",
    "categories": [
      { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
    ],
    "models": [],
    "createdat": 1795195200,
    "updatedat": 1795195200,
    "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
  },
  "agentchatmodel": {
    "ref": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "model": "openai/gpt-5-6-sol",
    "blocked": true
  }
}
Field Description
preview Always true: nothing was changed
workspace The workspace the change would be made in, as in /ModelAccess/List: type, teamguid and canmanage, which is always true here
rule The rule as /ModelAccess/Set would save it, shaped like a row of /ModelAccess/List. Its guid and createdat are those of the rule it would replace, or null for a new rule, and its updatedat and updatedby are null
existing The current rule with the same scope and target, which the change would replace, or null when there is none
agentchatmodel For an agent rule only: the chat model the agent answers with, as its settings name it (ref) and by its owner/slug on Wiro (model), and whether the rule would block it (blocked)

When agentchatmodel.blocked is true, the agent stops answering within about a minute of the rule being saved: its turns end with [MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED]. Allow its chat model in the rule too, or allow LLM & Chat. The errors are those of /ModelAccess/Set, except that Preview does not count toward the hourly cap on changes made with API keys.

POST /ModelAccess/Remove

Removes a rule from the call's workspace. The people who can change rules can remove one, in the dashboard, with a Bearer token or with an API key.

Parameter Type Required Description
guid string Yes The rule's guid from /ModelAccess/List

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": []
}
Error Cause
guid is required. No guid was sent
Rule not found in this workspace. The guid is not a rule of the call's workspace, or it was already removed
You are not a member of this team. With a Bearer token, x-team-guid names a team you are not a member of, and whose organization you don't own
Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule. In a team, a signed-in caller is not a team admin or the organization owner
This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule. With an API key, the person who created the key's project is a team member who is not an admin
Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later. With API keys, this workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules have been changed 60 times in the last hour

POST /ModelAccess/Check

Shows how the rules of the call's workspace decide one model for one run: which rules apply, what each one decides and why, and the refusal the run would get. Nothing runs. A team project's API key reads its team, a personal project's key your personal account, and the dashboard the workspace you have selected. Any team member can call it, and it works with an API key. With only model, it checks a dashboard run of yours. To check another run, name it with member, project, agent or surface. check.context in the response says which run was checked.

Parameter Type Required Description
model string Yes The model's owner/slug or id
member string No In a team, the useruuid of the member whose dashboard run to check. Default: you (with an API key, the person who created its project). With project or agent, the run is checked as the person who created that API key, and member is not used
project string No A project's id, to check a run made with that project's API key, as the person who created the project. The surface is then api unless you name another one, and web is refused: a run made with an API key never counts as the dashboard
surface string No Where the run comes from: web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow. Default: web, a dashboard run. With project the default is api, and with agent the surface is always agent. The agent surface needs an agent: send its guid in agent
agent string No An agent's guid, to check a model run that agent makes: with the API key it runs models with, as the person who created that key, on the agent surface. project is not used then

Example

Can the Production API key run openai/gpt-6-2-astra?

{
  "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra",
  "project": "48211",
  "surface": "api"
}

Response

Each applicable rule comes back shaped like a row of /ModelAccess/List, with what it decides. This workspace is a team, so check.context shows the key's run checked as Jane Doe, who created the Production project:

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "check": {
    "model": "openai/gpt-6-2-astra",
    "categories": ["llm"],
    "allowed": false,
    "message": "This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.",
    "rules": [
      {
        "rule": {
          "guid": "a642eda4-68ef-4fa9-af15-7024f28b0332",
          "scope": "account",
          "target": "",
          "targetlabel": null,
          "access": "allow",
          "categories": [
            { "category": "video", "label": "Video Generation", "access": "block" }
          ],
          "models": [
            { "id": "2062", "model": "bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash", "title": "Seedance v2.5 Flash Video Generator", "access": "allow" }
          ],
          "createdat": 1795180800,
          "updatedat": 1795180800,
          "updatedby": { "useruuid": "c1d2e3f4-a5b6-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f", "label": "the organization owner" }
        },
        "access": "allow",
        "by": "default",
        "category": null
      },
      {
        "rule": {
          "guid": "a4308936-5441-4012-96ee-f2b32ad3fd40",
          "scope": "project",
          "target": "48211",
          "targetlabel": "Production",
          "access": "block",
          "categories": [
            { "category": "image", "label": "Image Generation", "access": "allow" }
          ],
          "models": [],
          "createdat": 1795184400,
          "updatedat": 1795188000,
          "updatedby": { "useruuid": "7a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d", "label": "John Doe" }
        },
        "access": "block",
        "by": "default",
        "category": null
      }
    ],
    "context": {
      "surface": "api",
      "member": { "useruuid": "3f5a9c20-6d41-4b8e-a1c7-5e9d0f2b4c61", "label": "Jane Doe" },
      "project": { "projectid": "48211", "label": "Production" },
      "agent": null
    }
  }
}
Field Description
check.model The model as owner/slug
check.categories The categories the model is in, such as ["llm"]. Empty when it is in none
check.allowed Whether every rule that applies allows the model
check.message The refusal a run would get with code 92, or null when the model is allowed
check.rules The rules that apply, in the order account, member, API key, surface, agent. Empty when none applies
check.rules[].rule The rule, shaped like a row of /ModelAccess/List
check.rules[].access What this rule decides: allow or block
check.rules[].by What decided it: model (the model's own entry), category (one of its categories) or default (Everything Else)
check.rules[].category The category that decided it when by is category, else null
check.context Which run was checked: surface, member, project and agent
check.context.surface The surface the run was checked on: the surface you sent, else api with project and web without it. Always agent with agent
check.context.member In a team, the member the run was checked as: useruuid, and the member's name as label. That is the member you sent, else you, and with project or agent the person who created that API key. null in a personal account
check.context.project The project whose API key the run was checked with: projectid, and the project's name as label. That is the project you sent, or for an agent the Wiro project it runs models with. null without project or agent
check.context.agent The agent whose run was checked: useragentguid, and the agent's title as label. null without agent
Error Cause
model is required. No model was sent
<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id. model is neither an owner/slug nor a number
<model> is not a model on Wiro. No model listed on Wiro has that owner/slug or id
A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow. Another surface
Name the agent to check its runs. surface is agent and no agent was sent
That API key's project is not in this workspace. project is not the id of a project of this workspace
A run made with an API key never counts as the dashboard. Leave surface out or pick another one. project with surface web
That agent is not in this workspace. agent is not the guid of an agent of this workspace
That agent has no API key to run models with yet. The agent has no Wiro project to run models with yet: connect one with /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind
That agent runs models with an API key of another workspace, so that workspace's rules decide them. The Wiro project the agent runs models with is in another workspace
This section as Markdown: View Download

Error Reference

Understand API error responses, error codes, and how to handle them.

Response Format

When an API request fails, the response includes result: false and an errors array:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": 97,
      "message": "Insufficient balance"
    }
  ]
}

All API responses return HTTP 200. Use the result field and error code to determine success or failure.

Error Codes

Error codes indicate the category of the problem. Use these for conditional logic in your application.

Code Category Description
0 General Server-side errors, validation failures, missing parameters
1 Not Found / Client Resource not found or not accessible
92 Model Access A Model Access rule of the workspace blocks the model. See Model Access
93 Spend Limit A spend limit of the workspace is reached. See Spend Limits
96 Concurrency Limit Too many concurrent tasks for your balance. See Concurrency Limits
97 Insufficient Balance Not enough funds to run the model
98 Authentication Required Sign in required to access this model
99 Token Invalid Bearer token missing, invalid, or expired

Authentication Errors

Returned when API key or bearer token authentication fails. All return HTTP 401.

Error Code Message
API key not found 0 Project authorization is not founded.
Signature required 0 Project requires signature authentication. x-signature and x-nonce headers are required.
Invalid signature 0 Project authorization is not valid.
IP not allowed 0 Requested ip {ip} is not allowed.
Key creator left the team 0 The person who created this API key is no longer in its team. Ask a team admin for a new key.
Team change with an API key 0 API keys can't manage teams or organizations. Sign in and try again.
Bearer token missing 99 Authorization bearer token is not founded in headers.
Bearer token invalid 99 Authorization bearer token is invalid.
Bearer token expired 99 Authorization bearer token expired.
Endpoint not found 0 Parsing url error. (HTTP 404)

Signature Auth Errors

If your project uses signature-based authentication, ensure all three headers are present and the signature is computed correctly:

x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
x-signature: HMAC-SHA256(key=API_KEY, message=API_SECRET + NONCE)
x-nonce: Unix timestamp or random integer

See Authentication for details.

IP Whitelist Errors

If your project has an IP whitelist configured, requests from unlisted IPs will be rejected. Use * in the whitelist to allow all IPs.

Team API Key Errors

A team project's API key works only while the user who created the project is an active member of the team or the organization owner. Once they leave the team, requests with the key fail with "The person who created this API key is no longer in its team." Public endpoints such as Tool/List and Agent/List still answer, as if the request had no key. Switch to a key from a project that an active member created.

Creating, changing, deleting or restoring organizations and teams, managing members and invitations, and moving projects, agents or credit need a signed-in user, in the dashboard or with a Bearer token. With an API key, these calls fail with "API keys can't manage teams or organizations." See Team API Access.

Studio and the Workflow Agent are stricter: the user who created the key's project must be an active member of the team, and being the organization owner is not enough. When that user is the organization owner but not a member of the team, requests to them fail with HTTP 403:

Error Code Message
Not a team member 0 You must be a member of this team to perform this action

Run Errors

Returned by POST /Run/{owner}/{model}.

Balance & Limits

Error Code Message Action
Insufficient balance 97 Insufficient balance Add funds: minimum $0.50 required ($10 for training)
Model blocked 92 This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run. Run a model the rules allow, or ask someone who manages the rule to change it under Controls > Model Access. The message names the rule. See Model Access
Spend limit reached 93 This API key's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.20 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC. Wait for the limit to reset, or have someone who manages it raise it under Controls > Spend Limits. The message names the limit. See Spend Limits
Concurrent task limit 96 You have reached your concurrent task limit. With your current balance of ${balance}, you can run up to {maxConcurrent} tasks at the same time. Add funds to increase your limit. Wait for a task to finish, or add funds. See Concurrency Limits
Sign in required 98 sign in to run this model Model requires a registered account

Validation Errors

Error Code Message
Missing parameter 0 Request parameter [{name}] required
Invalid number 0 Request parameter [{name}] must be integer or float
Out of range 0 Request parameter [{name}] must be between {min} and {max}
File required 0 Request files [{name}] required
Invalid request body 0 Request parameters are invalid.

Model Access Errors

Error Code Message
Model not accessible 1 tool-not-accessible
Model not found 1 slug-owner-project-not-exist
Account suspended 0 Your account has been suspended. Please contact support if you believe this is a mistake.
Permission denied 0 You don't have any permission for this action.
Model blocked by a Model Access rule 92 This API key can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra. Model Access rules decide which models can run.

Training Model Errors

Error Code Message
Invalid model name 0 Your model name should be contain (A-Z) (0-9) (-) (_) (.)
Reserved name 0 This name is not allowed
Name taken 0 This model name is already in use

Task Errors

Returned by POST /Task/Detail, POST /Task/Cancel, POST /Task/Kill, and POST /Task/InputOutputDelete.

Error Code Message Endpoint
Task not found 0 task-not-founded Detail
Task not found 1 There is no task yet. Cancel
Task not found 0 There is no task yet. Kill, InputOutputDelete
Missing identifier 0 Request parameter [taskid or tasktoken] required Detail
Missing identifier 0 taskid or socketaccesstoken is required Kill
Not cancellable 1 Task is not in a cancellable state. Cancel
Kill failed 1 Task could not be killed: {reason} Kill
Task not completed 0 Task must be completed or cancelled before deleting files InputOutputDelete
Permission denied 0 You don't have any permission for this action. Detail, Cancel

Error Handling

Always check result first, then inspect the code in the errors array:

const data = await response.json();

if (!data.result) {
  const error = data.errors[0];
  switch (error.code) {
    case 92:
      console.log('Model blocked by a Model Access rule: run a model the rules allow');
      break;
    case 93:
      console.log('Spend limit reached: wait for the reset or raise the limit');
      break;
    case 96:
      console.log('Concurrent limit — wait for a task to finish');
      break;
    case 97:
      console.log('Insufficient balance — add funds');
      break;
    case 98:
      console.log('Sign in required');
      break;
    default:
      console.log('Error:', error.message);
  }
}

Retry Strategy

Code Retryable Strategy
0 (validation) No Fix the request parameters
0 (server) Yes Retry with exponential backoff
1 No Check model slug or task token
92 No Run a model the rules allow, or ask someone who manages the rule to change it
93 No Wait until the limit resets or someone who manages it raises it
96 Yes Wait for a running task to complete
97 No Add funds, then retry
98 No Sign in or use authenticated credentials
99 No Check your API key or bearer token

FAQ

Common questions about using the Wiro API. If you can't find the answer here, contact support.

Sign up at wiro.ai, then create a project at wiro.ai/panel/project. Copy your API key (and secret, if signature-based) and store them securely. You can see them again on the Projects page after you confirm it's you.

Signature-Based is recommended. It uses HMAC-SHA256 so your API secret never leaves your environment. API Key Only is simpler and fine for server-side applications where you control the environment. Use either method only from your own server, never in browser or mobile app code. See Authentication for details.

Yes. Every account has a concurrency limit that controls how many tasks can run at the same time. The limit scales automatically based on your account balance. See Concurrency Limits for the full table.

No. If a task fails (non-zero pexit), you are not charged. Only successfully completed tasks are billed.

Use the POST /Tool/Detail endpoint. The response includes the model's pricing information. If you're using the MCP server, the search_models and get_model_schema tools also return pricing.

Output files are stored on Wiro's CDN and available for a limited time. Download and store any files you need to keep long-term. See Files for details on file management.

Yes. Output URLs returned by Wiro are publicly accessible. Anyone with the URL can access the file. If you need private storage, download the files to your own infrastructure.

Your account is closed right away and its API keys stop working. Its subscriptions stop renewing and end with their current billing period, without a refund. A renewal invoice that is still unpaid is cancelled. Its automatic top-ups stop. 30 days later, or later if something still needs it, such as an active subscription, we permanently delete its data, including your files, tasks, projects and API keys. Until then, write to support@wiro.ai if you want it restored. We keep records the law requires, such as payment and invoice records. See Data Deletion for details.

Connect to the WebSocket at wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1 and register with the socketaccesstoken from your run response. You'll receive events as the task progresses. For simpler integrations, you can poll the Task Detail endpoint.

LLM models return their response in two places: as merged text in debugoutput, and as a structured entry in the outputs array with contenttype: "raw" containing prompt, raw, and separate thinking and answer arrays. For streaming, each task_output WebSocket event carries the latest cumulative snapshot of the output. See LLM & Chat Streaming for details.

Yes. For fileinput parameters, use the {id}Url suffix (e.g., inputImageUrl). For multifileinput, send comma-separated URLs in the field that puts Url before Multiple (e.g., inputDocumentUrlMultiple). For combinefileinput, pass URLs directly in the original parameter. A fileinput or multifileinput with no URL field takes them in the parameter itself. The URL must be a public http(s) address. See Model Parameters.

pexit is the process exit code: "0" means success, any other value means failure. It's the most reliable way to determine if a task succeeded. Always check pexit in the task_postprocess_end event or Task Detail response. See Tasks.

No. The Wiro MCP server is free. You pay the normal prices for the work its tools start: model runs, the model steps of workflow runs, Studio and Workflow Agent turns, and agent plans and the AI usage agents pay from the balance.

Yes. Install the Wiro AI community node (@wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro) in your n8n instance to run any Wiro model from your workflows. Pick the model in the node and its inputs load with their defaults. The node is verified by n8n, so an instance owner can also install it from the nodes panel, on n8n Cloud too.

Wiro AI has open-source add-ons for these apps. Each repository has the install steps:

  • ComfyUI: nodes that run image, video, audio, 3D and LLM models inside your graphs, also on the Comfy Registry
  • Dify: the LLM gateway and voice models as a model provider, plus tools for images, video, speech, music and 3D in workflows and agents
  • WordPress: featured images, image edits, alt text, narration and SEO suggestions in the block editor, from the WordPress plugin directory
  • Obsidian: images, video, speech, music, transcription and text tools, saved into your notes, from Obsidian community plugins
  • Figma: images, SVG vectors, image edits, background removal and text rewriting or translation on the canvas
  • Blender: text to 3D, image to 3D and textures, with any model in the catalog
  • Raycast: image and video generation, LLM chat and model search from your launcher
  • Zed: the Wiro MCP server in Zed's Agent Panel
  • GitHub Actions: run models, workflows and LLM prompts from a workflow step
  • Hermes Agent: media tools, plus the LLM gateway as a model provider
  • Coding agents: agent skills for images, image edits, video, music, speech, transcripts, 3D and model search in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and OpenClaw
  • Vercel AI SDK: chat, image, speech, transcription and video models, with a Next.js starter for Vercel and Railway
  • Chrome, Edge, Opera and Brave, Firefox and Safari: right-click an image, video, audio clip, text or page to run a model. Install it from the Chrome Web Store, Microsoft Edge Add-ons, Firefox Add-ons or the Naver Whale Store

AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code connect through the Wiro MCP server.

Yes. All models support an optional callbackUrl parameter. When provided, Wiro will POST the task result to your URL when the task completes. It must be a public http(s) address. See Webhook Callback in Model Parameters.

Wiro Agents are autonomous AI assistants that you deploy and manage via the API. Unlike single model runs, agents can connect to third-party services (Twitter, Google Ads, HubSpot, etc.), maintain conversation memory across sessions, and run scheduled tasks automatically. See the Agent Overview for details.

Pick a template in the agent catalog or build your own, then call POST /UserAgent/Deploy with useprepaid: true and a plan in tier: starter ($5 a month), pro ($30) or max ($100), each including its own price in AI usage a month. Your Wiro balance pays the plan, and Wiro queues the agent to start on its own. Then connect the services it uses. Every plan includes every skill and connector. See Agent Overview for the full lifecycle.

Each agent runs on one of three monthly plans: Starter ($5 a month), Pro ($30) or Max ($100), each paid from your Wiro balance and including its own price in AI usage: Pro includes $30 of AI usage a month. Every plan includes every skill and connector, so turning one on or off costs nothing. Each turn the agent runs is priced by the tokens its model uses; once the included usage is used up, the agent uses your Wiro balance, the same balance model runs use, and a new turn needs at least $0.50 there. A higher plan starts at once; a lower plan starts at the next renewal. See Pricing Model.

Starter gives an agent 250 MB, Pro 500 MB and Max 1 GB for its files: the workspace, generated media and temporary files. Chat history and system files don't count. Downloads and temporary files outside the workspace are cleared when the agent restarts, and when they pass 1 GB. When the disk is full, the agent can't save new files until some are deleted or it moves to a bigger plan. UserAgent/Detail shows the usage in disk. See Disk Space.

Yes. Use the Agent Messaging API to send messages programmatically, receive streaming responses via WebSocket, and get async notifications via webhooks. You can build white-label chat interfaces, webhook-driven pipelines, and multi-agent workflows. See Agent Use Cases. For a chat in your own product, with setup from chat, follow Agent Chat Integration.

Yes. In the Wiro panel, the people who manage an agent can open its Screen beside the chat and watch its computer live (on a team agent, while its Chat Mode is Collaborative). The owner of a personal agent that has never been in a team, or whose browser was reset after it last left one, can also take control and use the keyboard and mouse, for example to sign in to a site for the agent. Products built on the API can show the same Screen, and Take Control, in their own app and decide which of their users see it; the agent's screen setting turns it off for everyone. See Screen and Take Control and Screen and Take Control in Your App.

Agents connect to services like X, Instagram, Google Ads, and HubSpot through connectors, with your customer's own API keys or the vendor's sign-in. Browse them with POST /AgentConnector/List and connect one with POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect. See Agent Connectors. You can also ask the agent in its chat: it proposes a setup card, and an agent admin approves it and gives the key, which the agent never sees. See Setup From Chat.

Wiro MCP Server

Connect AI assistants to Wiro's models, workflows, Studio and agents through the Model Context Protocol.

Easiest way

Connect with a browser sign-in

No API key to copy. Add this URL as a remote MCP server in your app, then sign in with your Wiro account when the app asks:

https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1
  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Claude Code
  • Cursor
  • VS Code
  • Gemini CLI
  • Codex
  • Devin
  • Kiro
  • goose
  • Grok
  1. Add the serverIn your app, add a remote MCP server with the URL above. Leave the Authorization header out.
  2. Sign in to WiroThe app opens wiro.ai in your browser. Sign in, or create an account.
  3. Pick a project and how longRuns are paid from the project's workspace wallet. The app stays connected for 90 days unless you pick another length, from 7 days to unlimited.
  4. Click AllowYour browser goes back to the app, and the Wiro tools are ready to use.
Add to Cursor Install in VS Code Add to Kiro Add to goose

Claude, ChatGPT and Devin have no one-click link yet. Open the app's connector settings and paste the URL above:

Claude connectors ChatGPT plugins Devin MCP settings

What is MCP?

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants use external tools directly. With the Wiro MCP server, your AI assistant can find and run models, build and run workflows, create media with Studio, deploy and talk to your own agents, and check or change your spend limits and Model Access rules, all without leaving your editor or chat app.

The hosted MCP server is available at mcp.wiro.ai/v1. Most apps connect with the browser sign-in above. Clients that send custom request headers, including Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Kiro, goose, OpenClaw, and Hermes, can use your API key instead. An API key sent in a header is never stored on the hosted server.

You need a Wiro account. With a browser sign-in you pick a project while connecting. For the API key method, create a project here.

Links

  • Model Context Protocol (MCP): open standard specification
  • GitHub: wiroai/Wiro-MCP (source code & self-hosting instructions)
  • npm: @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp (npm package)
  • Wiro Model Catalog: browse all available models
  • Create API Key: get started in seconds

Browser sign-in details

ChatGPT, Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code), Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Zed, Devin, Kiro, goose, Grok, Grok Bot, Cline and MCP Inspector connect this way, and so does any app on your computer that follows the MCP authorization spec. An app that signs in through its own website needs its callback address on Wiro's list: write to support@wiro.ai to add one.

Projects and billing

  • Each connection uses one project. A personal project bills your personal wallet, a team project the team's wallet.
  • In a team, members can connect the projects they created. Team admins and the organization owner can connect any project of the team.
  • The connection acts as the person who created the project. Its Controls tools change spend limits and Model Access rules only when that person can: a personal account's owner, or in a team a team admin or the organization owner.
  • A project with an IP whitelist only accepts calls from the addresses on it. ChatGPT and Claude call from their own servers, so pick a project open to all addresses for them. Apps on your computer, such as Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code, call from your own address.

How long it stays connected

You pick it on the sign-in page: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days (the default), 180 days, 1 year, or unlimited. When the time is up, the app asks you to sign in again. An unlimited connection lasts until you disconnect it.

A connection also ends when its project is removed, or when you leave the team or lose the role that allowed it. The same happens once the project's API key stops working, for example when the person who created a team project leaves the team; the sign-in page then no longer offers that project. Access tokens last one hour and renew on their own, so there is nothing to copy or rotate.

See, change and disconnect apps

Every app you connected is listed under Projects, Connected Apps in the panel, with its project, when it was last used and when it ends. Pick a new length there to extend or shorten it; it counts from that day. Disconnect ends its access within a minute, and the app asks you to sign in again the next time.

For MCP client developers

Item Value
Protected resource metadata https://mcp.wiro.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1
Authorization server metadata https://mcp.wiro.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
Authorize, token, revoke https://mcp.wiro.ai/authorize, /token, /revoke
Client registration A Client ID Metadata Document, or dynamic client registration at https://mcp.wiro.ai/register
Resource and scope https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1, scope mcp

Use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256). Authorization responses carry iss. Sign-in returns only to the callbacks of known apps and to loopback addresses on your own computer (any port). To add your app's callback, write to support@wiro.ai.

Setup

Connect your AI assistant to Wiro's MCP server. Pick your client:

Cursor Sign in or JSON config Claude Code Sign in, plugin or command Claude Desktop Connector or local npx ChatGPT Connector with sign-in VS Code One-click install Gemini CLI Extension install Codex Sign in, plugin or command Devin Plugin install Kiro One-click install goose One-click install Grok Custom connector Windsurf MCP settings config OpenClaw Streamable HTTP config Hermes YAML config Other Clients Any MCP-compatible tool

Cursor

Sign in with your browser

Click Add to Cursor, or add the server to your mcp.json with only its URL:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1"
    }
  }
}

Cursor asks you to sign in to Wiro the first time it connects.

Or use your API key

  1. Open MCP Settings: Use Cmd+Shift+P (Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows) and search for "Open MCP settings".
  2. Add the Wiro server to your mcp.json file:

    Signature Auth (if your project uses signature-based authentication):

    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET"
      }
    }
  }
}

    API Key Only Auth (if your project uses API Key Only authentication):

    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
  3. Restart Cursor: Save the file and restart Cursor to activate the connection.

Claude Code

Sign in with your browser

Run this command in your terminal:

claude mcp add --transport http wiro https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1

Then run /mcp inside Claude Code, pick wiro and sign in to Wiro in your browser.

Or install as a plugin

Run these two commands inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add wiroai/Wiro-Plugin
/plugin install wiro-ai@wiro

Then open /mcp, pick the Wiro server and choose Authenticate to sign in to Wiro in your browser. The plugin comes from the wiroai/Wiro-Plugin repository.

The plugin also adds slash commands, such as /wiro-ai:image, /wiro-ai:video and /wiro-ai:speech, and five agent skills. Each command picks a model from the catalog, shows the price and waits for your yes before a paid run and can save the results into your project.

Or add the server with your API key

Run this command in your terminal:

claude mcp add --transport http wiro \
  https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1 \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET"

For an API Key Only project, use Bearer YOUR_API_KEY without the colon or secret. Verify the connection with claude mcp get wiro, or run /mcp inside Claude Code.

Claude Desktop

The quickest way is a custom connector: open Connectors in Claude, click Add custom connector, enter the URL https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1 and sign in with your Wiro account when Claude asks. See Connect with a browser sign-in. The same connector works on claude.ai.

You can also run the official local package. It provides the same Wiro tools through Claude Desktop's stdio MCP support.

Install Node.js 20 or later, then add the following to your claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "YOUR_API_SECRET"
      }
    }
  }
}

For API Key Only authentication, keep WIRO_API_KEY and remove the WIRO_API_SECRET entry completely. Save the file, fully quit Claude Desktop, and reopen it.

Keep @latest in args: npx then looks up the newest version on npm each time the client starts the server. Without it, npx can keep running an older cached build after a package update.

This setup runs the open-source @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp bridge on your machine and calls Wiro with your project credentials. See Self-Hosted MCP for the complete local package guide.

Claude connection and timeout troubleshooting

  • "Not valid MCP server configurations": ensure the entry contains "type": "stdio", command, args, and env exactly as shown above.
  • The Wiro tools do not appear: confirm node --version reports 20 or later, then fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop.
  • Tools appear but every call fails immediately: use @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest as shown above so npx does not reuse an older cached package, then fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop.
  • A generation reaches Claude's tool timeout: Wiro waits for at most 45 seconds per call. If the task is still running, Claude should execute the returned nextAction.tool: "wait_for_task" until completion and must not call run_model again.
  • Do not add a timeout field to claude_desktop_config.json; Claude Desktop versions with a fixed client-side tool timeout may ignore it. Wiro's bounded wait flow is designed to remain below that boundary.

In ChatGPT, open Plugins, click +, choose Add custom MCP server, enter https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1 and create the plugin. ChatGPT opens wiro.ai, where you sign in and pick a project.

ChatGPT calls Wiro from its own servers, so pick a project that is open to all IP addresses.
