goose

Sign in with your browser

Click Add to goose. To add it by hand in goose Desktop, open Extensions > Add custom extension, choose the Streamable HTTP type and enter https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1. In the goose CLI, run goose configure, pick Add Extension > Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP) and enter the same URL.

goose opens Wiro's sign-in page in your browser the first time it connects.

Or use your API key

Add Wiro to ~/.config/goose/config.yaml with an Authorization header:

extensions:
  wiro:
    name: Wiro AI
    type: streamable_http
    uri: https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

Use YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET (both values joined with a colon) if the project uses signature-based auth.

Grok

On grok.com

Open grok.com/connectors, click New Connector, choose Custom and enter https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1. Grok opens Wiro's sign-in page in your browser: sign in, pick the project whose wallet pays for runs and click Allow.

In Grok Bot

Ask your Bot to add the MCP server https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1. Grok Bot opens Wiro's sign-in page in your browser the first time it connects.

Windsurf

Open Settings → MCP and add a new server:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET"
      }
    }
  }
}

OpenClaw

Set WIRO_MCP_AUTH in the environment that starts OpenClaw. Use YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET for signature auth or only YOUR_API_KEY for API Key Only auth. Then add this server under mcp.servers in your OpenClaw config:

{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "wiro": {
        "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
        "transport": "streamable-http",
        "connectionTimeoutMs": 10000,
        "headers": {
          "Authorization": "Bearer ${WIRO_MCP_AUTH}"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Verify the saved definition, the connection and the advertised tools:

openclaw mcp doctor wiro --probe

On older OpenClaw releases without that command, use openclaw mcp show wiro, restart OpenClaw, and run /tools verbose.

Wiro's default bounded wait is 45 seconds; if your client has a configurable tool-call timeout, keep it above that value.

Hermes

Add WIRO_MCP_AUTH=YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET to ~/.hermes/.env, then add this to ~/.hermes/config.yaml:

mcp_servers:
  wiro:
    url: "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${WIRO_MCP_AUTH}"
    timeout: 60
    connect_timeout: 10

Use only the API key in WIRO_MCP_AUTH for API Key Only auth. Run /reload-mcp and then /tools inside Hermes.

Other MCP Clients

The Wiro MCP server uses the Streamable HTTP transport at:

https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1

A client that supports MCP sign-in needs only this URL: it opens a Wiro sign-in in your browser (see Connect with a browser sign-in). Any other client sends your API key in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET

Or for API Key Only auth: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Credentials are sent as plain text. No base64 encoding is needed. Clients must support Streamable HTTP, and for the header method a custom Authorization header.

Authentication

Apps that support MCP sign-in need no credentials here: see Connect with a browser sign-in. With an API key in the header, the MCP server supports both Wiro authentication types. Your project's auth type determines what credentials you provide.

Signature-Based (Recommended)

More secure. Requires both API key and API secret. Pass them as plain text separated by a colon:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET

API Key Only

Simpler. Only requires the API key:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

No base64 encoding needed. Credentials are sent per-request and are never stored. The server is fully stateless.

Authentication errors

A failed tool call comes back as a normal tool result with isError: true. Its text starts with Wiro API error and the HTTP status, then a message that says what to fix. For example, when a project uses signature-based auth and only its API key was sent:

{
  "isError": true,
  "content": [{
    "type": "text",
    "text": "## Error\n\nWiro API error 401: This project uses signature-based auth. Enter API_KEY:API_SECRET (the key and secret joined with a colon) as the API key."
  }]
}

Messages you may see while connecting:

Message What to do
This project uses signature-based auth. Enter API_KEY:API_SECRET (the key and secret joined with a colon) as the API key. Only the API key was sent, but the project uses signature-based auth. Enter API_KEY:API_SECRET in the plugin's key field, or send Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY:YOUR_API_SECRET.
Project authorization is not founded. No project has this API key. Copy the key again from your project page.
Project authorization is not valid. The API secret does not match the API key. Check that both come from the same project.
Requested ip {ip} is not allowed. The project has an IP whitelist, and the address in the message is not on it. Check the whitelist in your project settings.
The person who created this API key is no longer in its team. Ask a team admin for a new key. The user who created this team project has left the team, so its key no longer works. Use a key from another project, or sign in again and pick another project.

A request without an Authorization header never reaches a tool. The MCP endpoint answers HTTP 401 with Missing or invalid Authorization header in the body and a WWW-Authenticate header that points apps to the sign-in. An expired or disconnected sign-in gets the same answer with error="invalid_token", and the app asks you to sign in again. See Error Reference for every Wiro API error.

Available Tools

The MCP server has 56 tools. Most of them belong to one of four groups, Models, Workflows, Agents and Controls, and three tools for your account, the playbooks and the docs are always available. Your AI assistant picks the right tool for each request, and for longer jobs it reads a playbook first.

Model slugs: Use the clean/lowercase format owner/model (e.g. openai/sora-2, wiro/virtual-try-on). These correspond to the cleanslugowner/cleanslugproject values returned by search_models.

Models

Tool Description
search_models Search and browse AI models by keyword, category, or owner
get_model_schema Get the full parameter schema and pricing for any model, or the parameters and output ports of a workflow utility
recommend_model Find models for a goal from two or three key words, best matches first
explore Browse curated models grouped by category, no parameters needed
run_model Run any model, waiting up to 45 seconds by default before it returns a recoverable task token
wait_for_task Continue waiting for an existing task without submitting or billing a duplicate run
get_task Check task status immediately or wait up to 45 seconds with wait_seconds
list_tasks Browse authenticated task history across conversations, then continue with get_task
get_task_price Get the cost of a completed task
cancel_task Cancel a queued task
kill_task Stop a queued or running task
upload_file Upload a file from a public http(s) URL (up to about 100 MB) for use as model input

For long generations, run_model returns the existing task ID and token when its wait ends. The assistant continues with wait_for_task; calling run_model again would start a separate billable task.

Workflows

A workflow chains models and built-in utility steps into one graph with its own inputs and outputs. Every model step is charged like a normal model run when it finishes. Wiro fills a model input you leave out with the model's default, so the save result lists what it filled, and a graph can be at most 40 KB of JSON. The API behind these tools is described on the Workflows page.

Tool Description
list_workflows List the workflows in your workspace, or search the public gallery by text, tag or model
get_workflow Read a workflow's inputs, outputs and step graph
create_workflow Save a new workflow from a step graph. Wiro checks it against the live model catalog and returns every problem it finds at once
update_workflow Edit a workflow's title, description, tags or graph without overwriting newer changes; a new graph is saved only after you confirm a summary of the change
clone_workflow Copy a public workflow into your workspace
delete_workflow Delete a workflow, after your confirmation
run_workflow Run a workflow and wait for its outputs; can stop after a chosen step to test the first steps
wait_for_workflow_run Keep waiting on a run, read its outputs, or see why a step failed
resume_workflow_run Continue a failed or stopped run without paying again for finished steps
list_workflow_runs Browse past and current runs, including runs started on wiro.ai
save_workflow_from_agent Save a workflow the Workflow Agent proposed, as a new workflow, or onto an existing one after you confirm a summary of the change

The Workflow Agent designs workflows with you in plain language: talk to it with send_agent_message and agent: "workflow-agent", attach an existing workflow to edit, then save its proposal with save_workflow_from_agent. Conversations started through the MCP server belong to the connected project and are separate from your Workflow Agent chats on wiro.ai. See Workflow Agent.

Agents

One set of tools talks to every Wiro agent. agent is "studio", "workflow-agent" or the guid of one of your own agents. Session names use letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores and colons, up to 128 characters (100 for the Workflow Agent), and can't end in -r followed by a number, such as -r2. Studio refuses a message under any other name, and nothing is sent. A Studio session that already has another name can still be read and deleted; to go on with it, start a new session.

Tool Description
send_agent_message Send a message and wait for the reply, with any media, workflows or model runs it produced
get_agent_message Keep waiting on a reply, or read one again
get_agent_conversation List conversations, or read one conversation's history
cancel_agent_message Stop a reply that is still being written
delete_agent_session Delete a conversation and the agent's memory of it, after your confirmation
list_studio_results List the images, videos and other results Studio generated for you

Studio is Wiro's creative agent: it picks and runs models for you and charges your wallet after each reply (see Studio). Your own agents run on a monthly plan that includes AI usage, then on your Wiro balance (see Agent Overview).

Tool Description
list_agent_templates Browse ready-made agent templates and the three monthly plans
get_agent_template Read a template's skills, plans, the connectors it suggests and the keys it needs
list_agent_connectors Browse the connectors an agent can connect (ad accounts, stores, social accounts, mailboxes, data sources), what each one needs and the tools it gives the agent; with an agent, its connections
list_agent_skills Browse the skills an agent can have, and what each one needs to work
deploy_agent Deploy an agent from a template or build one from skills, on the Starter, Pro or Max plan; shows the plan's price and the AI usage it includes, the Wiro balance that pays it and the other plans' prices, and asks before charging
list_my_agents List your agents with their status, plan, AI usage and this month's spending
get_my_agent Read one agent's setup, plan, AI usage and the balance it runs on; can wait until it is running
control_agent Start, stop or restart an agent
update_agent Change an agent's name, description, time zone, models, chat commands and setup from chat
apply_agent_skills Turn skills on or off; every plan includes every skill, so a change costs nothing
set_agent_credentials Save an agent's chat channel keys (such as a Telegram bot token), Twilio Voice and settings
connect_agent_connector Connect a connector to an agent: save its keys, or start its sign-in, which you approve in your browser. A connector that runs with a Wiro project shows the project and its wallet first
set_agent_connector_accounts Choose the accounts a connected connector may act on, such as its ad accounts, pages or channels
disconnect_agent_connector Disconnect a connector from an agent, after your confirmation
list_projects List the projects of the connected project's workspace, to pick one for an agent; no keys are shown
bind_agent_project Connect an agent to a Wiro project so it can run models, with no key in the chat; shows the project first, then asks for your confirmation
manage_agent_custom_skill Add, edit, schedule, restore or remove an agent's own instructions and scheduled tasks; turning off its approval policy or changing its rules needs your confirmation
manage_agent_billing Subscribe, move to another plan, cancel or renew, paid from your Wiro balance, after your confirmation; buy_credits is retired and charges nothing
get_agent_activity Read an agent's AI usage, its transactions in dollars and its activity logs, including who changed what on it
delete_agent Delete an agent, after your confirmation

Setup changes from chat. A reply from one of your agents can propose a change to its own setup, such as connecting a connector, adding a skill, or creating a scheduled task (see Setup From Chat). The assistant shows you the proposal and never approves it on its own. When you agree, it sends your yes as the next message: Wiro answers the first yes with the exact change, and your next yes (or yes 2 for the second of several changes) applies it. Keys never go in a chat message: the assistant connects a connector with connect_agent_connector, and saves a channel's key with set_agent_credentials. This works while the agent's setup from chat is all, the default, which deploy_agent and update_agent set with chat_setup. With webchat, apply the change in the agent's chat on wiro.ai; with off, the agent asks for it on the agent page.

Controls

These tools read and change the workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules. Reading them is free. They change limits and rules only when the person who created the connected project can change them: a personal account's owner, or in a team a team admin or the organization owner. Other members' connections can read them.

Tool Description
get_controls Read the workspace's spend limits, with what each has used and when it resets, its Model Access rules, and whether this connection can change them; on request, also this month's or today's spending by surface, member, API key and agent
check_model_access Explain whether a model may run here and why, rule by rule. Nothing runs and nothing is charged
manage_spend_limit Set or remove a spend limit, after your confirmation
manage_model_access Update, replace or remove a Model Access rule, after your confirmation

The two manage tools always show a change summary first: what the change covers, the old and new values and, for a limit, what was spent this period. Nothing changes until you confirm. If the limit or rule changed in the meantime, nothing is saved and you get a new summary.

Account and guides

These three tools are always available, whichever groups are loaded.

Tool Description
get_account Show which workspace the connected project belongs to, its wallet balance, its spend limits and, when you ask, the wallet's recent transactions
get_playbook Step-by-step guides: getting started, models, workflows, workflow graphs, the Workflow Agent, Studio, agents, billing and Controls
search_docs Search the Wiro documentation for guides and API references

Playbooks

A tool description is too short to carry the order of calls, the money rules and the formats of a multi-step job, so the server keeps them in playbooks. The server tells the assistant to read the matching playbook with get_playbook before a multi-step job.

Topic What it covers
getting-started Which route fits a request, what costs money, keys and workspaces, errors, long waits and the money rules
models Finding and comparing models, schemas and file fields, running, batches, waiting and stopping, prices and limits, earlier tasks and LLM chats
workflows Finding and running workflows, costs, breakpoints, failed runs, editing, cloning and deleting
workflow-graph The graph create_workflow and update_workflow take: steps, Start fields, references, utilities and examples
workflow-agent Briefing the Workflow Agent, editing a workflow by chat, pricing and saving its proposals, sessions
studio When to use Studio, what a turn costs, the brief, collecting the results and slow turns
agents Templates and plans, deploying, statuses, setup and sign-ins, an agent that does not answer, messages, plan changes, AI usage and the balance, skills and schedules, removal
billing Which wallet pays, what is charged and when, minimums and limits, teams, estimates and where to see past spending
controls Spend limits and Model Access: who can change them, scopes and surfaces, periods, how rules combine, recipes, and the refusals with codes 92 and 93

Prompts

The server also offers prompts for common jobs. Clients that support MCP prompts show them as ready-made commands. Each prompt sends the assistant to the matching playbook first.

Prompt What it does
build_workflow Plan, save and test a multi-step workflow for a goal, confirming costs before any run
deploy_agent Choose a template or skills, quote and deploy an agent, then set it up and test it
create_with_studio Ask Studio to create images, video or audio, after showing what a turn can cost and getting your yes
talk_to_my_agent Find one of your agents, make sure it is running, send it a message and show the reply

Paid and irreversible actions

Running a model or a workflow, sending a message to Studio or the Workflow Agent, and messages to your own agents (which use the AI usage the agent's plan includes, then your Wiro balance) cost money. Before a run or a Studio or Workflow Agent turn, the assistant tells you the expected cost in one line and waits for your yes. A message to your own agent goes out once the assistant has said that it uses the agent's AI usage.

Agent plans and moves to a larger plan are paid from your Wiro balance, so deploy_agent and manage_agent_billing first return the price (for a move inside a billing period, the amount Wiro works out for the time left). They act only when they are called again with confirm: true and confirm_charge_usd, the approved amount, after you agree. If the price changed in between, nothing is charged and you get a new quote. Turning an agent's skills on or off with apply_agent_skills costs nothing, and so does connecting its connectors, since every plan includes every skill and connector, and a move to a smaller plan starts with the next renewal, with nothing charged or refunded. When the balance can't pay a plan, the quote says how much to add on wiro.ai and nothing is charged. buy_credits is retired and charges nothing: past its plan's included usage, an agent uses the Wiro balance.

Deleting a workflow, an agent, a conversation or a connector connection also waits for confirm: true, and so do replacing a working connector connection, connecting an agent or a connector to a Wiro project with bind_agent_project or connect_agent_connector, and replacing a workflow's steps with update_workflow or save_workflow_from_agent: you see a summary of the change first, with the old and new value of each step input that changes. Changing a spend limit or a Model Access rule with manage_spend_limit or manage_model_access also waits for confirm: true: you see the old and new values first and, for a limit, what was spent this period. No tool adds funds or takes a card payment: funds are added in the Wiro dashboard.

The connected project decides the workspace: a personal project uses your personal wallet, a team project uses the team wallet. get_account shows which one, its balance and its spend limits, and get_controls its spend limits and Model Access rules in full.

Calls through the hosted MCP server count toward the workspace's spend limits on the mcp surface, and calls from the Wiro browser extensions on the extension surface. The self-hosted package's calls count on the api surface for now, as calls with its API key. Messages to Studio and the Workflow Agent count on the studio and workflow-agent surfaces, and workflow runs on workflow, whichever way they are sent (see Surfaces). When a limit refuses work (error code 93), the tool returns an error with Wiro's message and a note: nothing ran and nothing was charged, and the work should not be tried again until the limit resets or someone who manages it raises it. get_controls shows the limit and when it resets, and manage_spend_limit changes it after a change summary. Limits are also managed under Controls > Spend Limits.

The workspace's Model Access rules apply to these calls too, on the same surfaces. A model a rule blocks is refused before anything runs (error code 92), and the tool returns an error with Wiro's message, which names the rule. A message to Studio or the Workflow Agent is refused the same way when a rule blocks its chat model, the one it names or the default. Nothing ran and nothing was charged. check_model_access shows why the model is blocked, and manage_model_access changes the rule after a change summary. Rules are also managed under Controls > Model Access.

MCP Request and Response Contract

Every tool advertises typed MCP inputSchema and outputSchema values. Successful calls return structuredContent for reliable LLM tool chaining, concise text content for compatibility, and MCP resource links for generated media.

Every tool that takes arguments refuses an argument it does not know, and nothing is run. The answer lists the arguments the tool takes and names the right one where it can, such as taskid for task_id; run_model adds that model parameters go inside params, and run_workflow that input values go inside input. The one exception is a call that carries toolCallId, a key some clients add on their own: the tool then reads only the arguments it takes.

When a task completes with media, Wiro also returns an assistant-audience delivery instruction. MCP clients do not all preview resource_link blocks inside tool cards, so the assistant is explicitly told to render image URLs and preserve clickable video, audio, and file links in its user-facing response. The standard resource link and full-resolution URL remain available without embedding a large base64 payload.

In the text of a result, an agent's reply, the file and link addresses taken from it and a model's answer sit in fenced blocks under fixed labels. The server's own guidance, its Next: lines and notes, stays outside them, so the assistant can treat that text as content and act only on the guidance and nextAction. A workflow run's text outputs and step errors show the same way. A saved workflow's title, description and input list are shown as data too, in every result, since an agent or another person can have written them. structuredContent keeps each text unchanged in its own field.

For example, an LLM submits one generation:

{
  "name": "run_model",
  "arguments": {
    "model": "owner/model",
    "params": { "prompt": "A mountain lake at sunset" },
    "wait": true,
    "timeout_seconds": 45
  }
}

If the generation outlives the bounded wait, the same tool returns the existing task and an executable next action:

{
  "state": "running",
  "task": {
    "id": "123",
    "token": "task-token",
    "status": "task_start"
  },
  "outputs": [],
  "nextAction": {
    "tool": "wait_for_task",
    "arguments": { "tasktoken": "task-token" },
    "reason": "Continue this exact task. Do not call run_model again."
  }
}

Task states are submitted, running, completed, failed, or cancelled. The LLM should execute nextAction when present. A two- or three-minute video can therefore use several bounded wait_for_task calls without creating another billable generation.

Workflow runs, agent replies and agent start-up follow the same pattern: when a wait ends before the job does, the result names the tool and arguments that keep waiting on that same job, such as wait_for_workflow_run or get_agent_message.

An LLM model can continue a chat only when its schema lists session_id. Send the same session_id on every turn, the first one included, with the next prompt. A turn that ended with tool calls is continued with previousTaskToken, that turn's task token, and toolOutputs, as the turn's nextAction template shows.

Examples

Generate an image

"Generate a photorealistic image of a mountain lake at golden hour"

The assistant will use search_models → get_model_schema → run_model and return the image URL.

Generate a video

"Create a 5-second cinematic video of a drone shot over mountains using Kling V3"

The assistant will use get_model_schema → run_model, then continue with wait_for_task using the returned token if the generation is still running.

Find models

"What models are available for text-to-video?"

The assistant will call search_models with categories filter.

Check task status

"Check the status of my last task"

The assistant will call get_task with the task token from the previous run.

Resume a previous production

"Show my latest productions and open the newest result"

The assistant will call list_tasks, select the matching task, and call get_task with its task ID. Task history covers the authenticated project's workspace, personal or team: model tasks from every project in it and from wiro.ai. Steps of workflow runs and the runs Studio starts are not listed: list_workflow_runs and list_studio_results have those. The LLM never sends a user UUID.

Build and run a workflow

"Build a workflow that turns a product photo into a short ad video, then run it on this photo"

The assistant reads the workflows and workflow-graph playbooks, picks a model for each step with search_models and get_model_schema, and saves the graph with create_workflow. It tells you the expected cost and waits for your yes, then calls run_workflow and follows wait_for_workflow_run until the video is ready.

Edit a workflow with the Workflow Agent

"Ask the Workflow Agent to add an upscale step to my product ad workflow and save it"

The assistant finds the workflow with list_workflows and sends your request with send_agent_message (agent: "workflow-agent") with the workflow attached. It shows you the proposal and the models it uses, and saves it with save_workflow_from_agent once you agree to the change.

Fix a failed run

"Why did my last workflow run fail? Resume it if it can be resumed"

The assistant calls list_workflow_runs with status failed, reads the failed step with wait_for_workflow_run, and continues the run with resume_workflow_run. Steps that already finished are not charged again.

Create with Studio

"Ask Studio for three logo ideas for a coffee shop"

The assistant checks the balance with get_account, tells you what a Studio turn costs, sends the brief with send_agent_message (agent: "studio") and shows the images from the reply.

Deploy an agent

"Deploy an agent that posts to our Instagram account and tell me what it still needs"

The assistant compares templates with list_agent_templates and get_agent_template, gets the price from deploy_agent, and deploys only after you confirm the amount. Then it lists the missing setup with get_my_agent and connects the Instagram connector with connect_agent_connector. If the agent runs Wiro models, it connects a Wiro project with bind_agent_project once you agree to the project it shows.

Talk to your agent

"Tell my support agent to summarise today's tickets"

The assistant finds the agent with list_my_agents, checks that it is running with get_my_agent, and sends the message with send_agent_message. The message uses the agent's AI usage. If the reply proposes a setup change, the assistant shows it and sends your yes only after you agree.

Cap your spending

"Cap this team's spending at $200 a month"

The assistant calls manage_spend_limit to set a $200 monthly limit on the whole team (scope: "account"). Nothing changes yet: it shows you the change summary, with what was already spent this month, and saves the limit with confirm: true once you agree.

Find out why a model is blocked

"Why can't I run this video model here?"

The assistant calls check_model_access with the model and shows each rule that applies and the one that blocks it. It changes a rule with manage_model_access only when you ask, after you agree to the change summary.

How It Works

The MCP server is stateless. Each request is fully isolated:

  1. Your AI assistant sends a request to mcp.wiro.ai/v1 with your credentials
  2. The server calls the Wiro API on your behalf
  3. Results are returned to your assistant

All tools are dynamic: they fetch model data at runtime. New models are instantly available via MCP.

Tool Reference

The model tools are described one by one below. The workflow, conversation, agent and Controls tools follow in tables of their main arguments.

search_models

Search Wiro's model catalog by keyword, category, owner, or any combination. Calls POST /Tool/List on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
search string (optional) Free-text search, e.g. "flux", "video generation"
categories string[] (optional) Filter by category: text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, llm, text-to-speech, image-editing, etc.
slugowner string (optional) Filter by model owner slug, e.g. "openai", "google", "klingai"
sort string (optional) Sort by: relevance, time, ratedusercount, commentcount, averagepoint
start number (optional) Pagination offset (default 0)
limit number (optional) Max results (default 20, max 100)

Returns a list of models with their cleanslugowner/cleanslugproject (the slug you pass to other tools), title, description, categories, and pricing.

get_model_schema

Get the full parameter schema for a specific model. Calls POST /Tool/Detail on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
model string Model slug using clean/lowercase format: "owner/model". Use cleanslugowner/cleanslugproject from search_models. Examples: "openai/sora-2", "black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro", "wiro/virtual-try-on"

Returns the model's parameter groups, each containing items with id, type (text, textarea, select, range, fileinput, etc.), label, required, options, default, and note. Also includes pricing information. Use these to construct the params object for run_model.

recommend_model

Describe what you want to create and get model recommendations ranked by relevance. Calls POST /Tool/List on the Wiro API with relevance sorting.

Parameter Type Description
task string What you want to do, e.g. "generate a photorealistic portrait", "upscale an image to 4K", "transcribe audio to text"

Returns a list of recommended models with slugs, descriptions, categories, and pricing, sorted by relevance to your task.

explore

Browse curated AI models on Wiro, organized by category. Calls POST /Tool/Explore on the Wiro API. No parameters required.

Returns models grouped into curated sections like "Recently Added", "Image Generation", "Video", etc. Each model includes its slug, description, categories, and rating. Use this to discover what's available without searching.

run_model

Run any AI model on Wiro. Calls POST /Run/{owner}/{model} on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
model string Model slug in clean/lowercase format. Same as get_model_schema. Examples: "openai/sora-2", "klingai/kling-v3"
params object Model-specific parameters as key-value pairs. Use get_model_schema to discover accepted fields. Common: prompt, negativePrompt, width, height, aspectRatio
wait boolean (optional) If true (default), polls POST /Task/Detail until the task completes or the wait budget expires. If false, returns the task token immediately for wait_for_task or one-time get_task checks.
timeout_seconds number (optional) Max seconds to wait, counted from the start of the call (default 45, max 3600). Only applies when wait=true. The default suits clients with a 60-second tool timeout; wait longer, such as 300 seconds for a video, when the client allows longer tool calls.

When wait=true, returns the final task result including pexit (exit code, "0" = success), clickable outputs, and debugoutput (LLM text responses).

If the wait budget expires, the tool returns a normal Task Still Running result with taskid, tasktoken, and the last status. The generation continues. Call wait_for_task; do not call run_model again, because that creates a second billable task.

When wait=false, returns taskid and tasktoken immediately. Use wait_for_task to wait or get_task for a one-time status check.

wait_for_task

Wait for an existing task without submitting another model run. Calls POST /Task/Detail repeatedly for a bounded interval.

Parameter Type Description
tasktoken string (optional) The task token returned from run_model
taskid string (optional) The task ID (alternative to tasktoken)
timeout_seconds number (optional) Max seconds for this wait window (default 45, max 3600)

If the task completes, this tool returns the final text and file outputs. If it is still active, call wait_for_task again with the same identifier. This does not create or bill another model run.

get_task

Check task status and get results. It performs one immediate check by default, or a short bounded wait when wait_seconds is set. Calls POST /Task/Detail on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
tasktoken string (optional) The task token returned from run_model
taskid string (optional) The task ID (alternative to tasktoken)
wait_seconds number (optional) Short bounded wait before returning (default 0, max 45). Use wait_for_task for resumable long generations.

Returns the task's current status, pexit (process exit code), outputs (file URLs), debugoutput (LLM responses), elapsedseconds, and totalcost.

Determining success: Check pexit, where "0" means success and any other value means failure. For LLM models, the response is available as structured content in outputs (with contenttype: "raw") and as merged text in debugoutput. See Tasks for the full task lifecycle.

A live WebSocket task_error event is an interim stderr log, while persisted status: "task_error" returned by Task/Detail marks a pre-execution recovery state. Neither closes the task; wait_for_task continues until task_postprocess_end or task_cancel.

list_tasks

List recent model-generation tasks in the authenticated project's workspace (personal or team), from every project in it and from wiro.ai. Steps of workflow runs and the runs Studio starts are not listed: list_workflow_runs and list_studio_results have those. Calls POST /Task/List without a uuid; Wiro derives the workspace from the API credential.

Parameter Type Description
start number (optional) Pagination offset (default 0)
limit number (optional) Maximum tasks to return (default 20, max 100)
model string (optional) Model slug or partial model-name filter

Returns newest-first task summaries with stable state, model, task ID, timestamps, duration, cost, and limited output links. Call get_task with a returned taskid for the complete result.

get_task_price

Get the cost of a completed task. Calls POST /Task/Detail on the Wiro API and returns billing information.

Parameter Type Description
tasktoken string (optional) The task token returned from run_model
taskid string (optional) The task ID (alternative to tasktoken)

Returns the task's billing status, total cost, and duration. Only successful tasks (pexit: "0") are billed. Failed tasks show $0 with a clear explanation that they were not charged.

cancel_task

Cancel a task that is still queued (before worker assignment). Calls POST /Task/Cancel on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
tasktoken string (optional) The task token returned from run_model
taskid string (optional) The task ID (alternative to tasktoken)

Tasks that have already been assigned to a worker cannot be cancelled. Use kill_task instead.

kill_task

Kill a task that is currently running (after worker assignment). Calls POST /Task/Kill on the Wiro API.

Parameter Type Description
tasktoken string (optional) The task token returned from run_model
taskid string (optional) The task ID (alternative to tasktoken)

The worker will stop processing and the task will move to task_cancel status.

upload_file

Upload a file from a URL to Wiro for use as model input. Downloads the file and uploads it via POST /File/Upload.

Tip: Most models take a public URL instead of an upload, so you don't need to upload first: in the field itself for a combinefileinput (e.g. inputImage on most image models), or in the {id}Url / UrlMultiple field for a fileinput or multifileinput (e.g. inputImageUrl). get_model_schema shows each parameter's type. Use upload_file when you need to reuse the same file across multiple runs or when the model specifically requires a Wiro-hosted file. See Model Parameters for details.

Parameter Type Description
url string URL of the file to upload (image, audio, video, document)
file_name string (optional) Custom filename. If not provided, derived from the URL.

Returns the uploaded file's Wiro URL, which can be passed to any model parameter that accepts a file.

search_docs

Search the Wiro documentation for guides, API references, and code examples.

Parameter Type Description
query string What you're looking for, e.g. "how to upload a file", "websocket", "authentication", "LLM streaming"

Returns relevant documentation sections matching your query.

get_account and get_playbook

get_account names the workspace of the connected project, personal or a team, and shows that wallet's balance. It is also the call that proves the connection works, since model search, schema reads and search_docs answer without credentials. Without arguments it reads the balance and the workspace's spend limits, each with what it has used this period and whether it is used up. A used-up limit refuses new work with error code 93 even when the wallet has money. With recent_transactions (1 to 50) it also lists that many of the wallet's latest transactions, newest first, as the Transactions page of the Wiro dashboard shows them: each row's time, type, whether it adds to the wallet or takes from it, the amount in USD and what it was for, such as a model run, a store item or an agent. That is how to check that a charge or a credit landed. In a team the wallet is shared, so the list holds the whole team's activity. transactions_start pages back: pass the nextStart of the last answer. get_playbook takes topics, one or more of the playbook topics listed under Available Tools, such as ["workflows"] or ["agents", "billing"].

Workflow tools

The workflow, conversation, agent and Controls tools publish their full input schemas, which your MCP client reads, so the tables below list only their main arguments. A workflow is named by its full slug, such as product-shots-a1B2c, and a run by its run token. The Workflows page describes the API behind these tools.

Tool Main arguments
list_workflows scope (mine or public), search, tags, model, sort, start, limit
get_workflow slug, include_graph
create_workflow title, contents (the graph), description, tags
update_workflow slug, loaded_updatetime, title, description, tags, contents, confirm
clone_workflow slug
delete_workflow slug, confirm
run_workflow slug, input (values keyed by the workflow's input names), breakpoint_node_id, wait_seconds
wait_for_workflow_run workflowtoken, wait_seconds, debug_node_id (shows what a step's model received)
resume_workflow_run workflowtoken, breakpoint_node_id, wait_seconds
list_workflow_runs status, search, start, limit
save_workflow_from_agent message_id, session, artifact_hash (which proposal), workflow and loaded_updatetime to save onto an existing workflow, confirm

Conversation tools

These tools work the same for Studio, the Workflow Agent and your own agents. agent is "studio", "workflow-agent" or the guid of one of your agents, and session names the conversation, following the session name rule under Available Tools. See Studio, Workflow Agent and Agent Messaging.

Tool Main arguments
send_agent_message agent, message, session, model (Studio and the Workflow Agent), attachment_urls, workflow (the workflow to edit, Workflow Agent only), wait_seconds
get_agent_message agent, message_id, session, wait_seconds
get_agent_conversation agent, session (leave it out to list the conversations, newest first), limit, before (older messages: pass nextBefore), start (older conversations: pass nextStart; a list longer than one page also returns total)
cancel_agent_message agent, message_id, session
delete_agent_session agent, session, confirm
list_studio_results limit (up to 100 recent runs), state, since

Agent tools

An agent is named by its guid, which list_my_agents returns. See Agent Overview, Agent Builder, Agent Connectors, Agent Credentials and Agent Skills for the API behind these tools.

Tool Main arguments
list_agent_templates search, category, sort (newest, popular or title), start, limit
get_agent_template template, include_tasks
list_agent_connectors name, search, category, agent_guid (its connections too)
list_agent_skills name, category, capability
deploy_agent template, or custom: true with skills; tier (starter, pro or max), title, credentials, chat_setup (all, webchat or off), confirm, confirm_charge_usd
list_my_agents sort, start, limit
get_my_agent agent_guid, wait_seconds (wait until it is running)
control_agent agent_guid, action (start, stop or restart)
update_agent agent_guid, title, description, timezone, team_session_mode, chat_model, cron_model, enabled_commands, chat_setup (all, webchat or off; null goes back to all)
apply_agent_skills agent_guid, skills, add_dependencies, idempotency_key (only to repeat a change whose answer did not arrive)
set_agent_credentials agent_guid, credential, fields
connect_agent_connector agent_guid, connector, action (connect or status), values, mode (sign_in or key), project_id, redirect_url, wait_seconds, confirm
set_agent_connector_accounts agent_guid, connector, accounts (leave it out to see the choices)
disconnect_agent_connector agent_guid, connector, confirm
list_projects agent_guid (optional: also says which listed project that agent uses)
bind_agent_project agent_guid, project_id (from list_projects; leave it out for the connection's own project), confirm
manage_agent_custom_skill agent_guid, action (upsert, rename, delete, history or revert), key, kind, value, interval, enabled, confirm
manage_agent_billing agent_guid, action (subscribe, change_plan, cancel or renew; buy_credits is retired and charges nothing), plan (starter, pro or max, for subscribe and change_plan), confirm, confirm_charge_usd
get_agent_activity agent_guid, kind (usage, logs or log_dates), entries (for usage: all, ai-usage, model-run, plan or funds), date
delete_agent agent_guid, confirm

list_projects lists the projects of the connected project's workspace by id and name. It marks the connection's own project, the projects this connection can connect to an agent (the ones you created, or any project of a team you are an admin of) and the projects with an IP whitelist, and it shows no keys. bind_agent_project connects the Wiro project an agent runs models with. Called without confirm, it changes nothing: it shows the project, the one it replaces, whether a running agent restarts and which wallet pays for the agent's model runs (the wallet of the workspace that owns the project). After you agree, the assistant repeats the call with confirm: true, as its nextAction shows. Connecting the project an agent already has changes nothing and restarts nothing. On a team agent, a team admin can connect any project of the team, and the person who deployed the agent the projects they created. The API behind it is POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind.

Controls tools

A limit or a rule is for one scope: account, member (a team member, by e-mail or user uuid), project (an API key, by its project's id or name; left out, the key of this connection), surface or agent (by guid or name). See Spend Limits and Model Access for the API behind these tools.

Tool Main arguments
get_controls usage (month or day: also that period's spending by surface, member, API key and agent)
check_model_access model (owner/slug or id), member, project, surface, agent
manage_spend_limit action (set or remove), scope and its target (member, project, surface or agent), period (month or day), amount_usd, alert_percent (50, 80, 90 or null), limit_guid (to remove), confirm
manage_model_access action (update, replace or remove), scope and its target, everything_else (allow or block), categories, models, rule_guid (to remove), confirm

Called without confirm, the two manage tools change nothing: they return the change summary. After you agree, the assistant repeats the call with confirm: true, as its nextAction shows. update keeps the entries of a rule that you don't name, and replace writes the whole rule again.

FAQ

What models can I use?

All models in the Wiro catalog.

Is my API key stored?

No. The server is fully stateless. Credentials are sent per-request and never stored or logged.

Does it cost extra?

No. The MCP server itself is free. You pay the normal prices for the work the tools start: model runs, the model steps of workflow runs, Studio and Workflow Agent turns, and agent plans and the AI usage agents pay from the balance.

What about rate limits?

The hosted MCP endpoint counts requests for each Bearer token, or for each caller IP when a request has none, in a fixed 60-second window. Each window allows 60 tool calls and prompt reads, where every message of a batch counts, and 300 other requests, such as initialize, notifications, listings and ping. Responses carry RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (seconds) for the 60-call budget.

A request over the limit gets HTTP 429 with Retry-After, the same RateLimit headers for the limit it hit, and a JSON-RPC error (code -32000) that says it was not run and when to try again. A batch larger than one window allows gets HTTP 400 (code -32600): it was not run, and it has to be split. These limits come on top of Wiro API project limits. Long generations do not require rapid polling: follow the returned bounded wait_for_task action.

Can I self-host?

Yes. See Self-Hosted MCP for instructions.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Self-Hosted MCP

Run the Wiro MCP server locally on your own machine using npx.

Quick Start

Add to your AI assistant's MCP config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}

That's it. Your assistant can now run Wiro models, build and run workflows, and work with Studio and your own agents. The @latest in args makes npx look up the newest version on npm each time the client starts the server, so it never reuses an older cached build.

Setup

Add the self-hosted MCP server to your AI assistant:

Cursor MCP settings JSON config Claude Code One command setup Claude Desktop JSON config setup Windsurf MCP settings config Kiro JSON config setup goose Command-line extension Other Clients Any MCP-compatible tool

Cursor

Open MCP settings (Cmd+Shift+P → "Open MCP settings") and add:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}

Claude Code

claude mcp add wiro -- npx -y @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest

Then set environment variables:

export WIRO_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export WIRO_API_SECRET="your-api-secret"

Claude Desktop

Add to claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}

Windsurf

Add to your MCP settings:

{

    "wiro": {

      }

Kiro

Add to ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json (every workspace) or .kiro/settings/mcp.json (this workspace):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}

goose

In the goose CLI, run goose configure, pick Add Extension > Command-line Extension, enter npx -y @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest as the command and add WIRO_API_KEY and WIRO_API_SECRET as environment variables. goose Desktop takes the same command and variables under Extensions > Add custom extension. Or add Wiro to ~/.config/goose/config.yaml:

extensions:
  wiro:
    name: Wiro AI
    type: stdio
    cmd: npx
    args: ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest"]
    envs:
      WIRO_API_KEY: your-api-key
      WIRO_API_SECRET: your-api-secret
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

Other Clients

Any MCP client that supports the stdio transport can connect. The command is:

npx -y @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp@latest

Set WIRO_API_KEY and WIRO_API_SECRET as environment variables in your client's MCP configuration.

Authentication

Signature-Based (Recommended)

Provide both API key and secret:

WIRO_API_KEY=your-api-key
WIRO_API_SECRET=your-api-secret

API Key Only

Omit WIRO_API_SECRET:

WIRO_API_KEY=your-api-key

Authentication errors

If the project uses signature-based auth and WIRO_API_SECRET is not set, tool calls fail with:

Wiro API error 401: This project uses signature-based auth. Set WIRO_API_SECRET to the project's API secret in your MCP server config.

Add WIRO_API_SECRET to the env block of your MCP config and restart the client. The other messages are the same as on the hosted server: see Authentication errors.

Available Tools

The self-hosted server provides the same 56 typed tools, playbooks and prompts as the hosted MCP server. Successful calls include structuredContent for LLM chaining plus text content for compatibility. Completed media calls return standard MCP resource links and an assistant-audience delivery instruction so the assistant can present image previews and clickable media links in its user-facing response even when the client does not render media inside its tool card.

All four tool groups load by default. To load fewer tools, set WIRO_TOOLSETS (see Environment Variables). get_account, get_playbook and search_docs are always available.

Model slugs: Use the clean/lowercase format owner/model (e.g. openai/sora-2, wiro/virtual-try-on). These correspond to cleanslugowner/cleanslugproject values returned by search_models.

Models

Tool Wiro API Description
search_models POST /Tool/List Search and browse AI models by keyword, category, or owner. Returns model slugs, titles, descriptions, categories, and pricing.
get_model_schema POST /Tool/Detail, POST /Workflow/UtilityDetail Get full parameter schema and pricing for any model: parameter names, types, options, defaults, and required fields. For a workflow utility, its parameters and output ports.
recommend_model POST /Tool/List Find models for a goal from two or three key words, best matches first.
explore POST /Tool/Explore Browse curated AI models organized by category. No parameters needed.
run_model POST /Run/{owner}/{model} Run any model with parameters. Waits up to 45 seconds by default; if still active, returns a recoverable token for wait_for_task.
wait_for_task POST /Task/Detail Continue waiting for an existing task in bounded windows without creating a duplicate model run.
get_task POST /Task/Detail Check task status immediately, or wait up to 45 seconds with wait_seconds. Returns pexit, outputs, logs, elapsed time, and cost.
list_tasks POST /Task/List Browse authenticated generation history across conversations and continue with get_task.
get_task_price POST /Task/Detail Get the cost of a completed task. Shows whether it was billed and the total charge. Only successful tasks (pexit: "0") are billed.
cancel_task POST /Task/Cancel Cancel a task still in queue (before worker assignment).
kill_task POST /Task/Kill Stop a queued or running task. Task moves to task_cancel status.
upload_file POST /File/Upload Upload a file from a public http(s) URL (up to about 100 MB). Most models also take a public URL directly, without uploading first.

Workflows

Tool Wiro API Description
list_workflows POST /Workflow/List List the workflows in your workspace, or search the public gallery by text, tag or model.
get_workflow POST /Workflow/Detail Read a workflow's inputs, outputs and step graph.
create_workflow POST /Workflow/Prepare, POST /Workflow/Add Save a new workflow from a step graph. Wiro checks it against the live model catalog and returns every problem it finds at once.
update_workflow POST /Workflow/Prepare, POST /Workflow/Update Edit a workflow's title, description, tags or graph without overwriting newer changes; a new graph is saved only after you confirm a summary of the change.
clone_workflow POST /Workflow/Clone Copy a public workflow into your workspace.
delete_workflow POST /Workflow/Delete Delete a workflow, after your confirmation.
run_workflow POST /Workflow/Run Run a workflow and wait for its outputs; can stop after a chosen step to test the first steps.
wait_for_workflow_run POST /Workflow/RunDetail, POST /Workflow/RunNodeDetail Keep waiting on a run, read its outputs, or see why a step failed.
resume_workflow_run POST /Workflow/RunResume Continue a failed or stopped run without paying again for finished steps.
list_workflow_runs POST /Workflow/RunHistory Browse past and current runs, including runs started on wiro.ai.
save_workflow_from_agent POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/Detail, then /Workflow/Add or /Workflow/Update Save a workflow the Workflow Agent proposed, as a new workflow, or onto an existing one after you confirm a summary of the change.

Agents

The conversation tools call the matching Message/* route of Studio (/Studio/), the Workflow Agent (/StudioWorkflow/) or a deployed agent (/UserAgent/), chosen by their agent argument.

Tool Wiro API Description
send_agent_message Message/Send, or Message/SendForm with attachments Send a message and wait for the reply, with any media, workflows or model runs it produced.
get_agent_message Message/Detail Keep waiting on a reply, or read one again.
get_agent_conversation Message/Sessions, Message/History List conversations, or read one conversation's history.
cancel_agent_message Message/Cancel Stop a reply that is still being written.
delete_agent_session Message/ClearSession (Studio), Message/DeleteSession Delete a conversation and the agent's memory of it, after your confirmation.
list_studio_results POST /Studio/Tasks List the images, videos and other results Studio generated for you.
list_agent_templates POST /Agent/List Browse ready-made agent templates and the three monthly plans.
get_agent_template POST /Agent/Detail Read a template's skills, plans, the connectors it suggests and the keys it needs.
list_agent_connectors POST /AgentConnector/List, /AgentConnector/Detail, /UserAgent/ConnectorList (with agent_guid) Browse the connectors an agent can connect, what each one needs and the tools it gives the agent; with an agent, its connections.
list_agent_skills POST /Skills/List, /Skills/Detail, /Skills/Capabilities Browse the skills an agent can have, and what each one needs to work.
deploy_agent POST /UserAgent/PricingPreview, /UserAgent/Deploy Deploy an agent from a template or build one from skills, on the Starter, Pro or Max plan; shows the plan's price and the AI usage it includes, the Wiro balance that pays it and the other plans' prices, and asks before charging.
list_my_agents POST /UserAgent/MyAgents List your agents with their status, plan, AI usage and this month's spending.
get_my_agent POST /UserAgent/Detail Read one agent's setup, plan, AI usage and the balance it runs on; can wait until it is running.
control_agent POST /UserAgent/Start, /UserAgent/Stop, /UserAgent/Update (restart) Start, stop or restart an agent.
update_agent POST /UserAgent/Update, /UserAgent/UpdateSettings Change an agent's name, description, time zone, models, chat commands and setup from chat.
apply_agent_skills POST /UserAgent/PricingPreview, /UserAgent/SkillsApply Turn skills on or off; every plan includes every skill, so a change costs nothing.
set_agent_credentials POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert, /UserAgent/CredentialFileUpload Save an agent's chat channel keys (such as a Telegram bot token), Twilio Voice and settings.
connect_agent_connector POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect, /UserAgent/ConnectorList (status) Connect a connector to an agent: save its keys, or start its sign-in, which you approve in your browser. A connector that runs with a Wiro project shows the project and its wallet first.
set_agent_connector_accounts POST /UserAgent/ConnectorAccounts, /UserAgent/ConnectorSetAccounts Choose the accounts a connected connector may act on, such as its ad accounts, pages or channels.
disconnect_agent_connector POST /UserAgent/ConnectorDisconnect Disconnect a connector from an agent, after your confirmation.
list_projects POST /Project/List, /UserAgent/Detail (with agent_guid) List the projects of the connected project's workspace, to pick one for an agent; no keys are shown.
bind_agent_project POST /UserAgent/Detail, /Project/List, then /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind Connect an agent to a Wiro project so it can run models, with no key in the chat; shows the project first, then asks for your confirmation.
manage_agent_custom_skill POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillUpsert, CustomSkillRename, CustomSkillDelete, CustomSkillHistory, CustomSkillRevert Add, edit, schedule, restore or remove an agent's own instructions and scheduled tasks; turning off its approval policy or changing its rules needs your confirmation.
manage_agent_billing POST /UserAgent/CreateSubscriptionCheckout, UpgradeTier, CancelSubscription, RenewSubscription Subscribe, move to another plan, cancel or renew, paid from your Wiro balance, after your confirmation; buy_credits is retired and charges nothing.
get_agent_activity POST /UserAgent/TransactionList, /UserAgent/LogsList, /UserAgent/Logs Read an agent's AI usage, its transactions in dollars and its activity logs, including who changed what on it.
delete_agent POST /UserAgent/Delete Delete an agent, after your confirmation.

Controls

These tools read and change the workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules. They come with @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp 1.9.0 and later. The self-hosted server's calls count on the api surface for now, as calls with its API key, except its messages to Studio and the Workflow Agent and its workflow runs, which count on studio, workflow-agent and workflow (see Surfaces). Its Controls tools change limits and rules only when the person who created the key's project can change them: a personal account's owner, or in a team a team admin or the organization owner.

Tool Wiro API Description
get_controls POST /SpendLimit/List, /ModelAccess/List, /SpendLimit/Usage Read the workspace's spend limits, with what each has used and when it resets, its Model Access rules, and whether this connection can change them; on request, also this month's or today's spending by surface, member, API key and agent.
check_model_access POST /ModelAccess/Check Explain whether a model may run here and why, rule by rule. Nothing runs and nothing is charged.
manage_spend_limit POST /SpendLimit/List, /SpendLimit/Preview, /SpendLimit/Set, /SpendLimit/Remove Set or remove a spend limit. It shows a change summary first and changes nothing until you confirm.
manage_model_access POST /ModelAccess/List, /ModelAccess/Preview, /ModelAccess/Set, /ModelAccess/Remove Update, replace or remove a Model Access rule. It shows a change summary first and changes nothing until you confirm.

Account and guides

Tool Wiro API Description
get_account POST /Wallet/List, /SpendLimit/List, /Wallet/TransactionList Show which workspace the connected project belongs to, its wallet balance, its spend limits and, when you ask, the wallet's recent transactions.
get_playbook Built into the server Step-by-step guides: getting started, models, workflows, workflow graphs, the Workflow Agent, Studio, agents, billing and Controls.
search_docs Wiro Docs Search the Wiro documentation for guides, API references, and examples.

See the Wiro MCP Server page for the playbook topics, the prompts, the rules for paid and irreversible actions, and the tool arguments.

Environment Variables

Variable Required Description
WIRO_API_KEY Yes Your Wiro project API key
WIRO_API_SECRET No API secret (for signature auth)
WIRO_API_BASE_URL No Override API URL (default: https://api.wiro.ai/v1)
WIRO_TOOLSETS No Comma-separated tool groups to load: models, workflows, agents, controls (default: all)

Choosing tool groups

Some clients work best with fewer tools. Set WIRO_TOOLSETS to load only the groups you need:

"env": {
  "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
  "WIRO_TOOLSETS": "models,workflows"
}

get_account, get_playbook and search_docs are always available, and workflows also brings the model search tools it needs. controls loads the four Controls tools. The conversation tools for Studio and the Workflow Agent, with save_workflow_from_agent, come with either workflows or agents, and each prompt appears only when its tools are loaded. If a job needs a tool from a group that is not loaded, the server instructions tell the assistant to say so.

GitHub & npm

  • GitHub: github.com/wiroai/Wiro-MCP
  • npm: @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp

Using as a Library

import { WiroClient } from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';
import { createMcpServer } from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/server';

const client = new WiroClient('your-api-key', 'your-api-secret');
const server = createMcpServer(client);

// Only the model and workflow tools
const modelsAndWorkflows = createMcpServer(client, { toolsets: ['models', 'workflows'] });
Export Description
createMcpServer(client, options?) Creates an McpServer with the tools, prompts and server instructions registered. options.toolsets picks tool groups and the prompts that use them; options.instructions replaces the instructions; options.wrapTool(tool, handler) returns the handler to register for each tool, for your own logging or permission checks; options.maxToolInputElements caps the array elements and object members one tool call may carry (default 10000, Infinity turns the check off)
WiroClient API client supporting both auth types (signature + apikey-only); post(path, body) calls any Wiro API endpoint with the same credentials, and isOwnApiKey(value) says whether a value is this client's API key. Its requestHeaders option sends headers of your own with every request (see Node.js Library) and replaces the trustedProxy option, which was removed in 1.5.0
registerTools(server, client, options?) Registers the tools on an McpServer you already have, with the same toolsets and wrapTool options. That server then lists every tool schema, its own tools included, as JSON Schema 2020-12
advertiseJsonSchema2020_12(server) Makes an McpServer list its tool schemas as JSON Schema 2020-12. Call it when you register single tools from @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/tools instead of using registerTools
withJsonSchema2020_12(transport) The same for one transport: await server.connect(withJsonSchema2020_12(transport))
parseToolsets(value) Parse a WIRO_TOOLSETS-style list such as "models,agents"

Self-Hosting on Your Server

git clone https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-MCP.git
cd Wiro-MCP
npm install
npm run build
export WIRO_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export WIRO_API_SECRET="your-api-secret"
node dist/index.js

Requires Node.js 20 or later. Create a project to get API keys.

Node.js Library

Use Wiro AI models directly in your Node.js or TypeScript projects with a simple API client.

Overview

The @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp package exports a WiroClient class that you can use as a standalone API client, with no MCP setup required. It handles authentication (both signature-based and API key only), model discovery, execution, task polling, and file uploads.

Links

  • npm: @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp
  • GitHub: wiroai/Wiro-MCP
  • Create API Key

Installation

npm install @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp

Requires Node.js 20 or later.

Quick Start

import { WiroClient } from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';

const client = new WiroClient('YOUR_API_KEY', 'YOUR_API_SECRET');

// Run an image generation model
const run = await client.runModel('google/nano-banana-pro', {
  prompt: 'A futuristic city at sunset',
  aspectRatio: '16:9',
  resolution: '2K'
});

if (!run.result) {
  console.log('Run failed:', run.errors);
  process.exit(1);
}

// Wait for the result (polls Task/Detail until complete)
const result = await client.waitForTask(run.socketaccesstoken);
const task = result.tasklist[0];

if (task.pexit === '0') {
  console.log('Output:', task.outputs[0].url);
} else {
  console.log('Failed:', task.pexit);
}

Authentication

The client supports both Wiro authentication methods:

Signature-Based (Recommended)

Provide both API key and secret. HMAC-SHA256 signatures are generated automatically per request.

const client = new WiroClient('your-api-key', 'your-api-secret');

API Key Only

Omit the secret for simpler server-side usage.

const client = new WiroClient('your-api-key');

Custom Base URL

Override the API endpoint if needed (third parameter):

const client = new WiroClient('key', 'secret', 'https://custom-api.example.com/v1');

Your Own Request Headers

To send headers of your own with every API request, pass requestHeaders in the options (fourth parameter):

const client = new WiroClient('your-api-key', 'your-api-secret', undefined, {
  requestHeaders: () => ({ 'x-app-name': 'my-app' })
});

The function runs for every request the client sends, JSON and multipart, and gets one object, { pathname, apiKey }, where pathname includes the base path, such as /v1/Tool/List. It returns a plain object of string values, and those headers are sent after the client's own. It cannot set x-api-key, x-signature, x-nonce or Content-Type, in any letter case: such a request fails before it is sent. Type it with RequestHeadersHook. This option replaces trustedProxy, which was removed in 1.5.0: a client created with trustedProxy throws.

Available Methods

Method Description
searchModels(params?) Search and browse models by keyword, category, or owner.
getModelSchema(model) Get full parameter schema and pricing for a model.
explore() Browse curated models organized by category.
runModel(model, params, signal?) Run a model. Returns task ID and socket access token.
waitForTask(tasktokenOrReference, timeoutMs?, options?) Poll until completion. Default timeout: 120 seconds. Supports AbortSignal, stepped polling, progress callbacks, and transient retries.
getTask({ tasktoken?, taskid? }, signal?) Get current task status and outputs.
cancelTask(tasktokenOrReference, signal?) Cancel a queued task. Resolves a token to the task ID required by the API.
killTask(tasktokenOrReference, signal?) Kill a running task using its socket access token or task ID.
listTasks(params?, signal?) List the tasks of the key's workspace, newest first.
uploadFile(url, fileName?) Upload a file from a URL for use as model input.
post(path, body?, signal?) Call any other Wiro API endpoint with the same credentials, for example post('/Workflow/List', { scope: 'my' }). Wiro reports each outcome in the response body, so check result on the returned body.
postForm(path, form, signal?) Same as post, for endpoints that take multipart/form-data.
isOwnApiKey(value) Says whether a value is this client's API key, without handing the key out.

If waitForTask exceeds its timeout, it throws TaskWaitTimeoutError and preserves lastDetail. Call it again with the same token or task ID; do not call runModel again for the same generation.

Examples

Search Models

const models = await client.searchModels({
  search: 'image generation',
  categories: ['text-to-image'],
  limit: 5
});

for (const model of models.tool) {
  console.log(`${model.cleanslugowner}/${model.cleanslugproject} — ${model.title}`);
}

Get Model Parameters

const detail = await client.getModelSchema('google/nano-banana-pro');
const model = detail.tool[0];

if (model.parameters) {
  console.log('Parameters:');
  for (const group of model.parameters) {
    for (const param of group.items) {
      console.log(`  ${param.id} (${param.type}) ${param.required ? '— required' : ''}`);
    }
  }
}

Run an LLM

const run = await client.runModel('openai/gpt-5-2', {
  prompt: 'Explain quantum computing in 3 sentences'
});

const result = await client.waitForTask(run.socketaccesstoken);
const task = result.tasklist[0];

if (task.pexit === '0') {
  // Merged text
  console.log(task.debugoutput);

  // Structured thinking/answer
  const output = task.outputs[0];
  if (output.contenttype === 'raw') {
    console.log('Thinking:', output.content.thinking);
    console.log('Answer:', output.content.answer);
  }
}

Upload a File and Use It

Tip: Most models take a public URL instead of an upload. For most image and video inputs you pass it in the field itself, such as inputImage: 'https://example.com/photo.jpg'; a fileinput takes it in its {id}Url field (such as inputImageUrl), so check the model's parameter types. Use uploadFile() when you need to reuse files across multiple runs.

// Upload an image
const upload = await client.uploadFile('https://example.com/photo.jpg');
const fileUrl = upload.list[0].url;

// Use it in a model run
const run = await client.runModel('wiro/virtual-try-on', {
  inputImageHuman: fileUrl,
  inputImageClothes: 'https://example.com/shirt.jpg'
});

const result = await client.waitForTask(run.socketaccesstoken);
console.log('Output:', result.tasklist[0].outputs[0].url);

Poll Manually

const run = await client.runModel('klingai/kling-v3', {
  prompt: 'A drone shot over mountains',
  duration: '5',
  aspectRatio: '16:9'
});

// Poll manually instead of using waitForTask
const interval = setInterval(async () => {
  const detail = await client.getTask({ tasktoken: run.socketaccesstoken });
  const task = detail.tasklist[0];
  console.log('Status:', task.status);

  if (task.status === 'task_postprocess_end') {
    clearInterval(interval);
    if (task.pexit === '0') {
      console.log('Video:', task.outputs[0].url);
    }
  }
}, 5000);

TypeScript

All types are exported from the package:

import { WiroClient } from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';
import type {
  RunModelResult,
  TaskDetailResponse,
  Task,
  TaskOutput,
  ToolListResponse,
  ToolDetailResponse,
  ToolListItem,
  SearchModelsParams,
  TaskReference,
  WaitForTaskOptions,
  RequestHeadersHook,
} from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';
import {
  TaskPollingError,
  TaskWaitTimeoutError,
} from '@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp/client';
Type Description
RunModelResult Response from runModel(): taskid, socketaccesstoken.
TaskDetailResponse Response from getTask() / waitForTask(): contains tasklist array.
Task Individual task object: status, pexit, outputs, debugoutput, etc.
TaskOutput Output entry: file (name, url) or LLM (contenttype: "raw", content).
ToolListResponse Response from searchModels(): contains tool array.
ToolDetailResponse Response from getModelSchema(): contains model with parameters.
SearchModelsParams Search parameters: search, categories, slugowner, limit, etc.
TaskReference Existing task identifier: tasktoken or taskid.
WaitForTaskOptions Polling options: signal, onPoll, pollIntervalMs, and retry limit.
RequestHeadersHook The requestHeaders option: gets { pathname, apiKey } and returns the headers to add.
TaskWaitTimeoutError Bounded wait expired; carries the last Task/Detail response.
TaskPollingError Repeated or permanent status lookup failure; also carries the last response.

n8n Wiro Integration

×

Run any Wiro AI model from your n8n workflows: video, image, audio, LLM, 3D, and more.

Overview

n8n is a powerful workflow automation platform. The Wiro AI community node, published on npm as @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro, runs any model in the Wiro AI catalog from a single node.

Pick a model from a searchable list and its inputs load into the node with their default values. The node starts a task on Wiro, waits for it to finish and returns the output files, or the reply of a text model. It also works as a tool for an n8n AI Agent.

Links

  • npm: @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro
  • GitHub: wiroai/n8n-nodes-wiro
  • n8n: Wiro AI integration (verified)
  • n8n Community Nodes Installation Guide
  • Wiro Model Catalog: browse all available models

Available Model Categories

Category Models Examples
Video Generation Text-to-video, image-to-video Veo 3.1, Kling V3, Seedance, Hailuo, PixVerse, Runway
Image Generation Text-to-image, style transfer GPT Image 2, Flux 2 Pro, Seedream, Nano Banana, Qwen Image
Image Editing Try-on, face swap, background removal Virtual Try-On, Face Swap, Prompt-based Editing, Style Transfer
Audio & Speech TTS, STT, voice clone, music ElevenLabs TTS, Gemini TTS, Whisper STT, Voice Clone
LLM Chat Chat completion, RAG GPT-5.2, GPT-5 Mini, Gemini 3, Claude Fable 5.2, RAG Chat
3D Generation Image/text to 3D Trellis 2, Hunyuan3D 2.1
Translation Multi-language with image support Gemma-based (4B, 12B, 27B)
E-Commerce Product photos, ads, templates Product Photoshoot, Shopify Templates, UGC Creator
HR Tools CV analysis, job descriptions CV Evaluator, Resume Parser, Culture Fit

Wiro AI Node

Resource Operation What it does
Model Run Runs a model with your inputs and returns its outputs
Task Get Reads a task by its ID, with its status and outputs
Task Wait Waits until a task finishes, then returns its outputs
  • Model: pick the model from the searchable list, paste its wiro.ai link, or type it as owner/model, such as pruna/p-image.
  • Inputs: the inputs of the model you picked load into the node with their default values. Required inputs are always shown; add advanced ones with Add input to send. Fill them in or map them from the incoming item. File inputs take public URLs; separate several URLs with commas.
  • Wait for Completion is on by default, and the node waits up to 20 minutes (change it with Max Wait Time). Turn it off to get the task ID at once, then read the task later with Task > Get or Task > Wait.

The node returns the task with its output files and cost:

{
  "taskId": "5986221",
  "status": "completed",
  "model": "pruna/p-image",
  "url": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/xyz/0.png",
  "urls": ["https://cdn1.wiro.ai/xyz/0.png"],
  "costUsd": 0.005,
  "elapsedSeconds": 3
}
Field What it holds
taskIdThe ID of the Wiro task
statusqueued, running, completed, failed or cancelled
modelThe model, as owner/model
urlThe first output file
urlsEvery output file
textThe reply of a text model
costUsdWhat the task cost, in US dollars
elapsedSecondsHow long the task ran

A task that fails or is cancelled stops the node with an error. To handle it in its own branch, set the node's On Error setting to Continue (using error output). A task still running when the wait ends comes back with status: "running": read it later with Task > Wait and the same task ID instead of starting it again.

Installation

Install the community node package in your n8n instance:

From the nodes panel

The Wiro AI node is verified by n8n. An instance owner can search for Wiro AI in the nodes panel of the workflow editor and install it, on n8n Cloud and on self-hosted instances that show verified community nodes. After that, everyone on the instance can add it to their workflows.

Via n8n UI (Recommended)

  1. Open your n8n instance Navigate to your self-hosted or cloud n8n dashboard
  2. Go to Settings Open Settings → Community Nodes
  3. Install the node Click Install a community node and enter: @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro
  4. Confirm Click Install and wait for completion

Via Command Line

npm install @wiro-ai/n8n-nodes-wiro

Run it in ~/.n8n/nodes, then restart n8n.

Authentication

The node supports both Wiro authentication methods:

  1. Add credentials Go to Credentials → Add new → Wiro AI API in n8n
  2. Enter your keys Paste the project's API Key. If the project uses signature authentication, also paste its API Secret: the node then signs every request with HMAC-SHA256 and never sends the secret.
  3. Save Click Save, and n8n checks the key

Get your credentials at wiro.ai/panel/project. Runs are billed to the wallet of the project's workspace.

Usage

Search the node picker for "Wiro AI" and add the node with the Run a model action, then pick the model.

Example: Generate an Image with P-Image

  1. Add the Wiro AI node with the Run a model action
  2. In Model, search for p-image and pick pruna/p-image
  3. Under Inputs, set Prompt to A red bicycle on a sunny street
  4. Run the workflow: url in the output links to the image

Example: Generate a Video with Kling V3

  1. Add the Wiro AI node and pick klingai/kling-v3 in Model
  2. Set Prompt to A cat astronaut floating in space, and leave Duration and Ratio at their defaults or pick others
  3. Run the workflow: url in the output links to the video

Example: Turn an LLM Reply into an Image

  1. Add a Wiro AI node with openai/gpt-5-mini and a Prompt that asks for one image prompt. Its reply is in text
  2. Add a second Wiro AI node with pruna/p-image and map its Prompt to {{ $json.text }}
  3. Run the workflow: url in the second node's output links to the image

The package README has this workflow as JSON that you can paste into n8n.
