Workflows

Chain models and built-in steps into one graph, save it, and run it again with new inputs.

Overview

A workflow is a saved chain of steps. Each step runs one Wiro model or one built-in utility. The Start node holds the inputs people fill in, and the End node lists the results. A saved workflow runs each time someone starts it, on wiro.ai/workflows or through the API.

The /Workflow/* endpoints list and read workflows, save new ones from a graph, edit, clone and delete them, run them and follow their runs. To design a workflow in plain language, use the Workflow Agent. The Wiro MCP Server offers these endpoints as tools for AI assistants.

Authentication

Every /Workflow/* route on this page takes a project API key: x-api-key, plus x-nonce and x-signature for a project that uses signature authentication (see Authentication). A key acts as the person who created its project, in that project's workspace.

Workspaces and the gallery

  • A workflow belongs to the workspace it was created in: personal, or a team. Another workspace cannot read, run or change it, unless it is published in the public gallery: anyone can read and run a published workflow.
  • A protected workflow hides its steps from people outside its owner's workspace. They can still see its inputs and outputs and run it.
  • Workflows saved through the API are private. Publishing to the gallery happens on wiro.ai, and a published workflow goes through review again after its title, description, tags or steps change.

Slugs

A workflow is named by its full slug: its slug, a dash and its 5-character slugid, such as product-shots-a1B2c. Every endpoint that takes a workflow takes the full slug as slug. The workflow's page is https://wiro.ai/workflows/<full slug>.

The Workflow Graph

A workflow's definition is one JSON object, its contents. It holds the steps, the Start fields people fill in and the End node that lists the results. Before you save a graph you wrote yourself, prepare it with Workflow/Prepare: it checks the graph against the live model catalog and fills in what the Wiro editor would.

Field Type Description
version string Always "1".
nodes object The steps, keyed by step id, plus the End node under the key output. The Start node is not in nodes.
schema.input object The Start fields, keyed by the input names a run takes.
schema.output object Always {}.
output object A copy of the End node's fields.
metadata.input.position object Where the Start node sits on the canvas, such as { "x": 0, "y": 0 }.
metadata.input.values object Optional saved values for the Start fields. A run uses them for the fields it leaves out.

Workflow/Prepare accepts a graph of at most 40 KB of JSON (40,960 bytes), and counts it again after it fills each step's defaults.

Steps

Each step is "node-<id>": { "id", "type", "tool", "depends", "input", "metadata" }.

  • The key is node- followed by 1 to 64 letters, digits, - or _. id repeats the key exactly, and type is "run".
  • tool is a model slug (owner/model) or a built-in utility: workflow-utilities/output-filter, workflow-utilities/merge-text or workflow-utilities/split-text.
  • input maps the tool's parameter ids, from Tool/Detail, to values: fixed values, or references to Start fields and earlier steps.
  • depends lists every source the step reads: "input" when it uses a Start field, and the id of each step it references. No duplicates, never the step itself, never "output".
  • metadata.position is { "x": number, "y": number } and only places the step on the canvas.

Start fields

Each key in schema.input is that input's name at run time. Give each field label, type, defaultValue and ui (an object); Workflow/Prepare fills in the rest the way the editor does. wiro.ai titles each field with its key in the run form, so use a short readable key such as product_photo.

  • Text: "type": "string" with "ui": { "field": "textarea" }.
  • Choice list: "type": "string" with "ui": { "field": "select", "options": [{ "value": "16:9", "text": "Wide" }] }.
  • Number: "type": "number" (whole) or "float" (decimal). Yes or no: "type": "boolean". Both with "ui": {}.
  • File: "type": "string" with "ui": { "field": "image" }, or "audio", "video" or "pdf". The value is a public URL.

A Start field that the End node or a step leading to it uses, with no saved value and no default, must get a value when the workflow runs. Workflow/Detail names these fields in requiredinputs.

References

  • $input.<key> is the value of a Start field.
  • $node-<id>.outputs is everything a model step produced: its files, or an LLM step's reply.
  • $node-<id>.result is the result of output-filter or merge-text. $node-<id>.text1 to .textN are the parts produced by split-text.

A reference must be the whole string value, or one whole item of an array. It is never filled in inside longer text, and a fixed value that starts with $ is read as a reference. To put a Start field or an LLM answer inside a prompt, join the parts with merge-text, such as "texts": ["Write a caption for:", "$input.name"], and reference its result.

When a model step's outputs feed another model, a single file parameter takes the first file, a combined file parameter (combinefileinput) takes all of the files, and a text parameter takes the first file URL or the LLM's answer.

The End node

It is "output": { "id": "output", "type": "display", "depends", "input": {}, "fields", "metadata" }.

  • fields maps each result name to one reference. Give each result its own source.
  • depends lists the steps the fields read from. It cannot be empty: a workflow with nothing wired to its End node cannot run.
  • The top-level output must equal fields. Steps that do not lead to the End node never run.

Built-in utilities

Utilities are free and finish at once. Workflow/UtilityDetail returns their parameters and output ports.

  • output-filter picks items from a model step. Its outputs parameter must be a $node-<id>.outputs reference. With mode "file" it keeps the files that match contenttype (such as "image", "audio/*" or "mp3") and name, up to count items (default 1). With mode "llm" it takes field ("answer", "thinking", "raw" or "prompt") from an LLM step. Port: result.
  • merge-text joins texts (an array of references or fixed strings) with separator (default a space), skipping empty items unless skipEmpty is false. Port: result.
  • split-text splits text by separator (default a new line) into count parts, 2 to 10 (default 5). count must be a fixed value. Ports: text1 to textN.

Other operations, such as joining videos or adding a voice track to a video, are ordinary models in the catalog.

Model steps

  • Use only parameter ids from the model's Tool/Detail.
  • Set every parameter you care about. A parameter you leave out takes the model's default from Tool/Detail. To leave a file parameter empty, set it to [], or "" for a single file.
  • A single file parameter takes one URL string. A combined file parameter (combinefileinput) takes an array, even for one file. A multi-file parameter (multifileinput) takes its URLs comma-separated in its matching ...UrlMultiple field.
  • Take each value, such as a duration, a size or an option, from the model's schema in Tool/Detail.
  • Training models cannot be used in workflows.

A minimal workflow

One text input, one image model and one result. Replace owner/model with a real model and prompt with that model's text parameter id.

{
  "version": "1",
  "nodes": {
    "node-image": {
      "id": "node-image", "type": "run", "tool": "owner/model", "depends": ["input"],
      "input": { "prompt": "$input.prompt" },
      "metadata": { "position": { "x": 350, "y": 0 } }
    },
    "output": {
      "id": "output", "type": "display", "depends": ["node-image"], "input": {},
      "fields": { "image": "$node-image.outputs" },
      "metadata": { "position": { "x": 700, "y": 0 } }
    }
  },
  "output": { "image": "$node-image.outputs" },
  "schema": {
    "input": {
      "prompt": { "label": "Prompt", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "", "ui": { "field": "textarea" } }
    },
    "output": {}
  },
  "metadata": { "input": { "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 } } }
}

To turn that image into a video, add a second model step that reads the first step's file and a motion Start field:

"node-video": {
  "id": "node-video", "type": "run", "tool": "owner/video-model",
  "depends": ["input", "node-image"],
  "input": { "inputImage": "$node-image.outputs", "prompt": "$input.motion" },
  "metadata": { "position": { "x": 700, "y": 0 } }
}

Then set the End node's "depends": ["node-video"] and "fields": { "video": "$node-video.outputs" }, copy those fields to the top-level output, and move the End node to "x": 1050. inputImage stands for the video model's image parameter: check its real id in the model's schema.

How a Run Works

Workflow/Run answers at once with a run token, the workflowtoken; the steps run after that. Read the run with Workflow/RunDetail until its status is final.

  • Only the steps that lead to the End node run. Steps run in layers: a step that depends on no other step is in the first layer, and any other step is one layer after the latest of the steps it depends on. The steps of a layer start together, and the next layer starts once every step of the current one has finished.
  • When a step fails, every step in a later layer is skipped, on every branch, and the run ends as failed.
  • Check the expected cost (see Costs) before you start a run.
  • The run belongs to the caller's workspace and is paid from that workspace's wallet, also when the workflow is a public one from another workspace.

Run statuses

Status Meaning
running Steps are queued or running.
completed Every step finished. The End node's fields hold the results.
failed A step failed, and the steps after it were skipped.
stopped The run reached its breakpoint. Continue it with RunResume.
cancelled One of the run's steps was cancelled.

A step is pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled or aborted (skipped because an earlier step failed). A failed step's cause is tool-error (the model refused its inputs or the task failed; error says why), poll-timeout (the step ran past 4 hours and was not charged), spend-limit-reached (a spend limit refused the step before it started; error holds the limit's message), or another short code.

Breakpoints

To test the first steps, start the run with breakpointNodeId. The run executes every layer up to and including the one that holds that step, then ends as stopped, and the steps after it stay pending. The breakpoint must be a step the run executes and cannot be in the last layer. Only people who can edit the workflow can set one. Check the outputs, then continue with RunResume, to the end or to a later breakpoint.

Resuming

RunResume continues a failed or stopped run on the same workflowtoken. Completed steps keep their outputs and are not charged again. Failed, skipped and not yet run steps run again as new tasks, billed to the wallet that paid for the run.

A resume runs the remaining steps exactly as the run started them, with the same inputs and settings: changes saved to the workflow since then apply to new runs only. So resume after a temporary failure, such as a timeout or a model that asked to try again later. An error about a parameter value, a file or a limit such as duration or size comes from the inputs or the settings: fix them and start a new run.

Costs

  • Saving, reading, preparing, cloning and deleting workflows is free.
  • Nothing is charged when a run starts. Each model step is a normal model task, billed when it finishes successfully at that model's price. Failed steps are not charged, and utility steps are free.
  • To start, the wallet must hold $0.50 for each model step the run will execute (up to the breakpoint, when one is set). Otherwise the run is refused with code 97, Insufficient balance. The concurrency limit also applies (code 96).
  • The expected cost of a run is the sum of the model prices for the settings each step uses, from Tool/Detail. A run's totalcost shows the list price of the steps finished so far, and once the run has ended chargedcost and discountamount show what the wallet paid. chargedcost is null while a step's charge is still settling.
  • The workspace's spend limits apply when a run starts or resumes, and again before each step starts. A run is refused with code 93 when its known price would go over a limit that covers it, or once that limit has no room left. Each step is checked the same way with its own price, and holds that price until it is charged. A step a limit refuses fails with cause spend-limit-reached, and the run ends as failed: resume it with RunResume once the limit allows.
  • The workspace's Model Access rules apply when a run starts or resumes: when a rule blocks the model of a step that will run, the run is refused with code 92 before anything runs, and the message names that model. When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, as on a protected workflow from another workspace, the message names your rule but not the model, for example Your account can't use one of the models this workflow runs. Model Access rules decide which models can run. Steps that will not run, such as the steps after a breakpoint, are not checked.
  • A run, its resumes and every step it runs count on the workflow surface of spend limits and Model Access, whether you start it with an API key, through MCP or in the dashboard, and each step's task has surface workflow. A run that a deployed agent, Studio or the Workflow Agent starts keeps that surface instead. Before workflows had their own surface, a run counted on the surface it was started from, such as api.

POST /Workflow/List

Lists the workflows of the key's workspace, or searches the public gallery.

Parameter Type Required Description
scope string No "my" (default) for the key's workspace, "public" for the public gallery.
search string No Text to look for in the slug, title, description or tags.
sort string No my: createtime (default), updatetime or title. public: createtime (default), runcount, likecount, clonecount or ratingscore.
order string No DESC (default) or ASC.
start number No Offset for paging. Default 0.
limit number No Rows per page. my: default 20, maximum 1000. public: default 50, maximum 200.
ispublic string No my only: "0" for private workflows, "1" for workflows submitted to the gallery.
tags array No public only: workflows with any of these tags, up to 20.
model string No public only: workflows that use this model, as "owner/model".
onlyfavorites string No public only: "1" for the workflows you liked.
toolpreview string No public only: "1" adds toolitems, the models each workflow uses with their titles and covers.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [...], "total": 1 }. In your workspace (my), a personal key lists your own workflows and a team key lists every workflow of the team.

Field Description
id The workflow's numeric id.
slug, slugid The full slug is <slug>-<slugid>.
title, description, tags, cover The workflow's details.
ispublic 1 when the workflow was submitted to the gallery.
status null when never published, 1 waiting for review, 2 listed in the gallery, 3 rejected.
isprotected 1 when the steps are hidden from people outside the owner's workspace.
clonedfromid On a clone, the id of the workflow it was copied from.
stepcount, toolcount, utilitycount The number of steps, model steps and utility steps.
teamname The team the workflow belongs to, if any.
runcount, likecount, clonecount, ratingaverage, ratingcount, commentcount Gallery counters. runcount counts runs while the workflow is listed.
createtime, updatetime Unix seconds. Pass updatetime to Update as loadedUpdatetime.

Gallery rows (public) also carry tools (the models the workflow uses; null on a protected workflow) and user (username, avatar) for the creator.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workflow": [
    {
      "id": 1842,
      "slug": "product-ad",
      "slugid": "a1B2c",
      "title": "Product ad",
      "description": "Turns a product photo into a short ad video",
      "tags": ["ads", "video"],
      "cover": null,
      "ispublic": 0,
      "status": null,
      "isprotected": 0,
      "clonedfromid": null,
      "stepcount": 2,
      "toolcount": 2,
      "utilitycount": 0,
      "teamname": null,
      "runcount": 0,
      "likecount": 0,
      "clonecount": 0,
      "ratingaverage": null,
      "ratingcount": 0,
      "commentcount": 0,
      "createtime": "1761901200",
      "updatetime": "1761901200"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}

POST /Workflow/Detail

Returns one workflow with its graph.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes The full slug, such as product-ad-a1B2c.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [ { ... } ] }: the fields of List plus contents, the graph as an object (see The Workflow Graph). Its schema.input lists the inputs a run takes, and metadata.input.values the saved values.

  • requiredinputs lists the Start fields a run must be given: the ones used by the End node or by a step leading to it that have no saved value and no default. An empty array means a run needs no input. Read this list to decide what to ask for; a field's required flag in schema.input doesn't decide it. On a protected workflow from another workspace, a run doesn't use the creator's saved values, so only a default takes a field off the list.
  • A workflow from your workspace, or one published in the gallery, can be read. A private workflow of another workspace answers This workflow does not belong to your current workspace. or You don't have any permission for this action., and a clone can only be read by its owner's workspace.
  • A protected workflow read from outside its owner's workspace comes back with its steps removed: contents keeps only the Start fields and the End node, and estimatedcost gives an estimate of one run, { "type": "estimated", "value": 0.42 } ("unavailable" with value: null when it cannot be estimated).
  • rejectreason is present only for the workflow's own workspace: on a rejected workflow it says why.
  • A deleted or unknown workflow answers Workflow not found.

Saved Start values are part of the workflow: everyone who can read it sees them, the gallery too once it is published, and clones keep them. Never save a key, token or password there. Model steps are billed to the Wiro wallet and need no key from the model's provider.

POST /Workflow/Prepare

Prepares a graph you wrote for saving, the way the Wiro editor does: it checks every step against the live model catalog, fills each model parameter you left out with its default, completes the Start fields and the End node, and lays the steps out. It writes and charges nothing. Prepare the graph, then save the prepared contents with Add or Update.

Parameter Type Required Description
contents object Yes The graph, as an object or a JSON string.
mode string No "create" (default) lays every step out again, for a new workflow. "apply" keeps the positions you sent, for a change to an existing workflow; every step then needs a numeric position.
anchorNodeIds array No apply only: step ids ("input" for Start, "output" for End) that keep their exact positions; the other steps move down until nothing overlaps.

On success, contents is the prepared graph. On failure, result is false and issues lists every problem at once, each { code, message, nodeId, input }: nodeId is the step ("input" for a Start field, "output" for an End field) and input the parameter or field. warnings can come back either way; required-input-missing means a Start field a step uses has no default, so every run must send a value for it.

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 0, "message": "...", "time": 1761901200 }],
  "issues": [
    { "code": "unknown-input", "message": "...", "nodeId": "node-image", "input": "promt" },
    { "code": "contents-too-large", "message": "Workflow JSON exceeds the 40960-byte limit.", "bytes": 52114, "limit": 40960 }
  ],
  "warnings": []
}

Common issue codes: tool-not-found and tool-not-marketplace (the model does not exist or is not public), unknown-input (a parameter id the model does not have), unknown-input-reference, unknown-node-reference and reference-missing-dependency (a reference to a missing Start field or step, or one not listed in depends), embedded-workflow-reference (a reference inside longer text), file-input-not-array and single-file-only (one file where an array is needed, or the reverse), request-parameter-required (a required model parameter has no value), param-out-of-bounds, cycle-detected, workflow-has-no-reachable-nodes, duplicate-end-reference, and contents-too-large or prepared-contents-too-large with bytes and limit.

Prepare fills every model parameter you leave out with the model's default: compare the prepared step inputs with what you sent, and set or empty the ones you did not mean to keep.

POST /Workflow/Add

Saves a new, private workflow in the key's workspace.

Parameter Type Required Description
title string Yes The workflow's title. If the workspace already has a workflow with this title, a number is added, such as Product ad-2.
slug string Yes The title part of the slug: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, such as product-ad. Wiro adds the 5-character slugid.
contents string Yes The prepared graph as a JSON string.
description string No What the workflow does and what people should put in its inputs.
tags string No A JSON string of an array of tags, such as "[\"ads\",\"video\"]". Tags that start with wiro- are reserved.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [ { ... } ] } with the saved workflow, including its slugid and updatetime. Add checks that every model and utility exists; run the graph through Prepare first, which checks the references, the inputs and everything else a run needs.

POST /Workflow/Update

Changes a workflow of the key's workspace.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes The full slug.
title string No A new title.
description string No A new description.
tags string No A JSON string of the new tag array. Keep any wiro- tags the workflow already has.
contents string No A new graph as a JSON string, prepared with mode: "apply". It replaces the old one.
loadedUpdatetime string No The updatetime you read. If someone saved the workflow since then, nothing is written.
force boolean No true saves even when loadedUpdatetime no longer matches.
input object No Protected clones only: new saved values for the Start fields, by key.

Title and description are changed only when you send a non-empty value. The response holds the workflow after the change, with its new updatetime.

  • Concurrent edits. When loadedUpdatetime no longer matches, the update is refused with This workflow was modified by another user. Reload to see latest changes or save to overwrite. and the response carries currentUpdatetime. Read the workflow again and redo the change on top, or send force: true to overwrite.
  • Published workflows. Changing the title, description, tags or graph of a workflow in the gallery sends it back to review, and it leaves the gallery until it is approved again.
  • Clones. A clone of a protected workflow keeps its steps hidden: you can change its title, description and tags, and its saved Start values with input, but not its contents.
  • When a new graph stops using files that were uploaded into the workflow in the wiro.ai editor, those files are deleted, unless a past run or a clone still uses them.

POST /Workflow/Clone

Copies a workflow from the public gallery into the key's workspace.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes The full slug of a workflow listed in the gallery.

The copy is private and free. It keeps the graph and the saved Start values; a taken title becomes Title-Clone. The response holds the new workflow, without contents: read it with Detail. Each call makes another copy.

  • Only a workflow listed in the gallery can be cloned (This workflow cannot be cloned), and not into the workspace it already belongs to (This workflow already belongs to this workspace).
  • A clone can never be published or cloned again, and only its own workspace can read it.
  • A clone of a protected workflow keeps its steps hidden from everyone, its owner included. It can still be run.

POST /Workflow/Delete

Deletes a workflow of the key's workspace. It leaves every list and the gallery and can no longer be run or read. Runs already started finish, and clones keep working.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes The full slug.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflow": [] }. There is no undo.

POST /Workflow/Run

Starts a run and answers at once with its token.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes The full slug.
input object No Values for the Start fields, keyed as in schema.input: strings, numbers, booleans or arrays. Files are public URLs. A field you leave out uses its saved value, then its default.
breakpointNodeId string No A step id to stop after (see Breakpoints). 
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "workflowtoken": "Lk3vQ9xT2mWc7Rp4Yh8Nd1Fs6Gb0Zj"
}
  • Your own workspace's workflows and the workflows listed in the gallery can be run. On a protected gallery workflow from another workspace, a field you leave out uses its default, not the creator's saved value.
  • An unknown input key is refused with Unknown input field(s): <keys>. Check your workflow's Start Node schema for valid field names., and a Start field that a step needs and that has no value is refused with A required input value is missing: <key>.
  • Missing inputs and broken references are all returned at once, and nothing is charged for a refused run.
  • File inputs are fetched from public http(s) URLs, up to about 100 MB each.

POST /Workflow/RunDetail

Returns a run and its steps. Call it until status is completed, failed, stopped or cancelled.

Parameter Type Required Description
workflowtoken string Yes The run token.

The response has workflowrun and workflowrunnodes. Runs are private: the person who started a run can read it, and in a team workspace every member of the team can.

workflowrun field Description
workflowtoken, workflowslug The run token and the workflow's full slug.
status running, completed, failed, stopped or cancelled.
outcome The final status, once the run has ended.
canresume true when you can continue this run with RunResume.
breakpointnodeid The breakpoint in effect, or null.
contents The graph as this run started it, with the Start values it used.
totalcost The list price of the steps finished so far, in USD.
chargedcost, discountamount Once the run has ended: what the wallet paid and the discount. null while a charge is still settling.
startedAt Start time in milliseconds. resumedAt is added when the run was resumed.
elapsedseconds Running time, summed over resumes.
failedNodeCount, abortedNodeCount, cancelledNodeCount Step counts.
workflowrunnodes field Description
nodeId, tool, kind The step id, its model or utility, and tool or utility.
layerIdx The step's layer, from 0.
status pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled or aborted.
cause, error Why the step did not complete.
tasktoken For a model step that started a task. Pass it to RunNodeDetail.
outputs A model step's results: files with url, name, contenttype and size, or an LLM's reply as { "contenttype": "raw", "content": { "answer": [...] } }. A utility step's ports, such as { "result": [...] }. A file entry carries no path or mntpath: use its url.
elapsedseconds How long the step ran.

To find a run's results, read the End node's fields in contents and take the outputs of the steps they reference.

When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, as on a protected workflow from another workspace, the run comes back with graphmasked: true: contents shows only the Start fields and the End node, and workflowrunnodes holds only the steps the End node shows, with their status and outputs.

Response

  "errors": [],

POST /Workflow/RunNodeDetail

Shows what one model step received and returned, to debug a failed step.

Parameter Type Required Description
tasktoken string Yes The step's tasktoken from RunDetail.

The response's workflowrunnode has the step's RunDetail fields plus taskDetail: the parameters the model received, its debugoutput, taskStatus, and modelslugowner and modelslugproject. Utility steps have no task to read. When the workflow's steps are hidden from you, it answers You don't have any permission for this action.

POST /Workflow/RunHistory

Lists runs, newest first. A personal key lists your own runs; a team key lists the runs of every member of the team. Runs started on wiro.ai are included.

Parameter Type Required Description
start number No Offset. Default 0.
limit number No Default 20, maximum 1000.
status string No running, completed, failed, stopped or cancelled.
search string No Text in the workflow's title, or its slug without the 5-character id: product-ad finds the runs of product-ad-a1B2c.
workflowid number No Only the runs of this workflow id.
sort string No id (default), starttime, status or totalcost.
order string No DESC (default) or ASC.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflowruns": [...], "total": 12 }. Each row has the workflowrun fields of RunDetail without contents, plus workflowid, workflowtitle, teamname and nodes, each step's { nodeId, tool, kind, layerIdx, status }. To read a run's outputs, call RunDetail with its token.

POST /Workflow/RunResume

Continues a failed or stopped run on the same token. See Resuming.

Parameter Type Required Description
workflowtoken string Yes The run token.
breakpointNodeId string No A new breakpoint. Send null to run to the end. Leave the field out and a failed run keeps the breakpoint it started with, while a stopped run runs to the end.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "workflowtoken": "..." }; follow the run with RunDetail again.

  • The person who started the run can resume it after a failure. Continuing a stopped run, and setting a breakpoint, needs someone who can edit the workflow; in a team workspace any such member can.
  • The balance check runs again for the steps that will run.
  • This run is already resuming or still wrapping up. Try again in a moment and A step of this run is still finishing. Try again in a few minutes mean an earlier step is still settling: wait a few minutes and try once more.
  • Any other status is refused with Only a failed or stopped run can be resumed.

POST /Workflow/UtilityDetail

Returns a built-in utility's parameters and output ports, in the same shape as a model's parameters in Tool/Detail.

Parameter Type Required Description
slug string Yes workflow-utilities/output-filter, workflow-utilities/merge-text or workflow-utilities/split-text.

The response's utility holds one entry with slug, title, description, parameters (groups of parameter definitions with id, type, label, defaultvalue, options, minvalue and maxvalue) and outputs, the ports, each { id, label, type }.

Errors

Business errors come back with HTTP 200, result: false and an errors array, as everywhere in the Wiro API. The ones you will see most:

Message Code When
Workflow not found 0 An unknown or deleted workflow.
This workflow does not belong to your current workspace. 0 A private workflow of another workspace. Use a key from a project in the workflow's workspace.
You don't have any permission for this action. 0 The key's project creator has no rights on this workflow or run.
You must be a member of this team to perform this action 0 A team project's key whose creator is no longer a member of the team.
slug has invalid format 0 Not a full slug ending in a dash and a 5-character id.
invalid json for contents param. 0 Add or Update with contents that is not a JSON string.
Contents do not match the expected workflow structure. 0 A graph without the required shape (see The Workflow Graph).
This tool in the workflow was not found: <slug> 0 A step's model does not exist.
Tags that start with wiro- are reserved for Wiro 0 Add or Update with a wiro- tag.
This workflow was modified by another user. Reload to see latest changes or save to overwrite. 0 Update with an outdated loadedUpdatetime; the response adds currentUpdatetime.
This workflow cannot be cloned 0 Clone of a workflow that is not listed in the gallery.
Unknown input field(s): <keys>. Check your workflow's Start Node schema for valid field names. 0 Run with an input key the workflow does not have.
A required input value is missing: <key>. 0 Run without a value for a Start field a step needs.
Workflows cannot include train tools as they take days to complete 0 A step uses a training model.
Insufficient balance 97 The wallet holds less than $0.50 per model step that will run.
You have reached your concurrent task limit... 96 See Concurrency Limits.
Only people who can edit this workflow can stop a run at a step 0 breakpointNodeId from someone who cannot edit the workflow.
There is no workflow run yet. 0 An unknown run token.
Only a failed or stopped run can be resumed 0 RunResume on a run that is running or completed.

Authentication errors are listed in the Error Reference.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Workflow Agent

Design and edit Wiro workflows by chat: describe the job, read the agent's proposals and save the one you want.

Overview

The Workflow Agent is a Wiro chat agent that designs and edits workflows. It looks up current models and utilities in the Wiro catalog and replies with an explanation and zero or more proposed workflows. It never saves, changes or runs anything itself: your application saves a proposal with the Workflows endpoints and runs it there.

The Workflow Agent runs on one setup shared by everyone who uses it, so it never changes that setup: it proposes no setup cards, and its connectors, skills and scheduled tasks are fixed. Asked for a standing rule or a recurring job, it helps with the request once, as a one-time task.

The Workflow Agent API uses the message protocol of Agent Messaging on its own routes under /StudioWorkflow/:

  1. Send a brief with Message/Send. Attach a workflow in workflowContext to have it edited.
  2. Follow the turn on the Agent WebSocket with the agenttoken, or poll Message/Detail until it ends.
  3. Read the proposals from the reply (see Proposals) and save the one you want with Workflow/Add, or onto the attached workflow with Workflow/Update.

A question the catalog answers, such as which model is cheapest for a job, needs no turn: Tool/List and Tool/Detail answer it for free. When you already know the graph, write it yourself and save it with Workflow/Add.

Authentication

Every /StudioWorkflow/* route takes a project API key: x-api-key, plus x-nonce and x-signature for a project that uses signature authentication (see Authentication). A key acts as the person who created its project, in that project's workspace. For a team project, that person must still be a member of the team; otherwise every route answers HTTP 403 with You must be a member of this team to perform this action.

Sessions

A session is one conversation with its own memory. sessionkey names it, and "default" is used when you leave it out.

  • Sessions started with an API key belong to that key's project. Everyone who uses the key shares them, and they are separate from the Workflow Agent chats on wiro.ai and from other projects' sessions. Each project has its own "default" session.
  • A session name uses letters, digits, ., _, : and -, without :cron:, up to 100 characters. Any other name is refused with sessionkey has invalid format.
  • Use one session per task and keep using it to refine its proposals; start a new one for an unrelated task.
  • The turns of one session run one at a time. A project can have at most 2 turns queued or running at once through its API key; a third message is refused with This project already has 2 Workflow Agent replies in progress. Wait for one to finish before sending another message.

Costs

  • $10 to start a turn. Send and SendForm need at least $10 spendable in the wallet of the key's workspace. Below that, the message is refused with code 97 (Insufficient balance), with walletUsd and minTopup in the response, and nothing is charged.
  • Project. A call with an API key runs on that key's project. Messages sent from wiro.ai run on the workspace's Studio project, which the Workflow Agent shares with Studio: the first Studio or Workflow Agent message from wiro.ai creates it, or uses the workspace's existing project named "Studio". StudioWorkflow/Status shows it, and Studio/ProjectSet changes it.
  • Chat. Each turn is charged after it ends for the tokens it used, at the chat model's rates in StudioWorkflow/Status (cents per 1M tokens), on the turn's project and the workflow-agent surface. The reply's tokencost shows the charge in cents: tokencost / 100 is the amount in USD.
  • Spend limits and Model Access. The chat counts toward your workspace's spend limits, and its chat model follows your Model Access rules: the account's or the team's, your own in a team, those of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the Studio project for a message sent from wiro.ai), and those of the workflow-agent surface. A message whose chat model a rule blocks is refused with code 92 before anything runs.
  • The agent only reads the catalog, so its turns start no model runs. Saving a proposal is free, and running the saved workflow is billed like any workflow run.
  • StudioWorkflow/Transactions lists the charges.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Status

Returns the wallet check, the chat models the agent can use and the project it works on, after settling your pending Workflow Agent charges. It takes no request fields, and its fields are the same as Studio/Status: walletUsd, needsTopup, minTopup (10), tokenRates, agentModel.chatModel, blockedModels, agentModelBlocked, agentModelMessage and project (current, options and canchange): with an API key the key's own project, signed in the workspace's Studio project, which the Workflow Agent shares with Studio. title is "Workflow Agent".

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/Send

Sends a message to the Workflow Agent and returns at once with the turn's messageguid and agenttoken.

Parameter Type Required Description
message string Yes The brief, at most 16 KB (UTF-8). Say what the workflow should do, what people will give it as input and which results they want back. Pass on limits such as budget, speed, quality or a model.
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default", the project's main session.
model string No The chat model for this turn: a slug whose selectable is true in StudioWorkflow/Status. Leave it out to use the default chat model, agentModel.chatModel. A chat model your Model Access rules block is refused with code 92, the default included.
workflowContext object No A workflow for the agent to edit, at most 40 KB of JSON. See Editing a workflow.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messageguid": "0b7f2c1e-5d4a-4c3b-9a8f-1e2d3c4b5a69",
  "agenttoken": "Qm7Tz2LpX9vKc4RwN8yHa3JdF6sGb1",
  "status": "agent_queue"
}

If a request times out, check Message/History before you send it again: each accepted message starts a paid turn.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/SendForm

The same as Send, as multipart/form-data, to attach files such as a sample image or a brief as a PDF.

Parameter Type Required Description
message string Conditional The brief, at most 16 KB. Required unless a file is attached.
sessionkey string No The session.
model string No As in Send.
workflowContext string No The same object as in Send, as a JSON string.
attachments file No Repeat the attachments field once per file; a single file can also be sent as attachment.

Up to 8 files per message, each up to 50 MB (File too large (max 50MB): <name>). The accepted types are the same as for Studio.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/Detail

Returns one message and its reply.

Parameter Type Required Description
messageguid string Conditional The message id. Required unless agenttoken is given.
agenttoken string Conditional The turn token.
sessionkey string No The message's session. Defaults to "default". A message from another session or another project is Message not found.

The reply fields are those of Studio's Message/Detail: status, content, response, debugoutput, timeline, attachments, model, the token counts, tokencost, createdat, startedat and endedat, plus sessionkey. The proposals are in response once status is agent_end.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/History

Returns the messages of one session, newest first: sessionkey, limit (default 50, maximum 200) and before (a message guid, for the next page). The response is { "data": { "messages": [...], "count": 2, "hasmore": false } }. A proposal in an earlier reply can still be saved later.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/Sessions

Lists the sessions of the key's project, most recent first, each with sessionkey, messagecount, updatedat, lastmessage and an optional name. "default" is always listed. It takes no request fields.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/Cancel

Stops a turn that is queued or running (messageguid or agenttoken, and sessionkey). Only a message in agent_queue, agent_start or agent_output can be cancelled. Tokens the turn already used are charged.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/ClearSession

Deletes the session's messages and starts the agent's memory of it fresh. The session keeps its display name. It works on "default" too.

Parameter Type Required Description
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default".

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/DeleteSession

Deletes a session: its messages, its display name and the agent's memory of it. Send the sessionkey of the session to delete; "default" cannot be deleted (The main session cannot be deleted.), so clear it with ClearSession. Workflows you saved are not affected.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Message/RenameSession

Sets a session's display name: name (required, up to 40 characters) and sessionkey.

POST /StudioWorkflow/Transactions

Lists your Workflow Agent charges in the key's workspace, newest first (limit, default 50, maximum 200). Each row has guid, type, amount, description, modelid, taskid, confirmed and time; a chat charge is described as Workflow Agent LLM <model> (...) with its token counts.

Editing a workflow

To have the agent change a workflow, read it with Workflow/Detail and send it with the message as workflowContext:

{
  "message": "Add an upscale step after the image and return both images",
  "sessionkey": "product-ad-edit",
  "workflowContext": {
    "protocolVersion": 1,
    "source": {
      "slug": "product-ad",
      "slugid": "a1B2c",
      "fullSlug": "product-ad-a1B2c",
      "title": "Product ad",
      "description": "Turns a product photo into a short ad video",
      "updatetime": "1761901200",
      "workspace": "personal"
    },
    "contents": { "version": "1", "nodes": { "...": "..." }, "output": {}, "schema": { "input": {}, "output": {} }, "metadata": { "input": { "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 } } } }
  }
}
  • contents is the workflow's graph, as Workflow/Detail returns it (see The Workflow Graph). You can also send the graph alone, without protocolVersion and source.
  • source names the workflow: slug, slugid, fullSlug, title (up to 300 characters), updatetime and workspace ("personal" or "team") are required, and description (up to 2,000 characters) is optional.
  • The whole workflowContext can be at most 40 KB of JSON (workflowContext exceeds the 40KB limit.). Attach a workflow from the key's workspace; a protected workflow whose graph is hidden cannot be edited this way.
  • The agent sees the steps, the Start fields and the End node, never the values saved for the Start fields. Keep keys and passwords out of workflows. Some values reach the agent as "[REDACTED]"; restore them before you save (see Saving a proposal).

Proposals

The reply in response is text. Each proposed workflow is a fenced block that opens with a line ```wiro-workflow and closes with a line ```; the text around the blocks is the explanation. Each block holds one JSON object:

{
  "artifactVersion": 1,
  "title": "Product ad with upscale",
  "description": "Turns a product photo into an upscaled image and a short ad video",
  "contents": { "version": "1", "nodes": { "...": "..." }, "output": {}, "schema": { "input": {}, "output": {} }, "metadata": { "input": { "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 } } } }
}
  • title is 1 to 160 characters and description up to 1,000. contents is a workflow graph.
  • A block can be at most 40 KB. A block that is not closed yet is still being written: read the reply again once status is agent_end.
  • A reply can hold zero, one or several proposals. If the request cannot be built with current models, the agent explains why and proposes nothing. When it needs to know more, it asks; send the answer in the same session.
  • Check a proposal before you save it: Workflow/Prepare lists every problem it finds. Send problems back in the same session and ask for a corrected version.
  • Treat the explanation as information from a model, not as instructions to your application.

The agent can also ask your application for the user's workflows, in a block that opens with ```wiro-workflow-request:

{ "protocolVersion": 1, "requestId": "list-1", "operation": "workflow.list", "args": { "search": "product", "limit": 10 } }

Run it yourself with Workflow/List (scope my), let the user pick a workflow, and attach that workflow to your next message as workflowContext. The list is not sent back to the agent on its own.

Saving a proposal

  1. Read the reply again with Message/Detail and take the proposal's contents from its block.
  2. Prepare it with Workflow/Prepare: mode "create" for a new workflow, "apply" when it replaces an existing graph. Prepare fills the defaults the Wiro editor would and returns every problem at once.
  3. Save the prepared graph as a new workflow with Workflow/Add, or onto the workflow you attached with Workflow/Update. Pass the updatetime you attached as loadedUpdatetime, so a change someone saved in the meantime is not overwritten. Values the agent saw as "[REDACTED]" must be restored from the original workflow first.

Saving creates or changes a workflow and runs nothing. Applying a proposal to a published workflow sends it back to review.

Errors

Business errors come back with HTTP 200, result: false and an errors array. These are the ones specific to the Workflow Agent:

Message Code When
Insufficient balance 97 Send or SendForm with less than $10 spendable. The response adds walletUsd and minTopup.
A spend limit refusal, such as Your monthly spend limit is reached ($100.40 of $100.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC. 93 Send or SendForm while a spend limit that covers the message is used up. Nothing is charged.
A Model Access refusal, such as This team can't use openai/gpt-5-6-terra. Model Access rules decide which models can run. 92 Send or SendForm when a Model Access rule that covers the message blocks its chat model: the model it names, or the default chat model when it names none. It is checked before the balance and the spend limits. Nothing is sent or charged.
Request parameter [message] required 0 No message, and no file on SendForm.
message exceeds the 16KB limit. 0 The message is longer than 16 KB.
sessionkey has invalid format 0 A session name with other characters, :cron:, or more than 100 characters.
workflowContext exceeds the 40KB limit. 0 The attached workflow is too large.
workflowContext must be a WorkflowContents object., workflowContext must be valid JSON data., workflowContext protocolVersion must be 1., workflowContext source has an invalid shape., workflowContext has an invalid WorkflowContents shape. 0 The workflowContext does not have the shape described above.
This project already has 2 Workflow Agent replies in progress. Wait for one to finish before sending another message. 0 A third turn while two of the project's turns are queued or running.
Invalid model: <model> is not in the selectable model allowlist. 0 model is not one of the chat models the Workflow Agent offers. A model your Model Access rules block gets code 92 instead.
Too many files (max 8), File too large (max 50MB): <name> 0 SendForm attachment limits.
Message not found 0 Detail or Cancel with an unknown message, or one from another session or project.
The main session cannot be deleted. 0 DeleteSession on "default".
Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly. 0 Try again shortly.
You must be a member of this team to perform this action HTTP 403 A team project's key whose creator is no longer a member of the team.

Authentication errors are listed in the Error Reference.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Studio

Ask Wiro's creative agent for images, video, audio and more through the API, then collect every result it made.

Overview

Studio is Wiro's creative agent. You describe what you want, such as a product shot, a short video, a voice-over or a set of ad banners, and Studio picks suitable models from the Wiro catalog, runs them and replies with the results. It is the same Studio you use on wiro.ai.

The Studio API uses the message protocol of Agent Messaging on its own routes under /Studio/:

  1. Send a message with Message/Send and get its messageguid and agenttoken back at once.
  2. Follow the turn on the Agent WebSocket with the agenttoken, or poll Message/Detail until the turn ends.
  3. Collect the files. The reply lists them, and Studio/Tasks returns every model run Studio started for you, with its outputs and cost.

There is no agent guid to pass: every route talks to Studio. Studio is paid from your Wiro wallet, as described under Costs.

Studio runs on one setup shared by everyone who uses it, so it never changes that setup: it proposes no setup cards, and its connectors, skills and scheduled tasks are fixed. Asked to remember a rule or to repeat a job on a schedule, it helps with the request once, as a one-time task.

Authentication

Every /Studio/* route takes a project API key: x-api-key, plus x-nonce and x-signature for a project that uses signature authentication (see Authentication). A key acts as the person who created its project, in that project's workspace: a personal project works in the personal workspace and pays from the personal wallet, a team project works in the team and pays from the team wallet. For a team project, that person must still be a member of the team; otherwise every route answers HTTP 403 with You must be a member of this team to perform this action. The one exception is ProjectSet, which works only signed in.

Sessions

A session is one conversation with its own memory. sessionkey names it, and "default" is used when you leave it out.

  • Studio conversations belong to the person who created the key's project. "default" is their main Studio chat on wiro.ai, and sessions started with a key appear in their Studio on wiro.ai, in the same workspace. Everyone who uses the same key shares these sessions.
  • Use a new session name for each piece of work, such as "bakery-banners", and keep using it for follow-ups such as "make it brighter": Studio remembers the conversation.
  • A name uses letters, digits, ., _, : and -, up to 128 characters, and can't end in -r followed by a number, such as -r2. Names that contain :cron: are reserved.
  • Capitals are fine and are kept, but a new name that differs only in capitals from one of your sessions is refused: use its exact name, or another name.
  • Message/Send and Message/SendForm check the name first, so a refused message runs nothing and costs nothing. Reading, renaming and deleting a session work with whatever name it already has.
  • The turns of one session run one at a time, in order: a second message waits in agent_queue until the turn before it ends. Different sessions run in parallel.

Costs

  • $10 to start a turn. Message/Send and Message/SendForm need at least $10 spendable in the wallet of the key's workspace. Below that, the message is refused with code 97 (Insufficient balance), and the response carries walletUsd, the balance, and minTopup, the minimum. Nothing is charged for a refused message. Reading messages, sessions and results is free.
  • What a turn costs. A turn's cost depends on the models Studio runs for it, and can be more than $10.
  • Project. Studio works on a project of the workspace. A call with an API key runs on that key's project. Work sent from wiro.ai runs on the workspace's Studio project: one for a personal workspace and one for each team, shared by Studio and the Workflow Agent. The first Studio or Workflow Agent message sent from wiro.ai in a workspace that has none creates a project named "Studio" there, or uses the workspace's existing project of that name. It is a normal project: like any project you create, it gets an API key, and you get the email that comes with a new key. Studio/Status shows it, and Studio/ProjectSet changes it.
  • Chat. Each turn is charged for the tokens it used, at the chat model's rates in Studio/Status (cents per 1M tokens), on the turn's project and the studio surface. The reply shows the chat charge in tokencost, in cents: tokencost / 100 is the amount in USD.
  • Model runs. The models Studio runs for you are your own tasks, on the turn's project: Task/List and Task/Detail return them with surface studio, and Studio/Tasks lists them too. Each is charged like any model run when it finishes: at the model's price when it succeeds, and not at all when it fails or is cancelled. Studio/Tasks shows each run's totalcost.
  • Spend limits and Model Access. The models Studio runs for you follow your workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules, the same as the runs you start yourself: the account's or the team's, your own in a team, those of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the Studio project for a message sent from wiro.ai), and those of the studio surface. So does the chat: what it costs counts toward spend limits, and a message whose chat model a Model Access rule blocks is refused with code 92 before anything runs.
  • Chat charges are made within about a minute of the turn ending, and model runs are charged when they finish, like any model run. Both appear in the wallet's transactions, and Studio/Transactions lists the chat charges.

POST /Studio/Status

Returns the wallet check, the chat models Studio can use and the project Studio works on. It settles your pending Studio charges first, so walletUsd is current. It takes no request fields.

Field Type Description
walletUsd number Spendable balance of the workspace wallet in USD.
needsTopup boolean true when walletUsd is below minTopup.
minTopup number The balance a turn needs to start: 10.
tokenRates object Chat model rates. default_model is the default chat model, and models is keyed by model slug: each entry has input_per_1m and output_per_1m (cents per 1M tokens), optional cached-input, cache-write and long-context rates, a label, and selectable: true when you can pick it with model. A model you could pick that your Model Access rules block reads selectable: false and blocked: true.
agentModel.chatModel string The chat model a turn uses when you leave model out.
blockedModels string[] The chat models you could pick that your Model Access rules block. [] when none is blocked.
agentModelBlocked boolean true when your rules block agentModel.chatModel: a message that leaves model out is then refused with code 92.
agentModelMessage string | null The refusal such a message gets when agentModelBlocked is true, else null.
project.current object | null The project Studio works on, { "id", "name" } with id as a string (see Costs). With an API key, the key's own project. Signed in, the workspace's Studio project, or null until the workspace has one: the first Studio or Workflow Agent message from wiro.ai creates it.
project.options object[] The projects you can make the Studio project with ProjectSet, each { "id", "name" }. Signed in to a personal workspace, your personal projects; in a team, every team project for a team admin or the organization owner, and none for other members. Always [] with an API key.
project.canchange boolean true when you can change the Studio project. false for team members who are not admins, and with an API key.
title string The agent's name.
status number Always 4.

The response also carries fields that Wiro's own apps use. Ignore the ones not listed here.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "title": "Generative Media Agent",
  "status": 4,
  "walletUsd": 42.5,
  "needsTopup": false,
  "minTopup": 10,
  "tokenRates": {
    "default_model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "models": {
      "openai/gpt-5.6-sol": {
        "input_per_1m": 625,
        "output_per_1m": 3750,
        "cached_input_per_1m": 62.5,
        "selectable": true,
        "label": "GPT-5.6 Sol"
      },
      "openai/gpt-5.4-mini": {
        "input_per_1m": 93.75,
        "output_per_1m": 562.5,
        "cached_input_per_1m": 9.375,
        "selectable": true,
        "label": "GPT-5.4 Mini"
      }
    }
  },
  "agentModel": {
    "chatModel": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"
  },
  "blockedModels": [],
  "agentModelBlocked": false,
  "agentModelMessage": null,
  "project": {
    "current": { "id": "48211", "name": "Production" },
    "options": [],
    "canchange": false
  }
}

This call was made with the API key of the Production project, so project.current is that project, project.options is empty and project.canchange is false: the key's turns always run on its own project.

When a rule blocks a chat model, Status says so. With a team rule that blocks openai/gpt-5-6-sol, Studio's default chat model, these fields read:

{
  "tokenRates": {
    "default_model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "models": {
      "openai/gpt-5.6-sol": {
        "input_per_1m": 625,
        "output_per_1m": 3750,
        "cached_input_per_1m": 62.5,
        "selectable": false,
        "label": "GPT-5.6 Sol",
        "blocked": true
      },
      "openai/gpt-5.4-mini": {
        "input_per_1m": 93.75,
        "output_per_1m": 562.5,
        "cached_input_per_1m": 9.375,
        "selectable": true,
        "label": "GPT-5.4 Mini"
      }
    }
  },
  "agentModel": {
    "chatModel": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"
  },
  "blockedModels": ["openai/gpt-5.6-sol"],
  "agentModelBlocked": true,
  "agentModelMessage": "This team can't use openai/gpt-5-6-sol. Model Access rules decide which models can run."
}

A message that leaves model out is then refused with agentModelMessage. Send a model that is still selectable, such as openai/gpt-5.4-mini.

POST /Studio/ProjectSet

Changes the workspace's Studio project: the project that Studio and the Workflow Agent work on for messages sent from wiro.ai. It works only signed in, in the dashboard or with a signed-in user's Bearer token, and changes your personal workspace's Studio project, or the team's when x-team-guid names a team. In a personal workspace you can pick any of your personal projects; in a team, a team admin or the organization owner can pick any team project. project.options in Studio/Status lists them. A call with an API key always runs on the key's project, so ProjectSet refuses it.

Parameter Type Required Description
projectid string Yes The project's id, from project.options in Studio/Status.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "project": { "id": "7001", "name": "Mobile App" }
}

Studio/Status then shows the new project. For a team admin, signed in, it reads:

{
  "project": {
    "current": { "id": "7001", "name": "Mobile App" },
    "options": [
      { "id": "6839", "name": "Studio" },
      { "id": "7001", "name": "Mobile App" }
    ],
    "canchange": true
  }
}

A refusal comes back with result: false and code 0:

Message When
Studio runs on your API key's project. Change the Studio project on wiro.ai. The call was made with an API key.
Only a team admin can change the team's Studio project. In a team, the caller is a member who is not a team admin.
Project not found in this workspace. projectid is not a project of this workspace.

POST /Studio/Message/Send

Sends a message to Studio. It returns at once with the turn's messageguid and agenttoken; the reply arrives on the WebSocket and in Message/Detail.

Parameter Type Required Description
message string Yes Your request, as you would type it in Studio. Say what the result is for, the look (subject, style, format or aspect ratio, length for video and audio) and how many results you want. Quote any exact text that must appear in an image or be spoken.
sessionkey string No The session to send to. Defaults to "default", the main Studio chat.
model string No The chat model for this turn: a slug whose selectable is true in Studio/Status. Leave it out to use Studio's default chat model, agentModel.chatModel. A chat model your Model Access rules block is refused with code 92, the default included. Use the same model on every turn of a session; when it differs from the previous turn, the response includes modelChangeMarker, as in Agent Messaging.

To attach files, use Message/SendForm.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messageguid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
  "agenttoken": "aB3xK9mR2pLqWzVn7tYhCd5sFgJkNb",
  "status": "agent_queue"
}

A wallet below the minimum gets:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 97, "message": "Insufficient balance", "time": 1761902400 }],
  "walletUsd": 6.4,
  "minTopup": 10
}

A message whose chat model a Model Access rule blocks gets code 92, and nothing is sent or charged:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 92, "message": "This team can't use openai/gpt-5-6-terra. Model Access rules decide which models can run.", "time": 1761902400 }]
}

If a request times out, check Message/History before you send it again: each accepted message starts a paid turn.

POST /Studio/Message/SendForm

The same as Message/Send, as multipart/form-data, so you can attach files such as a product photo or a logo.

Parameter Type Required Description
message string Conditional Your request. Required unless at least one file is attached.
sessionkey string No The session to send to. Defaults to "default".
model string No As in Send.
attachments file No The files. Repeat the attachments field once per file; a single file can also be sent as attachment.
  • Up to 8 files per message, each up to about 100 MB. A larger file is refused with HTTP 413.
  • Accepted: images (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, heic, svg), video (mp4, webm, mov), audio (mp3, wav, m4a, webm) and documents (pdf, txt, md, csv, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, epub). The file name needs its extension. Other files are refused with Uploaded file format invalid. Supported: ....
  • The message's attachments then lists each file with ordinal, mentionLabel, url, name, type and size.

The response is the same as Send's.

POST /Studio/Message/Detail

Returns one message and its reply. Poll it until status is agent_end, agent_error or agent_cancel, or follow the turn on the Agent WebSocket.

Parameter Type Required Description
messageguid string Conditional The message id from Send. Required unless agenttoken is given.
agenttoken string Conditional The turn token from Send.
sessionkey string No The message's session. Defaults to "default". A message from another session is Message not found.

Reply fields

Field Description
status agent_queue, agent_start, agent_output, then agent_end; or agent_error or agent_cancel.
content Your message.
response The final reply, set when the turn ends. Each file Studio made is on its own line as a public URL. After agent_error or agent_cancel it holds a coded failure message, such as [AGENT_UNAVAILABLE] Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly. (see Failed turns).
debugoutput The reply text so far while the turn runs, the final text after.
timeline The ordered reasoning, answer and tool blocks of the turn, as described in Agent Messaging. Tool labels are display names: show them, but do not parse them.
attachments The files you attached.
model The chat model that ran the turn.
inputtokens, outputtokens, cachereadtokens, cachewritetokens, totaltokens The turn's token use.
tokencost The chat charge in cents; tokencost / 100 is the amount in USD. Model runs are charged separately (see Studio/Tasks).
createdat, startedat, endedat Unix seconds.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "data": {
    "guid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
    "agenttoken": "aB3xK9mR2pLqWzVn7tYhCd5sFgJkNb",
    "content": "Two square banner images for my bakery's weekend sale, warm colors",
    "response": "Here are your two banners.\nhttps://cdn1.wiro.ai/7f3a9c2e/banner-1.png\nhttps://cdn1.wiro.ai/7f3a9c2e/banner-2.png",
    "debugoutput": "Here are your two banners.\nhttps://cdn1.wiro.ai/7f3a9c2e/banner-1.png\nhttps://cdn1.wiro.ai/7f3a9c2e/banner-2.png",
    "status": "agent_end",
    "metadata": {},
    "createdat": "1761902400",
    "startedat": "1761902401",
    "endedat": "1761902466",
    "attachments": [],
    "timeline": [],
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol",
    "inputtokens": 6400,
    "outputtokens": 610,
    "cachereadtokens": 0,
    "cachewritetokens": 0,
    "totaltokens": 7010,
    "tokencost": 7
  }
}

In this example the chat part cost 7 cents ($0.07). The two images are charged separately, as the model runs Studio started.

POST /Studio/Message/History

Returns the messages of one session, newest first.

Parameter Type Required Description
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default".
limit number No Messages per page. Default 50, maximum 200.
before string No A message guid: returns the messages older than it, for the next page.

The response is { "result": true, "errors": [], "data": { "messages": [...], "count": 2, "hasmore": false } }. Each message has the reply fields of Message/Detail except startedat and endedat.

When a turn hands work to the background, its reply says so and ends early. The result arrives later as a new message in the same session, already finished: status is agent_end, content is empty and the text is in response. Read it with History, and find the files in Studio/Tasks.

POST /Studio/Message/Sessions

Lists your Studio sessions in the key's workspace, most recent first, including those started on wiro.ai. It takes no request fields.

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "data": {
    "sessions": [
      {
        "sessionkey": "bakery-banners",
        "messagecount": 3,
        "updatedat": 1761902466,
        "lastmessage": "Make the second one brighter",
        "name": "Bakery banners"
      },
      {
        "sessionkey": "default",
        "messagecount": 0,
        "updatedat": null,
        "lastmessage": ""
      }
    ]
  }
}

messagecount counts turns, lastmessage is the last message (up to 500 characters), and name is the display name set with Message/RenameSession. "default" is always listed.

POST /Studio/Message/Cancel

Stops a turn that is queued or running.

Parameter Type Required Description
messageguid string Conditional The message id. Required unless agenttoken is given.
agenttoken string Conditional The turn token.
sessionkey string No The message's session. Defaults to "default".

Only a message in agent_queue, agent_start or agent_output can be cancelled; any other is refused with Message cannot be cancelled (status: <status>). Cancelling stops the reply, and the message moves to agent_cancel. Tokens already used are charged, and model runs that already started are billed when they succeed.

POST /Studio/Message/ClearSession

Deletes your messages in a session and starts Studio's memory of it fresh. The session keeps its display name.

Parameter Type Required Description
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default", the main Studio chat.

Pending charges are settled first. Deleted messages cannot be restored, and they disappear from Studio on wiro.ai too. Files Studio made are not deleted.

POST /Studio/Message/DeleteSession

Deletes a session's messages and its display name.

Parameter Type Required Description
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default".

To start a session over with a fresh memory, use Message/ClearSession.

POST /Studio/Message/RenameSession

Sets a session's display name, the name shown in the session list on wiro.ai.

Parameter Type Required Description
name string Yes The display name, up to 40 characters.
sessionkey string No The session. Defaults to "default".

POST /Studio/Tasks

Lists the model runs Studio started for you in the key's workspace, newest first, across all your Studio sessions, including those on wiro.ai.

Parameter Type Required Description
limit number No How many recent runs to return. Default 30, maximum 100.
Field Description
id The run's id.
status The task status, such as task_queue, task_start, task_postprocess_end or task_cancel (see Tasks).
success true for a run that finished successfully, false for a failed or cancelled run, null while it runs.
terminal true once the run has finished.
model { title, slugowner, slugproject }.
categories The model's categories. llm marks a text run.
parameters The inputs the run used, such as its prompt.
outputs The result files, each with name, contenttype, size and url. An LLM run returns its text as { "contenttype": "raw", "content": { "answer": [...] } }.
totalcost The run's price in USD, charged when it succeeds.
socketaccesstoken While the run is active, a token for the task WebSocket; empty once it finished.
createtime, starttime, endtime Unix seconds.
elapsedseconds How long the run took.

Response

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": "48211907",
      "status": "task_postprocess_end",
      "success": true,
      "terminal": true,
      "model": {
        "title": "Nano Banana Pro API: Create Mobile & Web Apps with Nano Banana",
        "slugowner": "google",
        "slugproject": "nano-banana-pro"
      },
      "categories": ["text-to-image", "image-to-image", "image-editing"],
      "parameters": { "prompt": "Square banner for a bakery weekend sale, warm colors", "resolution": "2K" },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "banner-1.png",
          "contenttype": "image/png",
          "size": "1843212",
          "url": "https://cdn1.wiro.ai/7f3a9c2e/banner-1.png"
        }
      ],
      "totalcost": 0.14,
      "socketaccesstoken": "",
      "createtime": "1761902420",
      "starttime": "1761902421",
      "endtime": "1761902452",
      "elapsedseconds": 31
    }
  ]
}

Delete a finished run's files with Studio/Task/DeleteOutput.

POST /Studio/Transactions

Lists the wallet charges for your Studio use in the key's workspace, newest first.

Parameter Type Required Description
limit number No Default 50, maximum 200.

Each row has guid, type, amount, description, modelid, taskid, confirmed and time. A chat charge is described as Generative Media Agent LLM <model> (...) with its token counts. A model run from before Studio's runs became your own tasks is described as Generative Media Agent media run; the model runs since then are charged on their own tasks, like any model run (see Costs).

POST /Studio/Task/DeleteOutput

Deletes the output and input files of one of your Studio runs once it has finished or was cancelled.

Parameter Type Required Description
id string Yes The run's id from Studio/Tasks.

A run that is not yours answers There is no task yet., and a run that has not finished answers Task must be completed or cancelled before deleting files.

Errors

Business errors come back with HTTP 200, result: false and an errors array, as everywhere in the Wiro API. These are the ones specific to Studio:

Message Code When
Insufficient balance 97 Send or SendForm with less than $10 spendable. The response adds walletUsd and minTopup.
A spend limit refusal, such as Your monthly spend limit is reached ($100.40 of $100.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC. 93 Send or SendForm while a spend limit that covers the message is used up. Nothing is charged.
A Model Access refusal, such as This team can't use openai/gpt-5-6-terra. Model Access rules decide which models can run. 92 Send or SendForm when a Model Access rule that covers the message blocks its chat model: the model it names, or the default chat model when it names none. It is checked before the balance and the spend limits. Nothing is sent or charged.
Request parameter [message] required 0 Send without a message, or SendForm with neither a message nor a file.
Invalid model: <model> is not in the selectable model allowlist. 0 model is not one of the chat models Studio offers. A model your Model Access rules block gets code 92 instead.
A Studio session name may contain only letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" and "-", at most 128 characters, and cannot end in "-r" followed by a number. Nothing was sent or charged. 0 Send or SendForm with a session name outside that rule.
You already have a Studio session with this name in different capitals. Use its exact name, or another name. Nothing was sent or charged. 0 Send or SendForm with a new session name that differs only in capitals from one of your sessions.
Reserved sessionkey 0 The session name contains :cron:.
Too many files (max 8) 0 SendForm with more than 8 files.
Uploaded file format invalid. Supported: ... 0 An attachment type that is not accepted.
Message not found 0 Detail or Cancel with an unknown message, or one from another session.
Message cannot be cancelled (status: <status>) 0 Cancel on a turn that has already ended.
Studio runs on your API key's project. Change the Studio project on wiro.ai. 0 ProjectSet with an API key.
Only a team admin can change the team's Studio project. 0 ProjectSet in a team by a member who is not a team admin.
Project not found in this workspace. 0 ProjectSet with a projectid that is not a project of this workspace.
Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly. 0 Try again shortly.
You must be a member of this team to perform this action HTTP 403 A team project's key whose creator is no longer a member of the team.

Authentication errors are listed in the Error Reference.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Agent Overview

Deploy and manage autonomous AI agents through a single API.

Wiro Agents on the Web

The endpoints below cover the full programmatic surface. If you also want to see the web product alongside what you're building (landing pages, marketing copy, the visual catalog, and the no-code Build Your Own Agent flow), these are the public Wiro pages dedicated to agents:

Page URL What it covers
AI Agents Home wiro.ai/agents Top-level landing: what Wiro Agents are, how they compare to traditional setups, and a featured selection from the marketplace.
Learn About Agents wiro.ai/agents/learn Concept primer: security model, deployment lifecycle, and the difference between marketplace templates and custom builds.
Anatomy of an Agent wiro.ai/agents/anatomy Fullscreen interactive walkthrough of the pieces that make a Wiro agent reason: system prompt, knowledge, skills, memory, guardrails, model, tools, scheduling, and observability.
Build Your Own Agent wiro.ai/agents/build The web wizard for the same custom-build flow exposed by POST /UserAgent/Deploy with custom: true. Useful for previewing the skill picker and the three plans before scripting it.
Browse Agents wiro.ai/agents/browse Full marketplace catalog with categories, descriptions and screenshots, the visual mirror of POST /Agent/List. Each row links to a dedicated agent page at /agents/{slug}.
Use Case Showcases wiro.ai/agents/usecase/... Seven fullscreen, auto-looping product stories that show real businesses operated end-to-end by a Wiro agent. See Agent Use Cases for the full list.

All pages are public: no Wiro account required to browse. Sign-in becomes mandatory only when you click "Deploy" on a specific agent (which then drops you into the Wiro dashboard at wiro.ai/panel/agents).

What are Wiro Agents?

Wiro Agents are autonomous AI assistants that keep running on Wiro. Unlike one-shot model runs, agents maintain conversation memory, connect to external services, and use tools to complete tasks on your behalf, all managed through the API.

The system has two layers:

  • Agent templates (the catalog): Pre-built agent definitions published by Wiro. Each template defines the agent's default skill set and required credentials, and runs on any of the three plans. Browse the catalog with POST /Agent/List.
  • UserAgent instances (your deployments): When you deploy an agent template (or build a custom one), Wiro creates a personal instance tied to your account. Each instance runs in its own isolated environment with its own credentials, configuration, conversation history, billing, and per-model token-rate profile, and its own computer in the cloud with a web browser the agent works in. The people who manage the agent can watch that computer from the Wiro panel, and an app built on the API can show it to its own users (see Screen and Take Control).

Every instance is fully isolated. Your credentials, conversations, and data are never shared with other users.

Two deploy paths. You can deploy a marketplace template by passing agentguid, or build a custom agent from scratch with custom: true (no template: you pick the skill set yourself). Both flows are documented under POST /UserAgent/Deploy. The custom builder is detailed in Agent Builder.

Base URL

https://api.wiro.ai/v1

Authentication

Agents use the same authentication as the rest of the Wiro API. Include your key in every request:

Method Header
API Key x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
Bearer Token Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Public endpoints: Agent/List, Agent/Detail, Skills/List, Skills/Detail, Skills/CredentialSchema, Skills/Capabilities, Credentials/List, Credentials/Detail, AgentConnector/List, and AgentConnector/Detail are catalog endpoints and do not require authentication. You can browse available agents, the skill registry, the credential schema, and the connector catalog without an API key.

Authenticated endpoints: All UserAgent/* endpoints require a valid API key.

For full details, see Authentication.

Pricing Model: Plans, AI Usage & Balance

Every agent runs on one of three monthly plans, and the plan alone sets its price, the AI usage it includes and its disk space. Templates and custom builds use the same plans, and the skills an agent has never change the price. AI usage is what the agent's own model uses on each turn, priced by its tokens. Once the plan's included usage for the period is used up, the agent runs on the Wiro balance of its workspace, the same balance your model runs use.

Plans

Plan tier Price AI usage included Disk
Starter "starter" $5 a month $5 a month 250 MB
Pro "pro" $30 a month $30 a month 500 MB
Max "max" $100 a month $100 a month 1 GB

Each plan includes its own price in AI usage: Pro costs $30 a month and includes $30 of AI usage a month. A plan is bought per agent and paid from the Wiro balance: pass tier to Deploy or CreateSubscriptionCheckout. Catalog responses, instance responses (agent.plans) and PricingPreview list the three plans in order under plans:

"plans": [
  { "key": "starter", "title": "Starter", "priceUsd": 5,   "includedUsageUsd": 5,   "diskMb": 250 },
  { "key": "pro",     "title": "Pro",     "priceUsd": 30,  "includedUsageUsd": 30,  "diskMb": 500 },
