Agent Credentials

The values an agent keeps as credentials: its Telegram, Slack and Discord channels, its Twilio Voice phone line, the Wiro project it runs models with, and settings such as its support email and website. Read the credential registry, save values and audit their history. Connectors to outside services are on Agent Connectors.

Overview

A credential is a set of values an agent keeps for something it is, rather than a service it works with:

Credential Key What it is
Telegram, Slack, Discord telegram, slack, discord The agent's own external chat channels. See Communication Channels.
Twilio Voice twilio-voice The phone line the agent answers. See Twilio Voice Channel.
Wiro project wiro The project whose wallet pays for the Wiro model runs the agent makes, such as video and voice. See The agent's Wiro project.
Settings var-support-email, var-website, var-newsletter-test-email Values the agent's skills read: the support email it gives customers, its website addresses, and the inbox that gets a test copy of each newsletter before it goes out.

The services an agent works with (Google Ads, Shopify, HubSpot, Serper and the rest) are connectors, not credentials: browse, connect and disconnect them with the calls on Agent Connectors. CredentialUpsert doesn't take a connector's values.

Not from the agent's chat. Setup cards connect connectors of the catalog only: no card saves a channel, Twilio Voice or a setting. Save them with CredentialUpsert; in chat, the agent asks an agent admin to make the change in the agent's settings. The one card that sets a credential is the wiro connector's project card: it binds the agent's Wiro project, as CredentialProjectBind does.

Read & write paths at a glance:

Operation Endpoint
Browse every credential in the registry POST /Credentials/List (public)
Inspect a single credential schema POST /Credentials/Detail (public)
Find the credential a skill needs POST /Skills/CredentialSchema (public)
Write one or more credential fields POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert
Connect the agent's Wiro project by its id POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind
Discover external communication channels POST /Skills/List → channels[] (public)
Connect or disable an external channel POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert
Read version history of a credential POST /UserAgent/CredentialFieldHistory
Connect a service the agent works with Agent Connectors

Read responses from POST /UserAgent/Detail expose the composed credentials tree (each credential with its _connected / optional / extra / _editable / _schema flags), the customskills[] array, the scheduledskills[] array (scheduled tasks), the skills[] array of enabled skill names, the tokenRates + agentModel objects, and the agent's AI usage and balance (usage) and this month's cost (spend) as top-level fields on the useragent object. POST /UserAgent/MyAgents rows carry tokenRates, agentModel, usage and spend, without the composed children. See Agent Overview for the full endpoint catalog.

Communication Channels

Every Wiro agent is reachable through web chat and the Agent Messaging API without additional configuration. Telegram, Slack, and Discord are optional external channels. They are available to every marketplace template and custom agent, but remain disabled until every registry-declared activation credential is complete. There is no separate enable switch on an existing agent.

Channels are not skills and do not affect pricing. Discover them from the top-level channels[] array returned by public POST /Skills/List:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/Skills/List" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'

Each row contains:

Field Description
id Channel identifier (telegram, slack, or discord).
credential_key Key used inside the credentials object.
required_fields Fields that must all be populated for automatic activation.
capabilities Public UI hints for direct messages, rooms, threads, role allowlists, and command menus.
credential Full form descriptor, including credential_schema, labels, validation patterns, and setup help.

POST /UserAgent/Detail, POST /UserAgent/Update and POST /UserAgent/Deploy return the same channels with this agent's state in communicationChannels: enabled, configured and missingfields.

Use POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert for an existing useragent. Send all activation fields in one fields[] request when connecting a channel:

{
  "useragentguid": "your-useragent-guid",
  "fields": [
    {
      "credentialkey": "telegram",
      "fieldname": "bottoken",
      "fieldvalue": "123456:ABC-DEF..."
    },
    {
      "credentialkey": "telegram",
      "fieldname": "allowedusers",
      "fieldvalue": ["123456789"]
    },
    {
      "credentialkey": "telegram",
      "fieldname": "groups",
      "fieldvalue": [
        {
          "chatid": "-1001234567890",
          "allowedusers": ["123456789"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

For a new useragent, include the complete channel group in credentials. The channel activates from those credentials; Deploy accepts neither an enabledchannels toggle nor a chat-mode field. Configure Chat Mode after deployment with teamsessionmode in POST /UserAgent/UpdateSettings.

Channel Required fields Optional scoped access
Telegram bottoken, allowedusers[] groups[] rows with negative chatid and room-specific allowedusers[].
Slack bottoken, apptoken, workspaceid, allowedusers[] channels[] rows with immutable channelid and room-specific allowedusers[]. Enable Socket Mode and grant the app token connections:write.
Discord bottoken, allowedusers[] applicationid; guilds[] rows with guildid, channelids[], and optional allowedusers[] / allowedroles[].

teamsessionmode: "private" isolates each approved direct-message operator and each team member's Wiro web-chat history and native agent memory. "collaborative" shares those runtime contexts. Team deployments and transfers default to collaborative; personal deployments and team detachments default to private. Web and external-channel message lists remain separate transports, and room/thread sessions remain scoped to their room.

Send immutable platform IDs only. Display names, usernames, email addresses, and free-form room names are not authorization identifiers. Unlisted users and rooms are rejected, and room messages must mention the bot. To disable a channel, clear at least one of its required_fields with CredentialUpsert. Completing the required fields again reactivates it automatically.

Credential Registry Endpoints

These endpoints are public, so no authentication is required. They return data straight from the credential registry, which is useful when you want to render a credential's form without a deployed useragent (e.g. inside an onboarding wizard).

POST /Credentials/List

Lists every credential in the registry: the channels, Twilio Voice, the Wiro project, the settings, and entries Wiro manages itself. Ignore keys this page doesn't list.

Parameter Type Required Description
credential_mode string No Filter by mode, such as "api_key" (values typed in) or "static" (settings).
Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "total": 14,
  "credentials": [
    {
      "key": "telegram",
      "title": "Telegram",
      "icon": "/images/icons/skills/telegram.svg",
      "brand_color": "#24a1de",
      "brand_text_color": "#ffffff",
      "brand_logo_filter": "brightness(0) invert(1)",
      "docs_url": "integration-telegram-skills",
      "credential_mode": "api_key",
      "channel": {
        "id": "telegram",
        "required_fields": ["bottoken", "allowedusers"],
        "capabilities": { "direct": true, "rooms": true, "threads": true, "roles": false, "command_menu": true }
      },
      "credential_schema": [
        {
          "key": "bottoken",
          "type": "password",
          "label": "Telegram Bot Token",
          "required": true,
          "encrypted": true,
          "show_toggle": true,
          "help": "<ol><li>Open Telegram and start a chat with the official @BotFather account.</li><li>Send /newbot, choose the bot's display name and a username ending in bot.</li><li>Copy the token returned by BotFather.</li></ol>"
        },
        {
          "key": "allowedusers",
          "type": "string-array",
          "label": "Allowed Telegram DM User IDs",
          "required": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

The example shows one entry, shortened. Keys this table doesn't list are for Wiro's own panel: ignore them.

Field Type Description
key string Canonical credential key. Use this in CredentialUpsert.fields[].credentialkey.
title string Display label for the credential's card.
icon string Path or URL to the icon (relative paths absolutized server-side).
brand_color / brand_text_color / brand_logo_filter string|null Colours and CSS filter for rendering the icon, the same shape as on skill registry entries.
docs_url string|null Slug of the page about it on this docs site, when it has one. Frontends prefix it with /docs/.
credential_mode string "api_key" for values typed in (the channels, Twilio Voice, the Wiro project) or "static" for settings.
channel object? Only on the external chat channels: their id, the required_fields that turn them on, and capabilities. See Communication Channels.
credential_schema array<field> Per-field schema describing the credential form. Each entry is a field object (see below).

credential_schema[] field object:

Sub-field Type Description
key string Field name (the fieldname you send to CredentialUpsert).
type string Input type: "text", "password", "email", "number", "textarea", "select", "boolean", "string-array", "object-array", "fileinput" (a public file, written with CredentialFileUpload), or "custom" (such as the Wiro project picker).
label string Display label for the form input.
required boolean Whether the field must be filled before the credential counts as set up.
placeholder string? Placeholder text for the input.
pattern string? Regex the value must satisfy.
maxlength / minlength number? Length constraints.
options array? For type: "select", [{ label, value }] choices.
default string? Default value applied when the user hasn't set anything yet.
help string? HTML help text rendered under the input.
show_toggle boolean? For type: "password", render a "show / hide" toggle.
encrypted boolean? true for a secret: it is stored encrypted and read back as the mask.
item_schema / item_type object? For array-of-object fields: describes the per-entry shape (e.g. Telegram groups[].{chatid, allowedusers}).

fieldstatus. Not part of the registry schema: the server stamps it onto each stored field when it is written. Values you save are user and come back in responses (a secret as the mask). platform fields are Wiro's own: you can't write them, and they never come back.

POST /Credentials/Detail

Returns a single credential entry by key.

Parameter Type Required Description
key string Yes Canonical credential key (e.g. "telegram", "twilio-voice", "wiro").
Response

Returns the same entry as a row from Credentials/List (shortened here):

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "credential": {
    "key": "twilio-voice",
    "title": "Twilio Voice",
    "icon": "/images/icons/skills/twilio.svg",
    "credential_mode": "api_key",
    "credential_schema": [
      { "key": "accountsid", "type": "text", "label": "Account SID", "required": true, "encrypted": true },
      { "key": "authtoken", "type": "password", "label": "Auth Token", "required": true, "encrypted": true },
      { "key": "phonenumbers", "type": "string-array", "label": "Phone numbers", "required": true },
      { "key": "maxcallseconds", "type": "number", "label": "Max call duration (seconds)", "required": false }
    ]
  }
}

Returns { "result": false, "errors": [{ "code": 404, "message": "Credential not found: <key>" }] } if the key is unknown, a connector's key included: a connector is read with POST /AgentConnector/Detail.

The Agent's Wiro Project

The wiro credential is the Wiro project an agent runs Wiro AI models with: the skills that make video or images, and the live audio of its voice calls. Each run is billed to the wallet of the workspace that owns that project (your personal wallet, or the team wallet for a team project).

  • Credential key: wiro
  • Field: apikey (label "Wiro Project"; single field, type custom:wiro-project-picker in the registry; the dashboard renders it as a project picker).
  • No secret to supply. Only the project is needed. Request signing for the agent's own Wiro calls is handled automatically, so there is no apisecret (or similar) field to paste.
  • Setup in the dashboard: open the agent's settings and pick a project, or create one on the Projects page.
  • Setup through the API: take the project's id from POST /Project/List and call POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind. A request made with a project API key can leave projectid out to bind that key's own project:
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "your-useragent-guid",
    "projectid": "your-project-id"
  }'

The response names the project and says what happened to the agent: { "result": true, "errors": [], "applied": 1, "project": { "id": "4821", "name": "Agent models" }, "restart": "scheduled" }. See CredentialProjectBind for every field and error. If you already hold a project's key, POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert with credentialkey wiro and fieldname apikey saves it too.

Don't confuse credentials.wiro.apikey with your operator-level Wiro API key. credentials.wiro.apikey is the project key the agent uses to run Wiro models. The x-api-key header you send to Wiro endpoints from your own backend is your operator key, which authenticates your request (see Authentication). They are the same key only when you bind the project of the key you call with.

The Wiro connector, which gives the agent Wiro's own model and task tools, always acts with this project, as the agent's own calls. Connecting it binds the project you pick, as CredentialProjectBind does, and moving the agent to a workspace the project isn't in disconnects both the project and the connector.

Platform-Managed Credentials

Some credential fields are managed by Wiro. You don't provide them, and they are never returned in API responses.

  • The chat model your agent runs on is set up by Wiro. Pick the model with UserAgent/UpdateSettings; there is no key to supply.

CredentialUpsert rejects writes to these fields with <Field label> is managed by the platform, and Deploy drops them from credentials.

Auditing Credential Changes: CredentialFieldHistory

Every credential field write is appended to a versioned history. Use POST /UserAgent/CredentialFieldHistory to read it, the same idea as CustomSkillHistory for skills.

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/CredentialFieldHistory" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "credentialkey": "telegram"
  }'
Response
{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "entries": [
    {
      "guid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
      "useragentguid": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
      "credentialkey": "telegram",
      "fieldname": "allowedusers",
      "fieldvalue": ["123456789"],
      "fieldstatus": "user",
      "parentfield": null,
      "ordinal": 0,
      "operation": "upsert",
      "changedby": "ada-uuid",
      "changedby_user": {
        "uuid": "ada-uuid",
        "firstname": "Ada",
        "lastname": "Lovelace",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "username": "ada",
        "avatar": "https://cdn.wiro.ai/avatars/ada.webp",
        "avatarinitials": "AL"
      },
      "changedat": 1714694410
    }
  ]
}

changedby_user is the resolved actor object (uuid, firstname, lastname, email, username, avatar, avatarinitials). It is null when changedby is a system value such as "system" or "backfill-*", or when the user record has been deleted.

Parameter Type Required Description
useragentguid string Yes Your UserAgent instance guid
credentialkey string Yes Credential key (e.g. "telegram", "twilio-voice")
startdate number No UTC epoch seconds: return entries on/after this time
enddate number No UTC epoch seconds: return entries on/before this time

Secrets stay out of the history's answers. A saved secret such as a bot token or an auth token comes back as "••••••••", in POST /UserAgent/Detail as in the history. CredentialFieldHistory only shows the audit trail.

Setting Credentials

Use POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert with a flat fields[] array. Each field row carries {credentialkey, fieldname, fieldvalue}. The Wiro project an agent runs models with has its own route, POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind, which takes the project's id.

Bulk upsert pattern

/UserAgent/CredentialUpsert takes an array of field rows in one request. Only the fields you send are written; other credential groups and other fields inside the same group are untouched. The Wiro Dashboard follows this pattern exactly: each credential card sends a single CredentialUpsert call with its group's fields.

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/CredentialUpsert" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "your-useragent-guid",
    "fields": [
      { "credentialkey": "telegram", "fieldname": "bottoken",     "fieldvalue": "123456:ABC-DEF..." },
      { "credentialkey": "telegram", "fieldname": "allowedusers", "fieldvalue": ["123456789"] }
    ]
  }'

Response: { "result": true, "applied": 2, "errors": [] }. applied is the count of fields saved without an error (a field sent with its current value still counts; a secret sent back as the mask isn't counted, see below). All fields are validated before any is written: if one fails validation (for example a reserved fieldname prefixed with _), the whole request is rejected and nothing is saved; result is false and errors lists every invalid field. If a save fails after validation has passed, the other fields are still saved and each failed field is listed in errors with result: false. A starting or running agent restarts to apply the new values when the call changes a saved value.

Field-level write rules

  • fieldstatus is assigned by the server. Any fieldstatus you send is ignored: a field that already exists keeps its stored status, and a new field gets the status its registry schema implies.
  • Wiro-managed fields are rejected. You can't write a field whose status is platform: it fails with <Field label> is managed by the platform (a field with no schema label is named <credentialkey>.<fieldname> instead). As with any invalid field, the whole request is rejected and nothing is saved.
  • Reserved fieldnames are rejected. Any fieldname starting with _ (e.g. _isoptional, _isextra) is a sentinel used by the template itself and cannot be set by API callers.
  • A secret sent back as the mask keeps its saved value. UserAgent/Detail shows a saved secret (a password field) as "••••••••". A row whose fieldvalue is that mask, with or without spaces around it, keeps what is saved: it isn't written, isn't counted in applied and restarts nothing. So a card sent back as Detail showed it changes only the fields you edited. To change a secret, send its new value. The mask with other text beside it is refused, with <Field label> holds "••••••••", which stands for a saved value. Clear it and enter the full value.
  • Whitespace around a value is trimmed. Text, password, email, URL and number values, and each entry of a list of strings, are saved without the spaces, tabs or line breaks around them and are validated after trimming, so a token pasted with a trailing newline is accepted. Spaces inside a value are kept, and multi-line text, selections, booleans, files and nested rows are saved as sent. The same applies to inline Deploy credentials.
  • Credential groups other than the channels must be declared by the agent template. Communication-channel credentials are the exception: every useragent may create the channel groups published in POST /Skills/List → channels[], using CredentialUpsert or inline Deploy credentials.
  • Lists (Telegram groups[], Slack channels[], Discord guilds[], Twilio phonenumbers[]) are sent as JSON arrays. An array fieldvalue (with no parentfield) replaces the whole stored list, so send the complete desired list. Per-row writes (a sub-field sent with parentfield, the list field's key, and ordinal, the array index) change only that entry; indices you don't send are kept. To clear an optional list, send [] as that field's fieldvalue with no parentfield.
  • Use POST /UserAgent/Detail to inspect which fields each credential exposes, and the _connected / optional / extra flags that describe its readiness state.

Prepaid deploy: inline setup supported (with limitations)

If you call POST /UserAgent/Deploy with useprepaid: true, you may pass credentials, customskills, and skills at the top level of the Deploy body. The server saves them on the new agent in the same call (one-shot deploy + initial setup). Connectors aren't part of Deploy: connect them once the agent exists, with ConnectorConnect.

Deploy body credentials rules:

  • Values are validated against each credential's public registry schema.
  • Registry-declared string-array and object-array fields are accepted as native JSON arrays. This includes channel allowlists (allowedusers, Telegram groups, Slack channels, Discord guilds).
  • Fieldnames starting with _ are reserved and ignored.
  • Each field's fieldstatus is assigned by the server, exactly as for CredentialUpsert.
  • Deploy never saves a platform field sent in credentials. In a communication-channel group (Telegram, Slack, Discord), such a field fails Deploy before the agent is created. In any other group, the field is dropped and Deploy continues.
  • A secret sent as the mask, "••••••••", isn't saved: a new agent has no saved value for it to keep. In a communication-channel group (Telegram, Slack, Discord), the mask is refused with <Field label> holds "••••••••", which stands for a saved value. Clear it and enter the full value, and Deploy fails before the agent is created. UserAgent/Detail never returns a saved secret, so to copy one agent's setup to another, send each secret's value.
  • If credentials includes a communication-channel group, all of that channel's required_fields must be present. A missing or invalid activation credential fails Deploy instead of creating a partially configured channel.

Deploy body customskills semantics:

  • Each entry must have a key. Server reads value, interval, enabled and description; _user_created: true marks the row as yours, so it can be renamed or deleted later. The key is stored in its full form, as CustomSkillUpsert stores it: a bare slug with an interval becomes cs-cron-<slug>, one without becomes cs-<slug>, and cron-<slug> becomes cs-cron-<slug>.
  • A scheduled task's interval is checked as in CustomSkillUpsert, and "manual" means no schedule. A schedule the agent can't run fails Deploy before anything is created or charged, with an error that starts with the skill's key, such as cs-cron-daily-report: This schedule can't run. The hour field takes 0 to 23. A schedule has five fields: minute hour day month weekday, for example 0 9 * * 1-5.
  • The request body accepts a single top-level customskills array; server-side values are merged onto any existing preset rows for the same key.
  • Up to 50 entries per Deploy. A longer list is refused before anything is created or charged; add the rest with CustomSkillUpsert once the agent is deployed.

If you skip these keys in Deploy entirely, the instance is created empty and you set credentials and skills later with CredentialUpsert, CredentialProjectBind, CustomSkillUpsert, and SkillsApply.

Setup Required State

Every fresh Deploy starts in Setup Required state (status: 6). While an agent is at status: 6, Start refuses it with Agent setup is not complete. Fill in the agent's required settings before starting.

API deploys must always pass useprepaid: true. The server provisions the prepaid subscription inline and moves the agent to status: 2 (Queued) whatever its credentials hold, and Wiro then starts it, so no Start call is needed. A credential the agent requires may still be incomplete while it runs: UserAgent/Detail reads setuprequired: true until every required credential is set up, and a running agent restarts to pick up each value you save.

Saving a credential doesn't move the agent out of status: 6, whether with CredentialUpsert or CredentialProjectBind. After the last one, call POST /UserAgent/Update once with { "guid": "<useragent-guid>" }: that call moves the agent to status: 0 (Stopped) once every required credential is set up, so Start can launch it. Start doesn't read setuprequired on a stopped (status: 0) or errored (status: 5) agent.

setuprequired in UserAgent/Detail is true while the agent is at status: 6 or any non-optional credential is still incomplete; on UserAgent/MyAgents rows it follows status: 6 alone. A credential counts as complete when at least one field saved on this agent with fieldstatus: "user" has a non-empty value (any one user-writable field filled in makes the credential count as "entered"; there is no deeper per-field validation). A value the agent template holds doesn't count here, though it counts toward the card's _filled and _required_missing.

Security

  • A secret you save is never returned. A bot token or an auth token reads as "••••••••" in UserAgent/Detail, as every saved secret does (see Credential object shape).
  • platform fields are always stripped from responses. credentials.wiro.apikey is user-supplied and appears in the response as saved.
  • fieldstatus is server-assigned. A fieldstatus sent to CredentialUpsert is ignored; the server assigns the status itself. Wiro-managed (platform) fields are rejected with <Field label> is managed by the platform. A request that fails validation saves nothing, and Deploy never saves such a field from its credentials body.
  • Connector values and sign-in tokens are kept apart from credentials, encrypted, and never returned either: see Agent Connectors.

For Third-Party Developers

If you're building a product on top of Wiro agents for your own customers:

  1. Deploy an agent instance per customer via POST /UserAgent/Deploy, with any channel groups in credentials.
  2. Connect the services it works with through Agent Connectors: your customer's own API keys, or the vendor's sign-in with a redirecturl on your own site, so the consent screen names your product.
  3. Set the channels and settings your customer wants with CredentialUpsert, and the Wiro project with CredentialProjectBind.
  4. Verify with POST /UserAgent/Detail (credentials, setuprequired) and POST /UserAgent/ConnectorList (each connector's status).

When the agent proposes a change in a chat, apply it with the same calls and record it on its setup card with SetupCardApply: see Agent Chat Integration.

This section as Markdown: View Download

Agent Chat Integration

Build your own chat for a Wiro agent, setup from chat included: every call, every answer field, and what your interface shows at each step.

Overview

This guide is for products that put a Wiro agent behind their own interface. Your users talk to the agent in your app. Your backend calls the API with your project API key, and your app shows the agent's answers, its setup cards and the connect steps with your own design. Your users never leave your product.

It covers the whole cycle in order: sending messages and showing answers, the setup cards the agent proposes, applying them, connecting connectors, restarts, errors, chats without cards, the agent's live Screen and Take Control in your app, security, three worked examples and a checklist. Every request and answer is shown as JSON, so the guide can also be handed to a coding assistant that builds the integration for you.

What setup from chat is

An agent can help the people who manage it set it up in the chat. Asked to report website traffic every Monday, draw a diagram or search the web, it can propose the change itself: turn on a skill, connect a connector, create or change a scheduled task or a custom skill, or change its time zone.

The agent never changes its own setup and never sees a key. It proposes the change as a setup card. Wiro checks the card against the agent's current setup and stores it on the message that asked for it, where it shows as a setup block in that message's timeline[]. Nothing changes until an agent admin applies the card. Wiro then applies the stored card, checked again against the agent as it is at that moment, and never anything written in the chat.

Your product shows everything

Wiro's answers in a chat sent with a project API key name no site, page or link. When something still has to be connected, the answer says so in a plain sentence and returns the same information as data, the next array, so your product shows its own Connect button. Keys, app keys and tokens go into your own forms and reach Wiro through the API, never through the chat. When a connector signs in, the vendor's consent screen shows your organization or your own app, and the browser comes back to a page on your own site (see Who your customer sees, which also says where the API's own address can still show).

A few fields are for your backend, not for your users: every message row and every card names your API key's owner as the person who sent, asked or applied (see API key), and the tokens and ids are your own references. Show your users your own names and words.

Connector titles name their vendors, such as Google Analytics 4 or WordPress. Two things carry Wiro's name: the agent's Wiro project (the credential wiro, which pays for the models its skills run, such as Video Creator's or a voice channel's) and the wiro connector, which gives the agent Wiro's own tools. That name comes wherever the API names them, in the card listing and in summary too. An agent that runs models can also write their public links in an answer, such as a model's page on wiro.ai or an output file on cdn1.wiro.ai. Your product may show its own label for them, as for any title the API gives.

A connector that signs in connects from its card too: SetupCardApply on its connect card answers the vendor's sign-in address, authorizeUrl, and the browser comes back to your redirecturl through one callback on the API host. A sign-in started with your API key always runs as your product: the consent screen names your organization, or the app of your own whose keys you send, never Wiro's own app. Send your own redirecturl with every sign-in: without one, the browser comes back to Wiro's return page on wiro.ai. The same connectors also connect on your own settings screens with the Agent Connectors calls.

The flow at a glance

Your user types           Your backend                     Wiro
--------------            ------------                     ----
"Report our traffic"  ->  Message/Send ------------------>  agent turn runs
                          WebSocket or Message/Detail <---  timeline: answer + setup blocks
Your app shows the card
User presses Save     ->  SetupCardApply with values ---->  key saved, card applied, agent restarts
  (a key card)
User presses Sign in  ->  SetupCardApply with redirecturl ->  authorizeUrl, the card stays pending
  (a sign-in card)        the browser signs in ---------->  consent, callback, your redirecturl;
                                                            the agent restarts
                          SetupCardApply again ---------->  card applied
User presses Apply    ->  Message/SetupCardApply -------->  change applied, agent restarts
Your app shows "Restarting", then the agent answers again

Before You Start

API key

Every call in this guide is authenticated with a project API key from your Wiro dashboard, sent as the x-api-key header (signature-based projects also send x-nonce and x-signature). See Authentication. Call Wiro from your backend only: never put the key in browser or mobile app code.

Your app may hold two kinds of token, so that the browser follows a chat on the Agent WebSocket itself: a turn's agenttoken and a session's sessiontoken. The socket takes no API key, and each token reads only its own turn or session, so give a person only the tokens of their own chats. Or keep the socket on your backend and relay its events. To show the agent's live Screen, the page also gets a one-time screenToken for each screen it opens (see Screen and Take Control in Your App).

A call made with your API key acts as the key's owner: the person who created the project. Messages you send are stored as that person's messages, and setup cards are applied with that person's rights. So every row your users write carries the owner's account: uuid and the user object (first and last name, email, username, avatar) of each message row, and requestedby and actedby of each card. Never show them as the sender. Keep your own record of who wrote what, for example by sessionkey and messageguid, and show your own names.

Deploy an agent

Deploy one agent per customer of yours with POST /UserAgent/Deploy, with useprepaid: true and a plan in tier. The answer's useragents[0].guid is the agent's id: the useragentguid of every other call. The agent is queued and Wiro starts it: it is ready for messages when POST /UserAgent/Detail reads status: 4. Give each conversation its own sessionkey.

{
  "agentguid": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "title": "Acme Marketing Agent",
  "useprepaid": true,
  "tier": "pro",
  "chatsetup": "all"
}

Allow setup cards in API chats

Where setup cards can be proposed and applied is the agent's chatsetup setting. Wiro reads every request sent with a project API key as an API chat:

chatsetup Cards in your API chat SetupCardApply with your API key
all (the default) Yes Works
webchat No: only the Wiro web chat gets cards. In your product, the same as off. Refused: Setup from chat is off for this agent.
off No Refused: Setup from chat is off for this agent.

So an integration that shows setup cards needs "all". Set it at Deploy with chatsetup, or later with POST /UserAgent/UpdateSettings, and read it back as chatSetup on UserAgent/Detail. A change from or to "off" restarts a starting or running agent once, and a change between "all" and "webchat" restarts nothing. UpdateSettings doesn't say whether it restarted the agent: read UserAgent/Detail after it, as in Showing a restart.

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/UpdateSettings" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "chatsetup": "all"
  }'

{ "result": true, "errors": [] }

With "webchat" or "off", the agent proposes no card in your chat and tells people that an agent admin makes the change in the agent's settings, which in your product are the settings screens you build on the same endpoints.

Who may apply a card

Applying a card needs an agent admin: the agent's owner, or an admin of the agent's team. With your API key, that is the key's owner, so every apply your backend sends counts as that person's approval. Dismissing a card needs only that the caller can see the chat.

Because of this, decide in your own product who may approve a change: show the Apply button, and pass a typed approval on to Wiro, only for the people allowed to change that agent. Wiro reads many words as an approval, not only yes, and a key pasted while a key connect card is the only connect card waiting can be saved to it: Typed replies has the whole list. When people who must not change the agent talk to it through your app, set chatsetup to "off" for that agent and change its setup from your own settings screens instead. That is the safe choice for any agent that several of your users share.

Messages and Answers

Send a message

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/Send" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "message": "Can you report our website traffic every Monday?",
    "sessionkey": "customer-42"
  }'

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messageguid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
  "agenttoken": "aB3xK9mR2pLqWzVn7tYhCd5sFgJkNb",
  "status": "agent_queue"
}

Keep messageguid (the turn) and agenttoken (its live stream). The full parameter list, attachments and per-turn model choice are in Message/Send. result: true means the message was queued: follow the turn to its end, since a turn that couldn't be handed to the agent still ends as agent_error (see When a turn fails).

When the agent isn't running, Send answers result: false with agentstatus and a sentence you can show as it is:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 0, "message": "Agent is restarting. Please wait a moment and try again.", "time": 1794654900 }],
  "messageguid": null,
  "agenttoken": null,
  "status": null,
  "agentstatus": 1
}

See Restarts for the other sentences.

When the agent has used the AI usage its plan includes and the balance is under $0.50, Send answers result: false with code 97, agentstatus and agentusage, the agent's usage:

{
  "result": false,
  "errors": [{ "code": 97, "message": "Support Desk used the $30.00 of AI usage its plan includes this month, and your balance is under $0.50. Add funds to keep it running, or it starts again when the plan renews on 1 December 2026.", "time": 1794654900 }],
  "messageguid": null,
  "agenttoken": null,
  "status": null,
  "agentstatus": 4,
  "agentusage": { "period": "2026-11", "resetsat": 1796083200, "includedusd": 30, "usedusd": 30, "leftusd": 0, "renewalusd": 30, "frombalanceusd": 12.85, "balanceusd": 0.31, "wallet": "personal", "minbalanceusd": 0.5, "paused": true, "pausedreason": "balance" }
}

That sentence speaks to whoever pays for the agent, which is you; it leaves out the date when the plan's renewal can't be read. Detect the refusal by agentusage, show your users your own words, and add funds to the balance of the agent's workspace (see Adding Funds), or move the agent to a larger plan with UpgradeTier. The agent answers again as soon as the balance is back at $0.50 or more. Your users in Telegram, Slack and Discord read This agent is paused for now. It runs again once its owner adds funds or its plan renews. instead, with no amount. Setup replies that Wiro answers itself still work while the agent is paused: see Replies the API answers itself.

Follow the turn

Use one of three ways:

  1. WebSocket (best for a live chat): connect to wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1 and send { "type": "agent_info", "agenttoken": "aB3xK9mR2pLqWzVn7tYhCd5sFgJkNb" }. You get agent_subscribed (a snapshot with status, debugoutput and timeline), then agent_start, one agent_timeline_delta per changed block, agent_output snapshots of the answer text, and agent_end, agent_error or agent_cancel. See Agent WebSocket.
  2. Polling: call POST /UserAgent/Message/Detail with { "messageguid": "..." } every second or two until status is agent_end, agent_error or agent_cancel.
  3. Webhook: send callbackurl with the message, and Wiro posts the final answer to it. See Agent Webhooks.

Setup blocks arrive on the WebSocket like any other block, as agent_timeline_delta:

{
  "type": "agent_timeline_delta",
  "agenttoken": "aB3xK9mR2pLqWzVn7tYhCd5sFgJkNb",
  "message": {
    "messageguid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
    "block": {
      "blockid": "s:k3v9q2m8x1za",
      "type": "setup",
      "callindex": 1000000,
      "contentindex": 0,
      "text": null,
      "setup": {
        "v": 1,
        "id": "k3v9q2m8x1za",
        "kind": "schedule",
        "action": "create",
        "key": "cs-cron-weekly-traffic",
        "title": "Weekly traffic report",
        "cron": "0 9 * * 1",
        "instructions": "Every Monday, report last week's sessions, users and top pages from Google Analytics 4.",
        "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
        "createdat": 1794654811
      },
      "phase": "end",
      "version": 1,
      "startedat": 1794654811,
      "updatedat": 1794654811
    }
  },
  "result": true
}

When someone applies or dismisses the card later, the block comes again on the same agenttoken with version: 2 and the new status, as long as your socket is still subscribed to that token. Message/Detail and Message/History always return the current state, so after a reconnect, read them again.

To stop a reply that is still running, call POST /UserAgent/Message/Cancel with its messageguid, and with its sessionkey when several of your users share the agent, so that one person can't stop another's reply. The turn ends as agent_cancel.

When a turn fails

A turn that fails ends with status: "agent_error", and a cancelled one with "agent_cancel". Its response and debugoutput, and the text of the agent_error or agent_cancel event and of the webhook, hold one code in brackets and a fixed sentence:

Code Status What to show
[SECURITY_BLOCKED] agent_error The agent's security rules blocked the message: ask the person to change it.
[SAFETY_POLICY_BLOCKED] agent_error The model's provider declined the request: ask the person to rephrase it.
[TURN_INTERRUPTED] agent_error A restart cut the turn short: offer to send it again.
[SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED] agent_error The agent's spend limit is used up: show the sentence as it is.
[USAGE_CEILING_REACHED] agent_error The agent reached its hourly or daily safety ceiling for AI model calls: say it runs again when that hour or day is over.
[MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED] agent_error The agent's Model Access rule blocks the model it uses: show the sentence as it is.
[CREDITS_EXHAUSTED] agent_error The agent has used the AI usage its plan includes and the balance is under $0.50: say it runs again once funds are added or its plan renews, and don't offer to try again before that.
[AGENT_UNAVAILABLE] agent_error Anything else, a message that couldn't be queued included: offer to try again shortly.
[REQUEST_CANCELLED] agent_cancel The turn was cancelled.

Match the code and show your own words, or the sentence after it. The full texts are in Failed turns.

Load a conversation

POST /UserAgent/Message/History returns a session's messages, newest first. Each row has the fields of a Message/Detail answer except sessionkey, startedat and endedat, which History doesn't return:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/History" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "sessionkey": "customer-42",
    "limit": 50
  }'

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "data": {
    "messages": [
      {
        "guid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
        "content": "Can you report our website traffic every Monday?",
        "response": "I can do that once Google Analytics 4 is connected. Sign in to it with the card below, then I will set up the weekly report.",
        "status": "agent_end"
      }
    ],
    "count": 1,
    "hasmore": false,
    "sessiontoken": "Lp4vQ8sWn2KxT7cRb1YhZ6mDg9FjA3uEo5iNk0wXyHt"
  }
}

The row is shortened here; a whole one has the fields of a Message/Detail answer. Page back with before (the oldest guid you have) while hasmore is true. A session holds four kinds of row:

Row How you know it What your UI shows
A turn content holds the message as stored (keys taken out, see Security Rules), response the reply, timeline[] its blocks, setup blocks included, in their current state The person's message and the agent's reply. While status is agent_queue, agent_start or agent_output, the reply is in progress: subscribe to its agenttoken to follow it.
A reply Wiro answered itself metadata.type is "setup_result", agenttoken is null, timeline is empty The message and response as plain text. See Replies the API answers itself.
A message added between turns content is empty, the text is in response, metadata.type is "subagent" or "system" The agent's message with no message of the person's above it: a scheduled task's report, files sent after an answer, or, for "subagent", the result of work the agent finished in the background.
A model switch status is "agent_done", metadata.type is "model_change" A thin separator, or nothing. It comes only when you pick a per-turn model.

A message added between turns has no turn of its own: nothing streams on an agenttoken for it and no webhook is called. A scheduled task's report goes to the session the agent's latest message is in, so on an agent that several of your users share it can reach any of their chats. To get it live, follow the session with the sessiontoken above: send { "type": "agent_session_subscribe", "sessiontoken": "Lp4vQ8sWn2KxT7cRb1YhZ6mDg9FjA3uEo5iNk0wXyHt" } on the socket, and each new row arrives as an agent_message_inserted frame. Follows end with the connection, so after a reconnect subscribe again and read History once. See Following a session. The weekly report of the GA4 example below reaches your chat this way.

To list a customer's conversations, call POST /UserAgent/Message/Sessions with the useragentguid: it answers each session's sessionkey, messagecount, updatedat, lastmessage and, once named with RenameSession, name. It lists every session of the agent that your key's owner can read, so on an agent that several of your users share, show each person only the sessions your own records give them.

Render the timeline

A reply is an ordered list of blocks. Keep a map keyed by blockid, keep a block only when its version is newer than the one you hold, and draw the blocks sorted by callindex, then contentindex, then blockid.

type What it holds What your UI shows
reasoning text: a short summary of the agent's thinking A collapsed "Thinking" section, in its place in the list.
answer text: the answer text The agent's message. Render it as Markdown.
tool toollabel, toolstatus (requested, completed, error), toolintegration, toolaction A small status line, such as "Working in Shopify" or "Taking a screenshot". Use your own labels for the toolintegration and toolaction words, and toollabel when both are null.
setup setup: a setup card; on a pending connect card, also next A card with buttons. See Setup Cards.

Setup blocks have callindex: 1000000, so they sort after the reply's other blocks, in the order the agent proposed them, at most three per message. Skip a block whose type you don't know. The block fields are listed in Public timeline block fields.

Wiro cleans the agent's text before it reaches you, in the blocks, in response and in every event: a link to a private address or into the agent's own system reads [link removed], and a path inside the agent's system reads [private detail removed]. A turn in which the agent wrote nothing, older ones included, can read No response from agent. Show these as they are, or your own words. Public links stay as written, the Wiro model links of Your product shows everything included.

Replies the API answers itself

Some messages are answered by Wiro itself, with no agent turn: a yes that applies a card or gets the card listing, a yes while a sign-in or project connect card waits, a key typed as the reply while the latest reply has one pending connect card and it is a key card with one secret field, and the others listed in Chats Without Cards. Message/Send then answers at once with status: "agent_end", agenttoken: null, the answer in response and the outcome in setupresult:

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messageguid": "d4e5f6a7-b8c9-0123-def4-567890123456",
  "agenttoken": null,
  "status": "agent_end",
  "response": "✅ Applied: Scheduled task Weekly traffic report created.\nYour agent is restarting to load the change. Continue in about a minute.",
  "content": "yes",
  "setupresult": {
    "applied": ["k3v9q2m8x1za"],
    "dismissed": [],
    "failed": [],
    "restarting": true
  }
}

Show response as the reply, as plain text. There is nothing to follow on the WebSocket. In Message/History the row reads status: "agent_end", metadata: { "type": "setup_result" } and an empty timeline. When the answer leaves connectors to connect, metadata also keeps its next, and a card listing keeps listed and listedfrom there: see Replies Wiro handles itself. These replies cost nothing, and Wiro gives them while the agent is stopped or restarting too: see Messages during a restart for which ones.

Wiro also answers a slash command the agent doesn't run, such as /status, or one of its commands that is turned off, while the agent is running. It costs nothing, even while the agent is paused for its balance, and the answer has no setupresult:

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "messageguid": "e5f6a7b8-c9d0-1234-ef56-789012345678",
  "agenttoken": null,
  "status": "agent_end",
  "response": "⛔ Unknown or disabled command: /status\nSend /agent_help to see the available commands.",
  "content": "/status"
}

The second line comes only when the agent has agent_help on. Show response as the reply, and the row in History as you show the other replies Wiro answers itself. A command counts anywhere in the message, as in Check the /pricing page, but never inside a link or a quoted line. A message that holds one of the agent's enabled commands, written in lower case and followed by a space, a line break or the end of the message, goes to the agent, which runs it, and so does a message whose first command is /model, /models or one of a few common words and paths, such as /start, /help or /usr/bin/env. While the agent isn't running, the message gets the refusal in Messages during a restart. The full rules are in Unknown or disabled commands.

Setup Cards

Block fields

A setup block has the usual block fields, type: "setup", text: null and a setup object, the card:

{
  "blockid": "s:h6w3k9p2m5tc",
  "type": "setup",
  "callindex": 1000000,
  "contentindex": 1,
  "text": null,
  "setup": {
    "v": 1,
    "id": "h6w3k9p2m5tc",
    "kind": "connect",
    "connector": "serper",
    "title": "Serper",
    "authtype": "fields",
    "mode": "key",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "apikey",
        "label": "Serper API Key",
        "description": "1. Sign up at [serper.dev](https://serper.dev). No credit card; new accounts get **2,500 free searches**.\n2. Open the dashboard and copy your **API key** from the **API Key** section.\n3. Paste it here.",
        "required": true,
        "secret": true,
        "format": "password",
        "placeholder": "your Serper.dev API key"
      }
    ],
    "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
    "createdat": 1794654811
  },
  "phase": "end",
  "version": 1,
  "startedat": 1794654811,
  "updatedat": 1794654811,
  "next": [{ "connector": "serper", "title": "Serper", "mode": "key" }]
}
Field Description
blockid s: and the card's id. Use it as the merge key.
type setup.
callindex 1000000 for every setup block, so it sorts after the reply's other blocks.
contentindex The card's place on the message: 0, 1 or 2. Add 1 for the card number a card listing uses.
text Always null.
setup The card. See Card fields.
phase Always end.
version 1 while the card is pending, 2 once it is applied, dismissed or failed. Keep the copy with the higher version.
startedat When the agent proposed the card (Unix seconds).
updatedat When the card last changed.
next Only on a pending connect card: how its own connector connects, as one entry { connector, title, mode } with the card's own title and mode. It is gone once the card is applied, dismissed or failed. See Your Own Connect Button. An add card's block has no next: its setup.needs lists what it needs. A card stored before cards carried mode can have no next: its connector signs in when its authtype on AgentConnector/Detail is oauth or provider-oauth, and takes a key otherwise.

Card fields

Field Kinds Description
v all Card format version, 1.
id all The card's id: 12 lower-case letters and digits. Send it as cardid to SetupCardApply.
kind all add, remove, connect, disconnect, schedule, skill or timezone. Skip a card whose kind you don't know.
action schedule, skill schedule: create, update, pause, resume or delete. skill: create, update, append (add text to the end), revert (undo the last change), disable or enable.
key add, remove, schedule, skill add and remove: the skill (util-<name>) as POST /Skills/List names it. schedule: the task's key (cs-cron-<name>). skill: the custom skill's key (cs-<name>).
connector connect, disconnect The connector's slug as POST /AgentConnector/List lists it, such as serper or hubspot. A card names only connectors of the catalog: never a channel or a credential, and never a key's value.
title connect, disconnect, schedule, skill connect and disconnect: the connector's title, written by Wiro, up to 120 characters. schedule and skill: optional, one line, up to 80 characters.
authtype connect Written by Wiro: the connector's authtype in the catalog, fields, headers, none, oauth or provider-oauth.
mode connect Written by Wiro: how the card connects, key (the values its fields ask for), signin (the vendor's sign-in) or project (a Wiro project for the wiro connector). See Modes.
fields connect Written by Wiro: what the card's form asks for, at most 30, in the shape of credentialfields on AgentConnector/Detail: name, label, description (Markdown), required, secret, format, and options, placeholder, pattern, maxlength, serveronly, mode or source where they apply. On a key card, the connector's Connect fields. On a project card, one field with source: "wiro_project": a project picker, never an input. On a signin card, the fields its sign-in takes: for a connector that signs in with an app of your own, that app's keys (serveronly: true). The fields of a connector's key way are never on a signin card. Empty when there is nothing to enter.
wiroapp connect Written by Wiro, only on a card from a Wiro web chat turn: true when its connector signs in there with Wiro's own app. Never on a card from a chat sent with your API key, whose sign-in always takes your own app's keys.
cron schedule Five fields, in the agent's time zone. Always on create, optional on update. A task set up from chat runs at most once an hour.
instructions schedule, skill create and update: the full text. append: only the text to add. revert: the text it restores. Up to 20,000 characters on what the agent writes.
before skill (update, append, revert) The skill's text when Wiro checked the card. Show it next to the text after the change: for append, that is before without the spaces and line breaks at its end, a blank line, then instructions. Can be absent on older cards.
with add, remove Other skills turned on (add) or off (remove) together with key, by name, sorted, at most 12. Written by Wiro. An add names only the ones still off on this agent, so the same key can bring a different list, or none, on another agent.
pauses, resumes add, remove Scheduled tasks (cs-cron-<name>) that stop, or run again, with this change, at most 20 each. Written by Wiro. Name each by the description of its entry in scheduledskills of UserAgent/Detail, or by its key in words.
needs add What the change needs that isn't connected yet, at most 3, each { connector, title, mode }. title can be absent: then use the connector's key. Written by Wiro. See Modes.
timezone timezone The proposed IANA time zone, such as Europe/Istanbul.
note all Optional. The agent's one-line note on the change, up to 300 characters.
status all Absent while pending, then applied, dismissed or failed.
actedat, actedby all When the card was acted on (Unix seconds) and the account UUID of who did it. Absent while pending. With your API key, actedby is your key's owner.
error all Only when status is failed: one plain sentence that says why.
requestedby all The account UUID of the person whose message asked for the change: in your chats, your key's owner.
createdat all When the agent proposed the card (Unix seconds).

A connect card carries everything its form needs, so you can draw it without another call. Fields that don't apply to a card's kind are absent, and a missing list reads as empty. More kinds, actions and fields can be added later.

Every kind

add turns on a skill. This one turns on Video Creator and the skills that come with it:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "m5t8c2w6r3pe",
  "kind": "add",
  "key": "util-video-creator",
  "with": ["util-motion-effects", "util-video-docs", "util-video-shots"],
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

When needs names connectors, Wiro stores a connect card for each of them on the same message, right after the add card, whatever its mode, while the message has room for it (three cards at most) and has no pending connect card for it yet. Show them together: see Buttons.

remove turns one off:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "w2c8n5q1x7rd",
  "kind": "remove",
  "key": "util-weather",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

connect connects a connector of the catalog that the agent doesn't have connected yet, by its slug. Wiro writes the connector's title, its authtype, the card's mode and the form's fields on it:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "h6w3k9p2m5tc",
  "kind": "connect",
  "connector": "serper",
  "title": "Serper",
  "authtype": "fields",
  "mode": "key",
  "fields": [
    { "name": "apikey", "label": "Serper API Key", "description": "1. Sign up at [serper.dev](https://serper.dev) ...", "required": true, "secret": true, "format": "password", "placeholder": "your Serper.dev API key" }
  ],
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

A connector that signs in gets a signin card: see Sign-in: HubSpot. The wiro connector gets a project card: see Project: Wiro AI Models.

disconnect disconnects a connector the agent has a connection for, and carries its title:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "b7k1m4t9w2zs",
  "kind": "disconnect",
  "connector": "serper",
  "title": "Serper",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

schedule creates or changes a scheduled task:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "k3v9q2m8x1za",
  "kind": "schedule",
  "action": "create",
  "key": "cs-cron-weekly-traffic",
  "title": "Weekly traffic report",
  "cron": "0 9 * * 1",
  "instructions": "Every Monday, report last week's sessions, users and top pages from Google Analytics 4.",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

skill creates or changes a custom skill. An append card carries only the text it adds, and before:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "p7d2m4x9q1ka",
  "kind": "skill",
  "action": "append",
  "key": "cs-blog-writing",
  "instructions": "End every post with three questions readers ask, each with a two-sentence answer.",
  "before": "Write each blog post in a friendly, plain tone.\nKeep posts under 900 words.",
  "note": "Adds the reader questions you asked for.",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

timezone changes the agent's time zone:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "z4x8c1v6b3nm",
  "kind": "timezone",
  "timezone": "Europe/Istanbul",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811
}

A card once acted on carries status, actedat and actedby, and a failed one error. This append card failed because someone edited the skill after the card was made:

{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "p7d2m4x9q1ka",
  "kind": "skill",
  "action": "append",
  "key": "cs-blog-writing",
  "instructions": "End every post with three questions readers ask, each with a two-sentence answer.",
  "before": "Write each blog post in a friendly, plain tone.\nKeep posts under 900 words.",
  "note": "Adds the reader questions you asked for.",
  "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "createdat": 1794654811,
  "status": "failed",
  "actedat": 1794654870,
  "actedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "error": "This skill changed after the card was made. Ask the agent again."
}

The full rules of each kind, such as what with, pauses and before mean, are in Setup From Chat.

Card states

State How you know What it means
Pending No status (block version 1) Waiting for someone to apply or dismiss it.
Applied status: "applied" The change is made. The answer that applied it says in restarting whether the agent restarts.
Dismissed status: "dismissed" Turned down. Nothing changed.
Failed status: "failed" Wiro tried to apply it and couldn't: error says why. Nothing changed.

Two more states exist only in your interface, between a click and the answer: applying (your call is under way), and refused, when SetupCardApply answers result: false and the card is still pending, for example a key the vendor refused or an add card whose sign-in hasn't finished. A refused card keeps its buttons. A signin card has one more: signing in, from the answer that gives authorizeUrl until the browser is back on your page. While the agent restarts after a change, show the card as applied with a restarting note; see Restarts.

Whenever a card is applied, dismissed or fails, Wiro also marks applied the same person's pending connect cards in that chat from the last 7 days whose connectors now read connected: the one this card connected, and any whose sign-in finished or that were connected on a settings screen. Their blocks come again on their own agenttokens, and History shows them applied.

What your UI shows for each kind

Kind Title line Body Buttons
add "Add <title>", the title of key in Skills/List with as "Also turns on", pauses and resumes, and each entry of needs with its connect card Apply, Dismiss, and the buttons of its connect cards; see Buttons
remove "Remove <title>" with as "Also turns off", pauses and resumes Apply, Dismiss
connect "Connect <title>" By mode: for key, a form from fields; for signin, the serveronly fields when the card has them, such as your own app's keys; for project, a picker of your projects Save for key (Connect when no field is required), Sign in for signin, Connect for project, and Dismiss
disconnect "Disconnect <title>" Say that the connection is removed and the agent loses the connector's tools until it is connected again Disconnect, Dismiss
schedule "Create", "Change", "Pause", "Resume" or "Delete" scheduled task <title or key> The schedule in words, in the agent's time zone, and instructions Apply, Dismiss
skill "Create", "Change", "Add to", "Undo the last change to", "Turn off" or "Turn on" custom skill <title or key> instructions; for update, append and revert, before next to the text after the change Apply, Dismiss
timezone "Set the time zone to <timezone>" The current zone, timezone on UserAgent/Detail (null means UTC) Apply, Dismiss

Show note, when there is one, under the title.

What your UI shows for each state

State Show Buttons
Pending, reply still being written The card Apply disabled while the message's status is agent_queue, agent_start or agent_output; Dismiss works
Pending The card All enabled
Applying The card with a spinner Disabled
Signing in (signin cards) "Waiting for the sign-in" until the browser is back on your page Sign in again (a new sign-in), Dismiss
Refused errors[0].message under the card Enabled
Applied "Applied", and summary from the answer when you have it None
Applied, agent restarting "Applied" and "Restarting, about a minute" until the agent runs again None
Dismissed "Turned down" None
Failed "Not applied" and setup.error None

Buttons

  • Apply: SetupCardApply with action: "apply".
  • Dismiss: SetupCardApply with action: "dismiss". A connect card connects its connector on its own, so dismissing an add card leaves its connect cards pending: dismiss them too when the person turns the whole change down.
  • A key card: show its fields and Save: SetupCardApply with the values in values. A card whose fields hold no required field connects with Connect and no values.
  • A signin card: show its serveronly fields when it has them, and Sign in: SetupCardApply with those keys in values and your redirecturl. Open the answer's authorizeUrl. Once the browser is back on your redirecturl with connector_connected=true, call SetupCardApply on the card again, with no values: it records the card applied. See Sign-in: HubSpot.
  • A project card: show a picker of your projects and Connect: SetupCardApply with the chosen project's id as wiroprojectguid, and no values. See Project: Wiro AI Models.
  • An add card with its connect cards: the connect cards on the same message whose connector is in the add card's needs belong to it. Show them inside the add card.
  • Add and connect, with a key: when the add card has one key card, show its fields and Add and connect: SetupCardApply on the add card with the values in values. Both cards apply in one step, with one restart.
  • Add and connect, with a sign-in: when the add card has one signin card, run Sign in on that connect card first, as above. Once the browser is back, Add: SetupCardApply on the add card with signin: true applies both cards, once the connector reads connected.
  • Add, then pick a project: a project card takes its own step. Offer Add on the add card, and Connect on the project card, in either order.
  • Several connect cards: offer Add alone, then each connect card's own button.
  • Add now, connect later: SetupCardApply on the add card alone, whose answer's next names the connect cards to finish later.

Applying and Dismissing

Request

POST /UserAgent/Message/SetupCardApply acts on one card:

Parameter Type Required Description
useragentguid string Yes The agent.
messageguid string Yes The message that holds the card: the row whose timeline[] has the setup block.
cardid string Yes The card's setup.id.
action string Yes "apply" or "dismiss".
values object No { "<name>": value } for the card's fields. On a key card: the connector's Connect fields. On a signin card: the fields its sign-in takes, such as your own app's keys. A project card takes none: send wiroprojectguid. Wiro checks them as ConnectorConnect does: required fields, format, pattern and maxlength (see Connect card fields for the limits), and a json field also takes an object. A field left out keeps a value saved before. On an add card whose needs has one pending key card: that card's values, and Wiro applies both cards in one step. Never returned and never shown to the agent.
signin boolean No true on an add card whose needs has one pending signin card, once that card's sign-in has connected the connector: Wiro applies both cards in one step. Not together with values.
redirecturl string No A signin card: where the browser comes back after the sign-in, with the rules of The redirect URL. Send a page on your own site: without one, the browser comes back to Wiro's return page on wiro.ai.
wiroprojectguid string No A project card, the wiro connector's: the id of one of your projects, from POST /Project/List. It becomes the agent's own Wiro project, as CredentialProjectBind binds it. Left out, a call made with your project API key binds that key's own project. 
curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/SetupCardApply" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "messageguid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
    "cardid": "k3v9q2m8x1za",
    "action": "apply"
  }'

Answer

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "setup": {
    "v": 1,
    "id": "k3v9q2m8x1za",
    "kind": "schedule",
    "action": "create",
    "key": "cs-cron-weekly-traffic",
    "title": "Weekly traffic report",
    "cron": "0 9 * * 1",
    "instructions": "Every Monday, report last week's sessions, users and top pages from Google Analytics 4.",
    "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
    "createdat": 1794654811,
    "status": "applied",
    "actedat": 1794654870,
    "actedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f"
  },
  "restarting": true,
  "summary": "Scheduled task Weekly traffic report created"
}
Field Description
result true when the action went through. false when it was refused or failed: read errors[0].message, and setup.status when setup isn't null.
errors [{ code, message, time }]. message is one plain sentence you can show as it is.
setup The card after the call: still pending after a refusal, applied, dismissed or failed otherwise. null when the call was refused before the card was read: a missing parameter, an agent or message your key can't reach, setup from chat off, a reply still running, code 97, a card someone is applying at that moment, or a card that isn't there.
restarting true when the agent restarts to load the change. See Restarts.
summary A short phrase that says what changed, such as Scheduled task Weekly traffic report created, Serper connected or, for an add card applied with its connect card, Google Play Promotional Content added. Google Play Console connected. An applied add card whose connectors have no connect card to finish them goes on with Still to connect: <titles>. Empty when nothing was applied.
authorizeUrl Only when a signin card's sign-in started: the vendor's sign-in address, to open in the browser. It works for 10 minutes and once. result is true, the card in setup is still pending, summary is empty, and next names the card. See Sign-in: HubSpot.
paired Only when values or signin: true came with an add card: its connect card after the call, [{ setup, result, error }]. result is true when that card was applied too, and error is null or the sentence that says why not. [] when the add card has no single connect card for them.
errorcode Only on some refusals of an add card sent with signin: true: not_connected (the connector doesn't read connected yet), signin_no_pair (no pending signin card on the message for it) or signin_many (more than one).
next Only when something is left to connect: [{ connector, title, mode, cardid?, messageguid? }]. An applied add card lists the connectors it needs that still aren't connected, and a connect card left pending (a refused key or project, or a sign-in just started) lists its own connector and card. See Your Own Connect Button.

Dismissing answers the card with status: "dismissed", restarting: false and an empty summary.

Everyone subscribed to the turn's agenttoken gets the card's new block as an agent_timeline_delta, and so does a connect card applied with an add card. Update your copy from the answer's setup right away, and from the block when it arrives.

Who may call it

With your project API key, a call acts as the key's owner, and works when all of these hold:

  • The agent's chatsetup is "all". Otherwise: Setup from chat is off for this agent.
  • The key's owner owns the agent or is a member of its team, and the key's project is in the agent's workspace: a team project's key for a team agent, a personal one for a personal agent. Otherwise: Agent not found or access denied, or a sentence that names the workspace to use.
  • The message is one the key's owner can read with Message/History: not deleted, not hidden, and in a private chat their own. Otherwise: This setup card was not found.
  • To apply: the reply that holds the card has finished (otherwise Wait until the agent finishes this reply, then apply it.), and the key's owner is an agent admin (otherwise code 97, Only an agent admin can apply setup changes.). Dismissing works at any time for anyone who can see the chat.
  • The card is pending. A card is applied at most once: on one that was acted on, the answer says This card was already applied., This card was already dismissed. or This card was already failed., with the card in setup.

SetupCardApply takes no sessionkey. When several of your users share one agent, check in your backend that the messageguid belongs to the session of the person who clicked, for example with Message/Detail and its sessionkey.

Connecting a Connector

A connect card connects its connector through SetupCardApply, with the checks and the outcome of ConnectorConnect: the connection is saved, the agent restarts with the connector's tools, and the agent never sees a key or a token. The card carries what its form needs (title, mode and fields), so you can draw it without another call.

Modes

mode How it connects Your UI Calls
key The values the vendor issues, such as an API key, typed by the person. A card with no required field connects with none. A form from setup.fields, with masked inputs for secret fields SetupCardApply with values: the connector connects and the card is applied
signin The vendor's consent screen, in the browser The serveronly fields when the card has them (your own app's keys), and a Sign in button SetupCardApply with your redirecturl, and the app's keys in values, answers authorizeUrl. Once the browser is back on your page, SetupCardApply again records the card applied
project One of your Wiro projects, picked for the wiro connector. It becomes the agent's own Wiro project. A picker of your projects (POST /Project/List) for its one source: "wiro_project" field, and a Connect button SetupCardApply with the project's id as wiroprojectguid and no values: the project is bound, the connector connects and the card is applied

A card's mode follows its connector in the catalog: oauth and provider-oauth connectors sign in, the wiro connector, whose one field is a Wiro project, gets a project card, and the other fields, headers and none connectors take a key. More modes can be added: show a card whose mode you don't know with Dismiss only, and connect its connector from your settings screen.

Key: Serper

A key connector takes its fields as values on its connect card. Serper has one field, apikey (label "Serper API Key"). Wiro connects it as ConnectorConnect does, with the same checks, and the agent never sees the key:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/SetupCardApply" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "useragentguid": "f8e7d6c5-b4a3-2190-fedc-ba0987654321",
    "messageguid": "c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-345678901234",
    "cardid": "h6w3k9p2m5tc",
    "action": "apply",
    "values": { "apikey": "THE_SERPER_API_KEY" }
  }'

{
  "result": true,
  "errors": [],
  "setup": {
    "v": 1,
    "id": "h6w3k9p2m5tc",
    "kind": "connect",
    "connector": "serper",
    "title": "Serper",
    "authtype": "fields",
    "mode": "key",
    "fields": [
      { "name": "apikey", "label": "Serper API Key", "description": "1. Sign up at [serper.dev](https://serper.dev) ...", "required": true, "secret": true, "format": "password", "placeholder": "your Serper.dev API key" }
    ],
    "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
    "createdat": 1794654811,

  },

}

A value Wiro refuses (a required field missing, a format that doesn't fit, or a key the vendor refused) saves nothing: the answer is result: false with the sentence, and the card stays pending for the person to try again.

Project: Wiro AI Models

The wiro connector gets a project card. Its one field has source: "wiro_project": show a picker of your projects (POST /Project/List) instead of an input, and never a box to type a key in:

Its block's next reads [{ "connector": "wiro", "title": "Wiro AI Models", "mode": "project" }]. Connect sends the chosen project's id as wiroprojectguid, with no values:

  • The project becomes the agent's own Wiro project, as CredentialProjectBind binds it and with the same checks, and the connector's tools act with it as the agent's own calls: see The Wiro connector. A project Wiro refuses saves nothing, and the card stays pending with the sentence, such as This is a team agent: use one of its team's projects.
  • Left out, a call made with your project API key binds that key's own project. When the card can't connect without a project, it stays pending with Pick a project on the card to connect Wiro AI Models., and next names it.
  • A project card never connects from a typed reply and never takes a pasted key. In a chat sent with your API key, a yes while only connect cards wait, this one among them, is answered A yes cannot connect Wiro AI Models. Its project is picked outside this chat.: nothing is applied and no agent turn starts.

Sign-in: HubSpot

A connector that signs in gets a signin card. HubSpot signs in with an app of your own, so its card's fields are that app's client id and secret, and the help text names the redirect URI to register in the app:

1. Start the sign-in. Your app shows the two fields and a Sign in button. Your backend sends the app's keys and a page on your own site to come back to:

curl -X POST "https://api.wiro.ai/v1/UserAgent/Message/SetupCardApply" \

  }'

The answer gives the vendor's sign-in address. The card stays pending, and next names it:

2. Open authorizeUrl in the person's browser, in a popup or the same window. HubSpot's consent screen shows the app whose keys you sent. The address works for 10 minutes and once: a new Sign in gets a fresh one.

3. The browser comes back. HubSpot sends the browser to the API's callback, which stores the tokens, marks the connection connected, restarts the agent and sends the browser on to your redirecturl with connector_connected=true, or with connector_error=<code> when the sign-in didn't finish (see The callback and your redirect URL).

4. Record the card. Call SetupCardApply on the card again, with no values:

      { "name": "clientsecret", "label": "Client Secret", "description": "", "required": true, "secret": true, "format": "password", "serveronly": true, "mode": "oauth" }
    ],
    "requestedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f",
    "createdat": 1794655200,
    "status": "applied",
    "actedat": 1794655390,
    "actedby": "5f0c9a2e-1b7d-4c3a-9e8f-2a6b7c8d9e0f"
  },

  "summary": "HubSpot connected"
}

The agent already restarted when the sign-in came back, so restarting is false. Without this call, the card is recorded applied the next time a card of the same person's is applied or dismissed in that chat; until then it still shows its Sign in.

  • A card from a chat sent with your API key never carries wiroapp: true: its sign-in always uses your own app, and HubSpot's consent screen shows that app. Send the app's keys with the first sign-in; a later sign-in of the same connection may leave them out and use the saved ones. Without them, the answer is Client ID is required. Client Secret is required. and the card stays pending.
  • An oauth connector, a vendor's own MCP server with its own sign-in such as TikTok Ads, has no fields on its card: send redirecturl only. Its consent screen names your organization.
  • A connector with account pickers, such as Facebook Pages, lists its candidates once it is connected. Let the person choose them on your settings screen with ConnectorAccounts and ConnectorSetAccounts: no card picks accounts.

Connecting on your settings screen

Every connector also connects without a card, on your own settings screens, with the Agent Connectors calls: fields, a key instead of a sign-in, or the vendor's sign-in with a redirecturl on your own site, then its account pickers. Each answers restart (or connector_connected=true on your page after a sign-in): see Showing a restart.
